The existing `rate_limit_saturated` reason code was renamed to `rate_limit_exhausted` — a response-contract label change flagged for operator tooling; it is a live label, not persisted data, so nothing is orphaned by the rename. **#369 interaction (dispatch-vs-claim suppression):** for an activity that carries a circuit breaker, rate limiting is enforced at dispatch rather than at claim, so `queue::claim_task` skips the rate-limit gate (and token debit) for CB activities; the explainer therefore suppresses `rate_limit_exhausted` for a CB activity and surfaces the breaker phase (`circuit_open`/`circuit_half_open`) instead — never a stale rate-limit reason. **Lazy Open→HalfOpen read caveat:** `CircuitBreakerRegistry::list()` reads (and prunes each breaker's rolling failure window on) phase without transitioning it — the Open→HalfOpen transition is driven exclusively inside `on_dispatch` — so a cooled-down breaker reads `circuit_open` here through the cooldown until a probe dispatch is admitted, and `circuit_half_open` is only observable after that probe; the endpoint is strictly read-only (`list()`/`snapshot` only, never `on_dispatch`/`on_result`/`force_*`). **Documented boundary (from adversarial review):** a CB activity whose breaker is CLOSED but whose rate-limit bucket is exhausted surfaces NO claim-time impediment through this explainer — its stall is dispatch-side (visible via `GET /admin/circuits/{activity_name}` + the token bucket), a pre-existing #369 consequence deliberately out of scope for #611's open/half-open focus. AC2 (concurrency-only labeling) and AC5 (multi-reason accumulation) were already shipped; the genuinely new work is the circuit codes (AC3/AC4), the rename (AC1), docs (AC6), and tests (AC7). **Implementation:** a pure, no-DB, unit-tested `task_intrinsic_impediment_reasons` helper in `api.rs` computes the task-intrinsic impediments (per-key concurrency saturation, rate-limit exhaustion, and circuit-breaker phase) that block every worker equally; a `cb_phase` map is built once per shard-eval via `circuit_breakers().list(Instant::now())` and passed in. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new route, no replay/determinism impact, no shard-semantics change, no core-crate behavior change** — plugin-only, read-only labeling. Files: `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/eligibility_tests.rs`, `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md`, `docs/api-contract.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Tests: 9 pure unit tests in `api.rs` (`eligibility_reason_tests`, covering AC1–AC5, the #369 suppression, and the documented closed-breaker-CB-activity boundary that reports nothing); integration tests in `eligibility_tests.rs` (open-circuit → `circuit_open` with worker-absent / `no_eligible_workers` assertions and end-to-end #369 suppression via a shared-key non-CB sibling task; concurrency-only exact; rate-limit-exhausted exact). The eligibility integration tests are testcontainers-based and were NOT previously wired into CI at all — this slice adds both a `--no-run` compile step and a Docker-backed Linux execution step; the DB-backed tests are compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker) and executed by CI, matching the repo's #543/#544/#601 precedent.
- **Per-execution stall diagnosis** (implemented) — see issue #809. **Before:** `StallReason` (#486) gave a coarse fleet-discovery bucket and `/stack` listed raw pending items, but neither answered *"is this a healthy wait or a pathological stall, and what is the actionable root cause?"*. The `pending_activity` bucket hid "running normally", "in retry backoff", "**no live worker polls this queue**", "**circuit breaker open**" and "**rate-limited / concurrency-deferred**" behind one label, so an operator correlated ≥4 endpoints by hand. **After:** one admin-gated, read-only call — `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/diagnose` — returns a one-word triage `health` (`healthy` | `stalled` | `blocked_external` | `terminal`), a discriminated `blocked_on` object, and `last_event_age_seconds`. **Pure core classifier:** new `autumn-harvest/src/stall_diagnosis.rs` owns `BlockedOn` (internally tagged on `type`, snake_case, closed over 21 variants: `healthy_in_progress`, `awaiting_signal`, `sleeping_timer`, `timer_overdue`, `pending_child`, `activity_retrying`, `activity_deferred`, `activity_no_worker`, `activity_circuit_open`, `activity_rate_limited`, `activity_rate_limit_bucket_missing`, `activity_concurrency_deferred`, `activity_queue_paused`, `activity_paused`, `awaiting_external_handoff`, `paused`, `non_determinism_blocked`, `awaiting_replay_wait`, `workflow_no_worker`, `workflow_queue_paused`, `no_pending_work`), `ExecutionHealth`, the `*Facts` input structs, `classify_pending_activity`, `activity_precedence`, `classify_execution`, `classify_workflow_task` and `summarize` — all pure, no I/O, no DB, 81 inline unit tests. The three output-only enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` (nothing outside the crate constructs them), so adding a variant is a non-breaking wire addition for Rust consumers too; the `*Facts` input structs deliberately are NOT, because the plugin builds `PendingActivityFacts { .. }` as a cross-crate struct literal. `activity_queue_paused` is beyond the AC's literal list (permitted by its "at least" wording) and **correctness-required**: a paused queue with live workers and no other impediment would otherwise report `healthy_in_progress`, which is flat wrong. **Precedence ladder** (fixed, strictly ordered, unit-pinned): `queue_paused > activity_paused > no_worker > rate_limit_bucket_missing > circuit_open > concurrency_deferred > rate_limited > retrying > deferred > healthy`. Every pending activity is classified and the **worst** wins, so one wedged slot in a wide fan-out is never masked by healthy siblings; `no_worker` deliberately outranks `retrying` because a task backing off on a pollerless queue will never run, so reporting "retrying" would promise an impossible retry. Category ladder above that: terminal → paused → activities → external handoffs → children → awaited signals → timers → `no_pending_work`. **Health is derived from the verdict class alone and never from event age**, so a long durable sleep reports `healthy` no matter how old its last event is (AC4). **Correlation, shard-local:** the plugin handler gathers the pending stack, per-queue worker liveness (reusing the canonical #774 `worker_covers_queue` + `fetch_potentially_live_workers`, promoted to `pub(crate)`, so it cannot drift from `/admin/queue-coverage` — the exact drift class that bit `shard_health` in #1150), the in-process circuit registry (#369, via `list()` **only** — never `on_dispatch`/`on_result`/`force_*` — so diagnosing can never advance a breaker's phase), rate-limit bucket and per-key concurrency saturation (SQL shaped exactly like `claim_task`'s own gates; a CB-tracked activity's bucket is deliberately skipped, matching #369's dispatch-time enforcement), the operator queue-pause table (#619, propagated on error rather than defaulting to "nothing is held"), and the task row's own `attempt`/`error`/`scheduled_at`. Shard resolution uses the execution row's **own** `shard_id` column, not `exec_id.shard()` — a pre-sharding (or `ExecutionId::new()`) id carries the `ShardId::UNENCODED` sentinel (`0xFFFF`), which would match no worker's `shard_assignments` and report a **false** `activity_no_worker` for a perfectly covered queue (a genuine bug caught by the integration suite). **Replay consulted only when it can change the answer:** an awaited-but-unsent signal exists solely as a parked command inside the coroutine, so observing one requires the #615 replay drive — which is comparatively expensive and ranks *below* activities/handoffs/children. The drive therefore runs **only** when the database-observable categories would otherwise resolve to `sleeping_timer` or `no_pending_work` (the two verdicts an awaited signal outranks); `wait_set` reports `replayed` / `history_only` (with `wait_set_reason`) / `not_consulted`. The verdict is identical either way, and the common triage path — a wedged pending activity — never pays for a replay, protecting the p95 < 500 ms metric. A replay failure **degrades** (`wait_set_unavailable`), never fails the request. **Multi-reason completeness alongside the single verdict:** `contributing_reason_codes` is the UNION of every claim-time impediment across ALL of the execution's activity rows — not just the row `blocked_on` names — so a lower-ranked cause is never hidden behind a higher-ranked sibling in a fan-out (that union is what makes the success metric's "surfaced 100% of the time it holds" literally true). Sourced verbatim from the eligibility explainer's own pure `task_intrinsic_impediment_reasons` (#611) so the two surfaces can never drift in how a cause is named. **Payload-free apart from the task row's own error text** (names, ids, timestamps and queue/bucket keys otherwise); that one error string IS routed through read-path payload decoding (#608) exactly as `/stack` routes the same column for its own `last_failure`, with the usual best-effort `payload.decode_read` audit row — otherwise an admin would read plaintext there and a ciphertext envelope here for the same column of the same row. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no task-queue mutation, no cross-shard fan-out — safe to call repeatedly.** Terminal executions return `health = terminal` with `terminal_outcome` and **no** `blocked_on`; unknown id → `404`, malformed id → `400`, missing admin → `401`. Registered `RouteClass::ReadOnly` in all three `audit.rs` lists (with a pinned `diagnose_route_is_classified_read_only` test), in `management_api_routes()`/`management_api_response_fields()`, and in `docs/api-contract.json`. CLI: `harvest workflow diagnose <exec-id>` renders a human-readable verdict (leading with `health` + `summary`, then every `blocked_on` member), `--json` prints the raw body. Runbook: a "Start here for a single wedged run" stanza with a `blocked_on.type` → action table at the top of `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md`. **Tests:** 97 pure classifier unit tests (`stall_diagnosis.rs`), 62 DB/HTTP integration tests (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/stall_diagnosis_integration.rs`, dual-mode `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`/testcontainers, registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`) covering AC3 (no-worker + its live-worker control), AC4 (future timer healthy with a two-year-old last event), AC5 (open circuit with cooldown; backing-off task with attempt/last_error/next_attempt_at), AC6 (`no_pending_work` stalled), AC7 (terminal outcome, 404/400, and a zero-writes + breaker-phase-unchanged assertion across three repeated calls), AC2 (replay-derived awaited signal, pending child, paused, and the fan-out worst-of rule), plus admin gating; and CLI mapping/coverage/renderer tests. Out of scope (per the issue): auto-remediation, fleet-wide stall *discovery* (#486), new stall-detection thresholds or scanners, historical/trend analysis, cross-shard aggregation. **Post-review hardening (four parallel adversarial reviews — correctness/classifier semantics, performance/read-only-safety/drift, test-quality/AC-evidence, and API-design/repo-conventions — every genuine finding fixed):** (1) **P1 — an unfired durable timer past its deadline reported `healthy`.** Timers fire ONLY when a worker claims the owning workflow task (`worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals`); there is no independent timer scanner, so a long-missed deadline proves that task was never claimed. The mere presence of a timer therefore DOWNGRADED the genuine lost-task stall the same wedge reports without one (`no_pending_work`). New `timer_overdue { fires_at, overdue_by_seconds }` variant (`stalled`), gated by `TIMER_OVERDUE_GRACE_SECONDS` (60 s) so ordinary poll latency is never reported as a wedge, and checked ABOVE the signal/child/handoff categories so a signal-or-deadline race (#476) whose deadline the engine missed cannot hide behind the healthy-looking `awaiting_signal`. (2) **P1 — the task-queue read loaded five jsonb payload columns it never used.** `TaskQueueItem::as_select()` on a stalled wide fan-out of large activity inputs — the exact shape this endpoint exists to diagnose — moved hundreds of megabytes to answer a triage question, twice on the replay path. Replaced with a ten-scalar projection; deliberately still unbounded, because the worst-of fold must see every row and the narrow projection already removed the cost. (3) **P2 — a claimed (`RUNNING`) row whose queue has no live poller reported `healthy`.** That is a poison-pill orphan (#367); the reclaimer heals it within a poll interval EXCEPT when the whole fleet for that queue is down, which is the flagship `activity_no_worker` case, so the endpoint answered "fine" forever for a run that could never move. Claimed rows now require a live poller to read healthy, and `queues_in_play` is built from ALL loaded rows (not just PENDING ones) so liveness is genuinely evaluated rather than defaulting to `false` because it was never checked. (4) **P2 — `saturated_rate_limit_keys` was fail-OPEN while `claim_task`'s gate is fail-CLOSED.** The gate is `EXISTS(bucket >= 1.0)`, so a key with no bucket row at all (registration failed, the row was deleted, or startup skipped an invalid config) is permanently unclaimable — but the positive "which keys are saturated?" query returned nothing for it and the classifier reported `healthy`. Inverted to ask the admissible set and subtract. (5) **P2 — a not-yet-due task was misreported as rate-limited/concurrency-deferred.** A backing-off task has not reached the claim gates at all, so a momentarily-empty bucket says nothing about it — and reporting one dropped `attempt`, `last_error` and `next_attempt_at`, the three fields an operator wants. Retry backoff now sits above the two SELF-HEALING gates in the per-row ladder while the three non-self-healing ones (`queue_paused`, `no_worker`, `circuit_open`) still outrank it. (6) **P2 — `contributing_reason_codes` could drop or misattribute reasons.** `diagnosed_activity` re-sampled `Utc::now()` instead of the handler's snapshot, so a task whose backoff expired mid-request could flip the winner's kind and silently empty the list — or attribute one row's reasons to a different row's verdict. The second scan is deleted outright: reasons are now unioned across all rows, which also fixes the masking hole and stops fabricating `no_live_worker` for a claimed row whose coverage was never evaluated. (7) **P2 — `last_error` bypassed #608 read-path decode** that `/stack` applies to the same column, so an admin saw plaintext there and ciphertext here; now decoded with the audit row. (8) **P2 — the AC5 `cooldown_until` clause had no proof at any level**: the one test claiming it used `force_open`, which sets `forced_open` and therefore structurally CANNOT produce a cooldown. Renamed to pin the forced-open shape (asserting the field is ABSENT — the signal that recovery needs an explicit `force-close`) and added an organically-tripped test that exercises the real `time_until_probe_secs` → `DateTime` derivation, plus unit tests for `circuit_cooldown_until` over NaN/±inf/negative/overflow. (9) **P2 — the replay was un-deadlined**: `build_awaitables_report` inflates offloaded payloads per event (#524) outside the query timeout, so a long history with a remote `PayloadStore` could run for minutes on a latency-budgeted triage endpoint; now bounded by the server's query timeout, degrading to `wait_set_timed_out`. A `terminal` wait-set answer from the TOCTOU race where the run goes terminal mid-request is mapped to `execution_went_terminal` rather than leaking a fourth undocumented vocabulary value. (10) **P3s:** rate-limit/concurrency key vectors deduped (a wide fan-out sharing one key bound one array element per row); the phantom `CLAIMED`/`BACKOFF` task states corrected in the docs (the engine's CHECK constraint admits only `PENDING`/`RUNNING`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`, and retry backoff is `PENDING` with a future `scheduled_at`); an unnamed activity in backoff no longer falls through to healthy (`ActivityRetrying.activity_name` is now `Option<String>`, uniform with every sibling variant); `summarize` re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside its three siblings; a Module Guide row added; the two `diagnose` / `replay-diagnosis` CLI subcommands cross-reference each other; and the runbook now notes that `cooldown_until` is absent for an operator-forced-open breaker. **Ten new integration tests** close the wire-coverage gaps the review found: `activity_rate_limited` (plus a missing-bucket case pinning the fail-closed fix), `activity_concurrency_deferred`, `activity_queue_paused`, `awaiting_external_handoff`, the orphaned-`RUNNING` case, `timer_overdue`, the cross-row reason union, the organically-tripped cooldown, and the replay degrade path (which revealed the endpoint passes the precise upstream `handler_not_registered` reason through verbatim — strictly better than its own generic fallback). **Known limitation, narrowed in rounds 7-8 below:** `has_live_worker` now applies the task's own `required_build_id` (#171/#604), `required_capabilities` (#804), **session pin** (#606) and **Active-only** poller liveness as well as queue coverage; an ordinary **sticky lease** (#235) is still deliberately not modelled, because it self-heals at `sticky_until` — see round 8 for why flagging a self-healing condition would be a false positive on the flagship verdict. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two P2s fixed, one P1 refuted with evidence):** (a) **P2 (fixed) — a future `scheduled_at` alone was read as "failed and retrying".** The dispatcher also pushes a task forward with NO failure at all: `queue::defer_rate_limited_task` (dispatch-time rate limiting, #699/#369) even decrements the claim-time attempt back down because "a rate-limit deferral is not an attempt", and the session-capacity (#606) and capability-miss (#804) paths reuse the same `CleanContinuationChangeset`. Reporting those as `activity_retrying` sent an operator hunting a failure that never happened. The not-yet-due branch now turns on **failure evidence** — a recorded `error`, which `CleanContinuationChangeset` never clears, so its presence is durable proof an attempt really did fail and its absence proof that none ever did — and reports the new `activity_deferred { activity_name?, next_attempt_at }` variant otherwise (`healthy`; it self-heals). It ranks directly below `activity_retrying` in the cross-task ladder (failure evidence is the more actionable of the two) and the three non-self-healing gates still outrank both. (b) **P2 (fixed) — the terminal fast path returned `execution.error` verbatim**, skipping the #608 read-path decode the pending-activity path applies to the same TEXT column, so on a codec-encrypting deployment an admin received a ciphertext envelope while the decode audit recorded nothing. Now routed through `decode_error_field` + `decode_outcome`, mirroring the activity site exactly. (c) **P1 (refuted, pinned by regression test) — "check overdue timers before returning an activity verdict".** Hoisting the overdue-timer check above the activity bucket would introduce a **false positive**, the one verdict this endpoint must never emit. Whether an overdue unfired timer is a wedge depends entirely on whether the owning workflow task was scheduled to wake at that deadline: a timer-only suspension (and the `receive_signal_timeout` deadline race, which routes to the same persist path) calls `queue::reschedule_task(task_id, fires_at)`, so an unfired timer past it proves the wake never happened — and those shapes leave no pending activity row, so they already reach the check. But `persist_scheduled_activities` parks the task on the ACTIVITY and explicitly discards the armed deadline (`_min_fires_at`, commented in the engine "armed timers observed on next wake; deadline unused here"), so a cancellable timer (#768) armed alongside an activity — `join!(handle.await_fire(), ctx.execute_activity(..))` — goes overdue as a matter of course while the activity runs and fires on the activity's completion wake. Hoisting would report that healthy run `stalled`. The ordering is now documented in-code with that engine evidence and pinned by three tests: `healthy_activity_alongside_an_overdue_timer_is_not_a_stall`, `overdue_timer_still_wins_when_no_activity_is_pending`, and `wedged_activity_alongside_an_overdue_timer_reports_the_activity`. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two more findings, both genuine and both fixed):** both are the same root defect — `no_pending_work`, the most alarming verdict this endpoint can return, was reached before two whole classes of evidence had been consulted. (a) **P1 — the run's OWN workflow task row was discarded.** The task query filtered `task_type = 'activity'`, so the `task_type = 'workflow'` row — which every non-terminal run has exactly one of — was invisible. That row is the only place three states are distinguishable: the handler EXECUTING right now (`worker_id` held, canonically a run mid-way through a long local activity (#98), which schedules no queue row of any kind), the decision cycle AWAITING DISPATCH (`PENDING`), and the genuinely PARKED row (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker, per `park_workflow_task`'s own SQL). Without it, a perfectly healthy in-flight or about-to-be-claimed run fell through every category and reported `no_pending_work`/`stalled`. Fixed with a single-row indexed lookup feeding the new `WorkflowTaskFacts` + pure `classify_workflow_task`, consulted **as a fallback below every side-table cause** (a workflow task always exists, so consulting it higher would flatten every specific verdict): a held claim → `healthy_in_progress`; a `PENDING` row → `healthy_in_progress` when a live worker polls its queue or it is deliberately deferred, the new `workflow_queue_paused { queue }` (`blocked_external`) when an operator holds that queue (#619), and the new `workflow_no_worker { queue }` (`stalled`) — the workflow-task analogue of AC3's flagship no-live-worker condition — when nothing polls it; a **parked** row yields `None` so the lost-task verdict is unchanged (a parked row advances on a *wake*, not a claim, so a live worker proves nothing). The workflow queue joins `queues_in_play` so its liveness is answered by the same canonical #774 predicate as every activity queue. (b) **P2 — every non-`Signal` replay awaitable was dropped.** The replay filter kept only `AwaitableKind::Signal`, discarding `Condition`, `Mutex`, `Update`, `ExternalWorkflow` (and `Activity`/`ChildWorkflow`/`Timer`) — and a command-less `ctx.await_condition` park, a durable mutex acquire (#691), an admitted update awaiting its handler, and a parked external-workflow operation (#492/#757/#751) leave **no row in any side table this endpoint reads**, so replay is the only source that can see them. A run legitimately parked on any of them reported `no_pending_work`/`stalled`. Fixed with the new `awaiting_replay_wait { wait_kind, name?, since? }` variant (`blocked_external`), fed from every non-`Signal` awaitable in recorded/command order (deterministic) and consulted **below every side-table cause** — so it can only ever replace a false lost-task verdict and can never mask a more precise one such as `sleeping_timer` (pinned by `replay_wait_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`); signals keep their own dedicated, higher-ranked verdict. Both fixes are additive to `DiagnosisInputs` (`workflow_task: Option<_>`, `replay_waits: Vec<_>`, both defaulting empty), so every pre-existing caller and the classifier's prior behaviour are byte-identical. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified by neutering the two ladder branches (6 unit tests fail, the ordering/regression guards stay green). 15 new pure unit tests and 5 new DB/HTTP integration tests (claimed → healthy, `PENDING` on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker` naming it, its live-worker control, parked → still `no_pending_work`, and the fallback-never-masks-a-wedged-activity guard). **Post-review hardening, round 4 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two more findings, both genuine and both fixed):** both are the round-3 workflow-task classifier reintroducing, for the workflow row, two defects already fixed for ACTIVITY rows in round 1 — a stored claim treated as progress without checking liveness, and a self-healing deferral returned ahead of a non-self-healing gate. (a) **P1 — a stale claim reported `healthy_in_progress`.** `classify_workflow_task`'s `has_worker` fast path returned healthy unconditionally, but a crashed worker leaves its workflow task `RUNNING` with a non-null `worker_id` until the poison-pill reclaimer processes it (issue #367) — exactly the orphan shape `orphaned_running_tasks_query` selects. With nothing polling the queue that claim never advances, so the endpoint answered “fine” forever for a run that could not move (indefinitely, if the reclaimer is itself impaired). (b) **P2 — a not-yet-due deferral was accepted before the coverage check.** For a `PENDING` row with `scheduled_at` in the future, `healthy_in_progress` was returned *above* the `has_live_worker` gate, so an uncovered queue read healthy until the timestamp arrived even though nobody would claim it then; unlike a timed sleep, a dispatcher deferral only self-heals if something claims the row. Both fixed by reordering `classify_workflow_task` onto `classify_pending_activity`'s **hard-impediment-first ladder**: a held claim is healthy only when a live worker still polls its queue (else `workflow_no_worker`), and a `PENDING` row resolves `queue_paused` → `no_worker` → not-yet-due → healthy. Liveness uses the same fleet-coverage proxy (`worker_covers_queue`, #774) the activity classifier uses, carrying the same documented limitation. The **parked** case (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker) is deliberately unchanged — it advances on a *wake*, not a claim, so a live poller proves nothing and it still yields `None` to the lost-task verdict. A pause remains a claim-time gate and so never downgrades an already-executing handler. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified (2 new unit tests fail against the old ordering, both controls stay green). 3 new pure unit tests + 2 controls and 3 new DB/HTTP integration tests (stale claim on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker`, not-yet-due on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker`, and its live-worker control); the round-3 `claimed_workflow_task_reports_healthy_not_a_lost_task` DB test named its worker `w-live` but never registered it as live, so it now seeds one to exercise the healthy path its name describes. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (Codex bot review of PR #1188, one P1 — genuine, and broader than reported):** the `timer_overdue` verdict was returned for **any** unfired timer past the grace window, without checking whether that timer actually owns the run's wake. Codex named the external-handoff case (`persist_scheduled_external_activity` parks the task and discards `_min_fires_at`, so a partner callback slower than the window leaves a legitimately-overdue row); auditing `worker.rs` showed the defect is a **class**, not a case — `_min_fires_at` is discarded at eight sites across seven persist functions (`persist_signal_wait_park`, `persist_mutex_acquire_park`, `persist_activity_wait_park`, `persist_scheduled_activities`, `persist_started_timer`, `persist_all_started_child_workflows`, and `persist_scheduled_external_activity` twice), and **only** `persist_started_timer` then calls `queue::reschedule_task(task_id, fires_at)` to hand the timer ownership of the wake. Because the overdue check ranked ABOVE external handoffs, children and awaited signals, a timer armed alongside **any** of those reported a false `timer_overdue`/`stalled` — activities were spared only by the round-2 ordering guard. Fixed with the precise gate Codex suggested rather than a reorder (which would be whack-a-mole across four ranked-below categories): the new pure `workflow_wake_was_missed(task, now)` keys on the workflow task row's **own** wake — a *claimed* row means the handler is executing, a *parked* row (`RUNNING`, NULL worker) means some other wake owns the run, and only a `PENDING` row past its own `scheduled_at` by the grace window is a genuinely missed timer wake. Absent facts resolve to `true`, so every pre-gate caller is byte-identical. This also handles the multi-timer case in both directions (an overdue passenger timer alongside a later-armed owning timer no longer wins) and **preserves** the round-2 refutation: the issue #476 `receive_signal_timeout` deadline race still routes to `persist_started_timer` (verified — `should_requeue_signal_wait`'s allowlist excludes `StartTimer`, so a mixed `StartTimer + WaitForSignal` batch falls through to `extract_started_timer_for_suspension`), so a genuinely missed deadline race still outranks `awaiting_signal`. The ordering guard is kept as well, because it remains load-bearing for the activity case specifically: `persist_scheduled_activities` leaves the row `PENDING` at a *retry* `scheduled_at`, which the gate alone cannot distinguish from a missed timer wake. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified at both levels (5 pure tests and the new DB test fail against the ungated classifier, each reporting `timer_overdue` where a precise verdict is expected). 7 new pure unit tests (parked-task → handoff/child/signal, the preserved genuine-miss case, claim-suppressed, next-wake-still-ahead, and a `workflow_wake_was_missed` truth table) and 2 new DB/HTTP integration tests (an overdue timer alongside a parked external handoff reports the handoff; a `PENDING` row long past its own `scheduled_at` still reports `timer_overdue`). `classify_workflow_task`, `workflow_wake_was_missed`, `WorkflowTaskFacts`, `ReplayWaitFacts` and `TIMER_OVERDUE_GRACE_SECONDS` are now re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside their siblings, making the module-guide claim accurate. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (Codex bot review of `7e7478c`, one P1): a timer cannot fire if its own workflow task can never be claimed.** Round 4 stopped `timer_overdue` from false-firing when some *other* wake owned the run; Codex found the mirror-image gap on the healthy side. A durable timer fires only when a worker claims the owning workflow task and `worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals` runs — there is no independent timer scanner — so a run "sleeping" on a timer whose **workflow** queue is operator-held (#619) or has no live poller is not sleeping: it can never wake. `classify_execution` returned `sleeping_timer`/`healthy` (before the deadline) or `timer_overdue` (after it) before `classify_workflow_task` could ever report `workflow_queue_paused`/`workflow_no_worker`, so the endpoint answered "fine" for a permanently wedged run and, past the deadline, named the elapsed timer rather than the queue an operator must actually fix. Fixed with a new pure `workflow_task_hard_impediment(&WorkflowTaskFacts) -> Option<BlockedOn>` that returns **only** the two hard impediments (`WorkflowQueuePaused`, `WorkflowNoWorker`) — never the ordinary healthy-dispatch verdict, which stays in the fallback so it cannot mask the more specific `sleeping_timer` — consulted in `classify_execution` immediately **above** the `timer_overdue` gate. Placement is deliberate in both directions: **below** the activity bucket, because a wedged activity names the specific thing to fix (pinned by `wedged_activity_still_outranks_a_workflow_queue_impediment`); **above** the handoff/child/signal categories is harmless *by construction*, because every one of those parks the workflow task and a parked row (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker) advances on a wake rather than a claim, so no claim-time gate applies and the helper returns `None` (pinned by `parked_workflow_task_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`). `classify_workflow_task` was refactored to delegate to the same helper, so the fallback verdict and the timer gate can never drift about whether a row is claimable; its `now` parameter became dead and was removed (the deferral branch and the due branch both resolved to `HealthyInProgress`, so the ladder is behaviour-identical — verified case-by-case and pinned by the pre-existing `classify_workflow_task` tests). **Known residual, deliberately scoped:** a *healthy* activity on a different, live queue alongside a dead/paused **workflow** queue still reports `healthy_in_progress` — hoisting above the activity bucket to catch it would mask wedged-activity verdicts, a strictly worse trade. (When the two queues are the same, the activity row reports `activity_no_worker` itself, so the common case is covered.) **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change.** Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified as 4 behavioural failures against the unwired classifier): 8 pure tests — `sleeping_timer_on_a_paused_workflow_queue_reports_queue_paused`, `sleeping_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, `sleeping_timer_with_a_healthy_workflow_queue_is_still_a_sleeping_timer`, `overdue_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, `claimed_workflow_task_on_a_dead_queue_outranks_a_sleeping_timer`, `parked_workflow_task_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`, `wedged_activity_still_outranks_a_workflow_queue_impediment`, and the `workflow_task_hard_impediment_truth_table` — plus 3 DB/HTTP tests (`sleeping_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, its live-poller control `sleeping_timer_with_a_live_workflow_queue_is_still_a_sleeping_timer`, and `sleeping_timer_on_a_paused_workflow_queue_reports_queue_paused`). `workflow_task_hard_impediment` is re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside its siblings. **Post-review hardening, round 6 (Codex bot review of `51789a3`, two findings — one P1, one P2):** (1) **P1 — an nd-blocked run reported healthy.** When replay diverges the engine BLOCKS the run (issue #603) rather than failing it: `block_workflow_for_non_determinism` leaves the execution `RUNNING` and `requeue_workflow_task_nd_blocked` re-pends its workflow task at a capped-exponential backoff (`5s * 2^count`, 300s ceiling) **indefinitely**, until a build that replays the recorded history cleanly is deployed. By task-row shape alone that is byte-identical to an ordinary dispatcher deferral (`PENDING`, unheld, future `scheduled_at`), so a permanently wedged run on a covered queue reported `healthy_in_progress` — the exact opposite of the truth, for a run only an operator rollback can free. Fixed with a new `BlockedOn::NonDeterminismBlocked { since, reason?, block_count }` (`non_determinism_blocked`, `stalled`) sourced from the execution row's own `nd_blocked_at`/`nd_block_reason`/`nd_block_count` columns via the new `NdBlockFacts`, ranked **directly under `paused`**: both are the same *class* of fact — an explicit state the engine or an operator stamped on the execution row, not an inference from a liveness proxy or a timestamp. It outranks every side-table cause because the block re-fires on **every** decision cycle regardless of what those rows are doing, and nothing is lost, since a pending activity's own impediments still reach the operator through `contributing_reason_codes` (a union across rows, not the winner's reasons). `paused` stays above it, mirroring the engine: a pause observed under the row lock supersedes the block and re-parks instead. (2) **P2 — decode exactly what is surfaced.** The per-row activity facts previously carried each row's `last_error` **decoded**, so on a codec-encrypting deployment a LOSING row's encrypted error was decrypted and counted into the `payload.decode_read` audit row even though it never left the handler — violating the issue #608 contract. Classification only needs the error's *presence* (it is the failure-evidence discriminator separating `activity_retrying` from `activity_deferred`), so the facts now carry it **raw** and only the winning `BlockedOn::ActivityRetrying { last_error }` is decoded, after `classify_execution` picks it, through the new pure `decode_surfaced_activity_error`. **Two latent footguns found while fixing the above, both closed:** `summarize` and `summarize_activity_cause` were **mutually recursive** through their two catch-all arms, so the new variant (owned by neither) overflowed the stack instead of returning a string — the helper now returns `Option<String>` and `summarize` falls back to `format!("blocked on {}", kind())`, making the pair non-recursive and total; and `kind()` (hand-written) had drifted from the serde-derived wire tag (`nondeterminism_blocked` vs `non_determinism_blocked`), silently splitting the bounded `blocked_on.type` vocabulary the CLI renderer and runbook key on — `kind()` now matches the derive, pinned for **every** variant by `kind_matches_the_serialized_wire_tag_for_every_variant` (`kind()` is exhaustively matched with no catch-all, so a new variant is a compile error there and the shared `all_verdicts()` fixture carries it into both pins). Tests, TDD red→green (RED confirmed by neutering the classify branch: the money test reports `healthy_in_progress` and the outranks test `activity_no_worker`): 5 pure nd-block classification tests plus `every_verdict_summarizes_without_recursing` and the wire-tag pin (`stall_diagnosis.rs`, 96 total); 4 pure plugin decode-scope tests (`only_the_surfaced_activity_error_is_decoded`, `a_losing_rows_error_is_never_decoded_or_audited`, `decode_is_a_noop_without_an_active_decoder`, `a_retrying_verdict_without_an_error_is_a_noop`, whose envelope fixture is built through the public `encode_event` seam so it cannot drift from the engine's real envelope shape); and 3 DB/HTTP tests (`nd_blocked_execution_reports_the_block_not_healthy_dispatch`, `nd_block_outranks_a_wedged_activity_but_keeps_its_reason_codes`, and the control `a_run_that_was_never_nd_blocked_keeps_its_ordinary_verdict`). `NdBlockFacts` is re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside its siblings. **Post-review hardening, round 7 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — one P1, one P2, both genuine and both fixed):** both are cases where a database-observable fact was read too coarsely, so a genuinely-unclaimable or genuinely-unrelated row produced a **healthy** verdict. (1) **P1 — queue coverage is not the claim predicate.** `has_live_worker` answered only "does any live worker poll this queue?", but `queue::claim_task` additionally enforces the row's `required_build_id` (exact, `harvest_build_compat`-declared, or legacy empty-build worker) and its `required_capabilities` (the same Exact/In label match). A task pinned to a build no live poller runs — the canonical mid-rollout shape after a build cutover (#171/#604) — or requiring a capability label no live worker advertises (#804) therefore sat `PENDING` indefinitely on a well-covered queue while the endpoint reported `healthy_in_progress`, defeating AC3's flagship "100% of the time it holds" no-live-worker guarantee for exactly the deployments that use build routing. Fixed with the new pure `task_has_eligible_worker(workers, shard_id, queue, required_build_id, required_capabilities, compat_set)`, which asks whether **any single worker** satisfies **every** dimension — queue coverage still through the canonical #774 `worker_covers_queue` predicate (so this surface and `GET /admin/queue-coverage` cannot drift), plus `BuildCompatibilitySet::is_eligible` and `eligibility::matches_requirements`, all evaluated against the **same** worker (a split fleet where one worker has the build and a different one has the label covers nothing — the exact discipline the stranded-work sampler already applies). `required_build_id`/`required_capabilities` are now loaded on the activity rows **and** on the run's own workflow-task row (the claim predicate's build clause has no task-type guard), and `harvest_build_compat` is loaded once per request. Unparseable `required_capabilities` fall back to the other dimensions rather than reporting a stall, so a value this endpoint cannot read can never fabricate a false `no_worker` — a false stall on the flagship verdict is the worst outcome for a triage tool. **Residual, deliberately left out:** a sticky lease / session pin (#235/#606) is still not modelled. The two cases need opposite treatment and getting them wrong produces a false positive: an ordinary #235 sticky lease self-heals the moment `sticky_until` elapses (reporting it as a stall would false-alarm on a row that resolves in seconds), whereas a #606 session pin never fails over and IS a genuine stall — so the leg is left as an honest documented gap rather than guessed at, and `GET /admin/queues/{queue}/eligibility` (#611) remains the per-worker surface that already reports `sticky_owned_by_other_worker`. (2) **P2 — detached children are not pending children.** The pending-child query keyed only on `parent_id`, but a **detached** child (#347) keeps `parent_id` while carrying a non-null `parent_close_policy`, and the engine uses exactly that discriminator (`worker.rs`'s `is_detached_child`) to decide a child does **not** wake its parent. A fire-and-forget child is therefore never something the parent waits on, so counting it reported a healthy `pending_child` for a parent genuinely parked elsewhere — masking an awaited signal or condition (visible only to the replay drive, which ranks *below* children and was consequently skipped entirely, `wait_set: "not_consulted"`) and even masking a lost workflow task as healthy for as long as the detached child happened to run. Fixed with a `parent_close_policy IS NULL` filter; awaited children are unaffected. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change** — both fixes are read-path accuracy. Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified for both by neutering the fix): 5 pure unit tests for `task_has_eligible_worker` (build absent/present, declared compatibility + legacy empty-build worker, capability unsatisfied/satisfied, same-worker-for-every-dimension, unparseable-capabilities fallback) and 8 DB/HTTP tests in `stall_diagnosis_integration.rs` — `task_requiring_an_absent_build_reports_no_worker_despite_queue_coverage`, `task_requiring_an_unsatisfied_capability_reports_no_worker`, `split_fleet_satisfying_each_dimension_separately_is_not_coverage` (all three reported `healthy_in_progress` pre-fix), their three positive controls, plus `detached_child_does_not_mask_the_signal_the_parent_is_parked_on` (pre-fix: `pending_child` + `health: healthy` + `wait_set: not_consulted`) and its `awaited_child_is_still_reported_as_pending` control. **Post-review hardening, round 8 (Codex bot review of `f9d0480` — one P1, one P2, both confirmed against engine source and both fixed):** both are cases where the diagnosis accepted a worker `queue::claim_task` would never let claim the row, producing a false `healthy_in_progress` on a genuinely unclaimable task. (1) **P1 — a session pin never fails over.** `claim_task_query`'s session clause is `session_id IS NULL OR sticky_worker_id = $1` — note it carries **no time component at all**, unlike the sticky clause directly above it. So a worker-session member (#606) is claimable ONLY by the host recorded in `sticky_worker_id`, forever; if that host dies, drains, or stops polling the queue, no peer can ever stand in for it and the row is permanently stuck. `task_has_eligible_worker` accepted any queue/build/capability-eligible worker, so exactly the scenario worker sessions exist for — a pipeline pinned to one host that then loses that host — reported healthy progress. Fixed by loading the row's `session_id` + `sticky_worker_id` and gating candidacy on the new `TaskClaimRequirements::session_admits`, a verbatim mirror of that SQL clause (a session member with a NULL `sticky_worker_id` matches no worker, since `sticky_worker_id = $1` can never hold against NULL). The pin composes with the round-7 dimensions against the **same** worker, so a live pinned host running the wrong build is still correctly reported unclaimable. (2) **P2 — a `Draining` worker claims nothing.** `queue_coverage::worker_covers_queue` counts `Active` **or** `Draining` as live — deliberate and correct for #774's deploy-oriented "is anything still attached to this queue?" — but `Worker::run` exits `run_poll_loop` **before** it transitions to `Draining` and then only waits for in-flight work, so a draining worker claims no new task for the entire drain window. A long drain therefore read as healthy progress on a queue nothing could pick up. Fixed with a private `worker_can_claim_now` that keeps the canonical #774 predicate for queue/shard attachment (so the two surfaces still cannot disagree about *what a worker is attached to*) and narrows only the liveness half to `Active`. **Deliberately still NOT modelled — an ordinary sticky lease (#235), now with a sharper rationale than round 7's:** its clause is `sticky_worker_id IS NULL OR sticky_worker_id = $1 OR sticky_until IS NULL OR sticky_until <= NOW()`, so it releases to the whole fleet at a known instant; a dead owner blocks the row only until `sticky_until`. Reporting a self-healing, seconds-long condition as `activity_no_worker`/`stalled` would be a false positive on the flagship verdict — the worst outcome for a triage tool — so the transient over-optimism is accepted, and `GET /admin/queues/{queue}/eligibility` (#611) remains the per-worker surface that reports `sticky_owned_by_other_worker`. A session pin has no such expiry, which is precisely why it IS modelled. Refactor: the six positional arguments of `task_has_eligible_worker` collapsed into a `TaskClaimRequirements<'_>` struct (`#[derive(Default)]`, so a test states only the dimension it exercises), keeping the function at four arguments as dimensions accumulate. Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified **behaviourally**, not merely as a compile error: neutering `session_admits` to always-true and dropping the `Active` check makes all four new pure tests fail): 5 new pure unit tests (`eligibility_session_member_requires_its_pinned_host`, `eligibility_session_member_without_a_recorded_host_is_unclaimable`, `eligibility_session_pin_still_applies_build_and_capabilities`, `eligibility_ignores_an_ordinary_sticky_lease` — which pins the deliberate omission above — and `eligibility_excludes_draining_workers`) and 4 new DB/HTTP tests (`session_pinned_task_whose_host_is_gone_reports_no_worker`, `draining_only_fleet_reports_no_worker`, plus their live-host and `Active`-fleet controls). **Post-review hardening, round 9 (Codex bot review of `03a0057`, two P2 findings, both confirmed and fixed):** (1) **P2 — a held row's liveness must follow its CLAIMANT, not claim eligibility.** Round 8's Active-only narrowing was applied to **every** row, including `RUNNING` ones — but `Worker::run` transitions a worker to `Draining` *before* awaiting `drain_in_flight`, so an activity already held by a gracefully-shutting-down worker is still legitimately progressing. It was reported `activity_no_worker`/`stalled` for the entire drain window (and the same hazard sat in `workflow_task_hard_impediment`'s `has_worker` branch for the run's own decision cycle). The two questions are now answered separately: a **PENDING** row asks "can any worker claim this right now?" (`worker_can_claim_now`, Active-only — unchanged), while a **HELD** row asks "is its own recorded claimant still alive?" via the new plugin helper `claimant_is_live`, which reuses the canonical #774 `worker_covers_queue` predicate verbatim (Active **or** Draining). Threaded as an additive `claimant_is_live: Option<bool>` on both `PendingActivityFacts` and `WorkflowTaskFacts`; `None` (no recorded claimant, or a caller that does not supply it) falls back to the previous queue-coverage answer, so a stall is never inferred from missing data. The activity task projection was widened with `worker_id` to carry it. The complement still holds: a held row whose claimant is **gone** is still the flagship orphan stall even when a healthy `Active` peer covers the queue, because a peer cannot pick up an already-claimed row — only the poison-pill reclaimer (#367) heals it. (2) **P2 — half-open must be distinguishable from operator-forced open.** Both report `cooldown_until: null` (a half-open breaker's cooldown has already elapsed; a forced-open one admits no timed probe), so they collapsed to the same wire shape and `summarize` told an operator a *self-recovering* breaker "needs an explicit force-close". The observed phase is now preserved: `BlockingCircuitPhase` gained `Serialize`/`Deserialize` (`open` | `half_open`), `BlockedOn::ActivityCircuitOpen` carries an additive `phase` field, and `summarize` gained a leading `HalfOpen` arm ("a probe is admitted now and it closes on success, with no operator action"). `health()` stays `Stalled` for both — the AC lists `circuit_open` as a stall root cause, and the actionable ask was the forced-vs-recovering distinction, not the severity. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change** — an additive fact field, an additive response field, and a widened read projection. Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified **behaviourally** at both levels): 7 new pure unit tests (`held_row_with_a_draining_claimant_is_still_progressing`, `held_row_whose_claimant_is_gone_is_still_an_orphan`, `held_row_without_an_identifiable_claimant_falls_back_to_coverage`, `pending_row_still_uses_claim_eligibility_not_the_claimant`, `claimed_workflow_task_with_a_draining_claimant_is_progressing`, `half_open_circuit_is_not_described_as_operator_forced`, `classifier_preserves_the_observed_circuit_phase` — neutering either fix fails exactly the corresponding subset) and 4 new DB/HTTP tests (`held_activity_on_a_draining_claimant_is_still_progressing`, `held_activity_whose_claimant_is_gone_reports_no_worker`, `held_workflow_task_with_a_draining_claimant_is_progressing`, `half_open_circuit_is_not_reported_as_operator_forced`; neutering the plugin `claimant_is_live` wiring to always-`None` fails the first three, proving the wiring — not just the classifier — supplies the value). **Post-review hardening, round 10 (Codex bot review of `dd33340`, one P2 — genuine, and self-inflicted by round 9):** the round-9 fix taught the CLASSIFIER to judge a held row on its own claimant's liveness, but `contributing_reasons_for` (the `contributing_reason_codes` union, issue #611) still keyed `no_live_worker` on the queue-level `has_live_worker` for **every** row — so the two surfaces of the same response contradicted each other in both directions: a row held by a live **Draining** claimant reported `health: healthy` / `healthy_in_progress` yet carried `no_live_worker`, and an orphan held by a **dead** claimant OMITTED that code whenever a healthy Active peer happened to cover the queue — the one case the reason exists to surface, and the flagship AC3 guarantee. Fixed by mirroring `classify_pending_activity`'s split exactly: a **PENDING** row still asks claim eligibility (`has_live_worker`, Active only), a **HELD** row asks its own recorded claimant's liveness (`claimant_is_live.unwrap_or(has_live_worker)`, Active OR Draining) — same fallback, so a row whose claimant cannot be identified is never inferred to be stalled. The `held` predicate is now computed once and reused for the existing claim-gate skip, so the two cannot drift. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change** — one read-path selector. Tests, TDD red→green (RED confirmed behaviourally: both new pure tests fail against the pre-fix selector, with the exact contradiction each names): 2 new pure unit tests (`contributing_reasons_use_claimant_liveness_for_a_held_row` — live draining claimant, no Active coverage → empty reason set; `contributing_reasons_report_an_orphan_even_when_an_active_peer_covers_the_queue` — dead claimant + live Active peer → `no_live_worker` present), plus reason-code assertions added to the two round-9 DB/HTTP tests so the wiring is proven end-to-end (`held_activity_on_a_draining_claimant_is_still_progressing` now asserts the code is ABSENT; `held_activity_whose_claimant_is_gone_reports_no_worker` asserts it is PRESENT). The 3 pre-existing `contributing_reasons_*` tests are unchanged and still pass, so the PENDING path and the claimed-row claim-gate skip are byte-for-byte preserved. **Post-review hardening, round 12 (Codex bot review of `426bbf2`, one P1 + one P2):** (a) **P1 — a per-process breaker snapshot is not a fleet-wide verdict.** `CircuitBreakerRegistry` is deliberately in-process (`circuit_breaker.rs`: "Each shard / worker process tracks its own breaker"), constructed per `HandlerRegistry`, with no table backing it — and the breaker that actually gates a dispatch belongs to whichever worker CLAIMS the task (`process_activity_task`). The endpoint nonetheless applied its own replica's phase to every pending row, so in a multi-replica fleet an open breaker here produced a false `activity_circuit_open`/`stalled` for a task a peer replica (breaker closed) could still dispatch — a false positive on the flagship stall verdict, the worst outcome for a triage tool. Codex's prescribed fix ("account for the eligible workers' actual breaker states") is not mechanically possible: there is no cross-process breaker state to read, and adding one is a #369 architectural change. Fixed by scoping the claim instead: `task_has_eligible_worker` is refactored onto a new id-returning `eligible_worker_ids` (the boolean stays exactly "the set is non-empty", so every prior eligibility guarantee is preserved by construction), and the new pure `local_circuit_snapshot_is_authoritative(eligible_ids, local_worker_id)` admits the local phase **only** when this process's own co-located worker (`HarvestApiRuntime::worker_id`) is the SOLE eligible worker — i.e. exactly when our breaker is provably the one that will gate the dispatch. An API-only replica (`worker_id: None`) drives no breaker at all and never decides the verdict. The accepted cost is a deliberate **false negative**: a genuinely fleet-wide outage (every replica open) degrades to the next-ranked verdict instead of `activity_circuit_open`, which is the safe direction for a stall verdict, with `GET /admin/circuits` per replica remaining the authoritative per-breaker surface. `contributing_reasons_for` now derives its phase map from the **gated facts** rather than the raw snapshot (dropping its `cb_phase` parameter), so the advisory reason codes and the headline verdict cannot disagree about a circuit block — the same two-surfaces-consistency rule the round-10 held-row liveness split established. (b) **P2 — a half-open breaker is not a stall.** `ExecutionHealth::Healthy` is documented as "progressing, **or blocked on something that clears without intervention**", and a `half_open` breaker admits a probe right now and closes on success — which the verdict's own summary already told the operator ("no operator action") while `health()` still returned `Stalled` ("needs a human: nothing will move this run forward on its own"). `health()` now branches on the phase: `HalfOpen` → `Healthy`, `Open` → `Stalled` (unchanged for both the operator-forced and organically-tripped shapes, which genuinely fast-fail every dispatch). Test fixtures: the three pre-existing circuit DB tests seeded a live worker (`worker-payments`) whose id never matched the runtime's own advertised `worker_id` (`diagnose-test`) — an artificial mismatch that never modelled the real co-located single-replica deployment; they now seed the co-located worker through a shared `LOCAL_WORKER_ID` constant so the fixture and the runtime cannot drift. Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified behaviourally by neutering the authority predicate to always-true, which fails both new DB tests, and by the `health()` assertion failing before the phase branch existed): 2 pure unit tests (`local_circuit_snapshot_is_authoritative_only_for_a_sole_local_eligible_worker` over all five shapes, `eligible_worker_ids_lists_every_worker_that_can_claim` incl. the boolean-equivalence pin), 1 pure classifier test (`half_open_circuit_health_is_healthy_not_stalled`, also pinning both OPEN shapes as still stalled), and 2 DB tests (`open_circuit_is_not_reported_when_a_peer_replica_could_also_dispatch` — which also asserts the reason codes decline in step with the verdict — and `open_circuit_is_not_reported_by_an_api_replica_with_no_local_worker`). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change.** **Post-review hardening, round 11 (Codex bot review of `f32664a`, one P2 — genuine):** `task_has_eligible_worker` read capability requirements from the task row's `required_capabilities` column ALONE, so a **legacy or manually enqueued** activity row — which can carry `NULL` there — was treated as having no requirements and any queue poller counted as coverage. But `claim_task_query`'s **ineligible-activities gate (`$6`)** does not skip such a row: it rejects any worker whose `ineligible_activities` list contains the row's `activity_name`, and that list is computed on each worker from the **registered** `ActivityInfo::requires` matched against its own labels (`Worker::new`). So the endpoint reported `healthy_in_progress` for a task no live worker could claim — an **AC3 false negative** on the flagship no-live-worker guarantee, and the one verdict class this endpoint exists to get right. Fixed with the new pure `effective_required_capabilities(row_capabilities, activity_name, registered)`: the row's own snapshot **wins** when present (`claim_task` short-circuits `$6` on `required_capabilities IS NOT NULL`, so the snapshot is what gates the claim and a since-changed registry must never override it), and only an **absent** snapshot falls back to the registered requirements — resolved once per request from `HandlerRegistry::activity_requirements_json()` (the same helper `queue::apply_activity_requirements` uses for the shard-health coverage backfill, and the same resolution the #611 eligibility explainer already performed), so all three surfaces answer the capability question identically. Applied at the **activity** fact site only: `claim_task`'s gate is guarded by `task_type != 'activity'`, so a workflow task is only ever gated by its own snapshot — documented inline at that site. With no runtime installed the map is empty, degrading to the previous snapshot-only answer rather than fabricating a stall. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change** — one read-path resolution. Tests, TDD red→green: 4 new pure unit tests (backfill-on-absent, snapshot-wins, neither-source, plus the behavioural composition through `task_has_eligible_worker` with a satisfying-worker control) and 3 new DB/HTTP tests using a dedicated `registry_gated` activity (`requires = "gpu=true"`) whose queue row carries **no** snapshot: `unsnapshotted_task_is_gated_by_the_registered_requirements` (RED against the pre-fix wiring with the exact `healthy_in_progress` vs `activity_no_worker` contradiction), plus the controls `unsnapshotted_task_with_a_satisfying_worker_is_healthy` and `unsnapshotted_task_for_an_ungated_activity_is_unaffected` — both of which stay GREEN under the neutered wiring, proving the fix is not over-broad. The dedicated activity name keeps the pre-existing build/capability tests (which seed `gated_activity` with a NULL snapshot deliberately) byte-for-byte unchanged. DB suite **60/60** against real Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 13 (Codex bot review of `521dadb`, one P2 — genuine):** the round-11 registry fallback (recovering an unsnapshotted row's capability requirement from the *registered* activity's `requires`) was applied to **every** eligible worker, but `claim_task`'s ineligible-activities gate (`activity_name = ANY($6)`) receives that list from **each claiming worker's own** registry (`Worker::new`, `worker.rs:19044`) — so during a rolling deploy where the new build adds `#[activity(requires = ...)]` to an activity the old build has no requirement for, the endpoint rejected the still-eligible old-build worker and fabricated `activity_no_worker` for a row `claim_task` would happily admit. A false **positive** on the flagship stall verdict is the worst error this endpoint can make, so the fallback is now scoped to workers this process can speak for: `resolve_required_capabilities` returns a `ResolvedCapabilities { requirements, from_registry_fallback }` (the row's own snapshot sets the flag `false` — a snapshot gates every build, since `claim_task` short-circuits on `required_capabilities IS NOT NULL`), and `eligible_worker_ids`/`task_has_eligible_worker` skip a fallback-derived requirement for any worker whose `build_id` differs from the local one (`registry_fallback_binds`). `local_build_id_from_workers` reads the local worker's advertised build from `harvest_workers`; an **unidentified** local build (an API-only replica, or a co-located worker whose row is absent) resolves to `""`, which is exactly the value every worker advertises in a deployment with no build routing — so the default deployment is byte-identical to round 11, and the fallback simply stops binding where it cannot be trusted. **Documented residual:** a rolling deploy in a deployment that sets **no** build ids is invisible to this discriminator (every worker reads `""`), so the round-11 behaviour still applies there. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change.** Tests: 3 new pure unit tests (`registry_fallback_binds_only_to_a_worker_on_the_local_build`, `local_build_id_reads_the_local_workers_advertised_build`, `registry_fallback_does_not_gate_a_worker_on_a_different_build` with two controls — same-build still gated, a snapshotted requirement gates every build) and 2 DB/HTTP tests (`rolling_deploy_old_build_worker_is_not_rejected_on_the_new_builds_requirement`, `same_build_workers_are_still_gated_by_the_registry_fallback`). DB suite **64/64** against real Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 14 (Codex bot review of `90fa404`, one P1 — genuine):** `saturated_rate_limit_keys` deliberately asked the ADMISSIBLE set and inverted it, so a key with **no bucket row at all** landed in the saturated set alongside a merely-drained one. That fixed the fail-open direction (an earlier round) but over-corrected: `claim_task`'s gate is `EXISTS(bucket WHERE ... >= 1.0)`, which refuses a missing row **forever** — nothing refills a row that does not exist — while the resulting `activity_rate_limited` verdict carries `health: healthy` and a summary that promises automatic refill. A permanent stall was therefore reported as self-healing. Split at the source: `rate_limit_gate_status` now asks one query (`SELECT key, (LEAST(...) >= 1.0) AS admissible`) and returns both answers — a key absent from the result has no row (`missing`), a key present but inadmissible is drained (`saturated`). New `PendingActivityFacts.rate_limit_bucket_missing` and a distinct `BlockedOn::ActivityRateLimitBucketMissing { key, activity_name }` whose `health()` is **`Stalled`**. Placed in the activity precedence ladder directly after `activity_no_worker` — both are permanent, and it outranks the not-due-yet check for the same reason `no_worker` does: a backing-off task whose bucket row does not exist will not be claimable when it becomes due, so reporting `activity_retrying` would promise a retry that cannot happen. The `rate_limit_exhausted` **reason code** still fires for a missing bucket (the headline verdict distinguishes permanence; the reason code names *which gate* refuses the row, and that gate is the rate-limit gate either way — omitting it would leave such a task with an empty reason set). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change.** Tests, TDD red→green (RED confirmed as 6 compile errors on the absent field): 6 new pure classifier tests (`missing_rate_limit_bucket_is_a_stall_not_a_refilling_saturation`, `..._outranks_a_saturated_one`, `..._outranks_retry_backoff_and_transient_gates`, `no_worker_still_outranks_a_missing_rate_limit_bucket`, `missing_bucket_without_a_key_cannot_be_reported`, `held_row_ignores_a_missing_rate_limit_bucket`) plus the strengthened DB test `ac2_missing_rate_limit_bucket_is_a_stall_not_a_refilling_saturation` (renamed from `..._is_treated_as_saturated_not_healthy`, whose `activity_rate_limited` assertion encoded exactly the precision compromise Codex flagged; its 'must not be healthy' intent is preserved and strengthened to `health: stalled` + the precise kind + the reason code).
- **Per-execution legal hold** (implemented) — see issue #747. **Before:** an operator could not exempt a single workflow execution's history from the retention janitor (issue #737) or from targeted PII erasure (issue #495). A subpoena/litigation hold on one run required disabling retention globally or racing the janitor. **After:** `POST /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/legal-hold` places a durable, per-execution hold that exempts that execution's `harvest_events` history from retention deletion **and** from PII erasure until it is released (`POST /workflows/{id}/legal-hold/release`) or auto-expires (optional `hold_until`). A held execution is skipped as the *first* per-candidate gate in the retention tick, so `harvest.retention.deleted` never counts a held id; an erase attempt on a held execution returns `409` naming the active hold. Additive nullable columns only (`legal_hold_set_at` / `legal_hold_until` / `legal_hold_reason` / `legal_hold_actor`) on `harvest_workflow_executions` (migration `20260709000001_harvest_legal_hold`), plus a partial discovery index. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact, shard-local.** Active-hold predicate is single-sourced in `legal_hold_active(set_at, until, now)` (re-exported from the crate root), shared by the retention gate, the erase gate, the describe/list surfaces, and the set/release core functions. Idempotent: re-holding an actively-held execution preserves provenance (`newly_held: false`); releasing an unheld execution is a `200` no-op (`released: false`). `GET /workflows/{id}` surfaces a derived `legal_hold` boolean (plus the four raw columns); `GET /workflows?legal_hold=true` filters to actively-held runs. Admin-only, audited under `legal_hold.set` / `legal_hold.release`. CLI: `harvest legal-hold set <id> --reason <r> [--until <rfc3339>]` and `harvest legal-hold release <id>`.
- **Tooling — property-based testing + cargo-fuzz harness bootstrap** (implemented, PR #1004): Bootstrapped a randomized-testing workstream with two complementary layers plus CI wiring — no product-code behavior change. **Property tests** (`proptest`, foundation commit `be8aaa7`): a single external `autumn-harvest/tests/property/` target (mirrors the `tests/integration/` one-`mod.rs`-entry-point convention), bounded to 128 cases by default and overridable upward via proptest's native `PROPTEST_CASES` env knob, with on-disk `failure_persistence` disabled so CI runners stay artifact-free. Pure, non-`db`-gated suites (`policy_props`, `queue_fairness_props`, `task_duration_props`, `completion_trigger_props`, `completion_callback_props`, `event_serde_props`) run under `--no-default-features`; `db`-gated suites (`build_routing_props`, `dlq_props`) are `#[cfg(feature = "db")]` submodules that target **pure functions** in `#[cfg(feature = "db")]` modules and need no live Postgres. Coverage: `policy::compute_retry_delay` (cap/monotonicity/jitter-band), `queue_fairness::weighted_queue_order`/`effective_queue_weights` (permutation, zero-weight-last), `task_duration` (round-trip/sum/totality), `completion_trigger::TriggerCondition::evaluate`/`gate_stored_condition` (totality + gate/evaluate agreement over corrupt stored values), `completion_callback::validate_target_url` (internal IPv4/IPv6 literals never validate even under the permissive policy), `WorkflowEvent` serde round-trip + #521/#488 additive-field back-compat, `build_routing::ramp_bucket`/`validate_ramp_percent` (with the inclusive `0`/`100`/`101` bounds explicitly seeded), `dlq::failure_signature` (**deterministic** — the documented contract, not idempotence, which is false at the cap boundary — plus a guaranteed-oversized-input arm that exercises the `<= SIGNATURE_MAX_LEN` truncation branch); in-crate proptests for non-public targets `worker::nd_block_backoff` (private, db-gated) and `context::remaining_secs_until` (`pub(crate)`). **Fuzz harness** (`cargo-fuzz` / libFuzzer, PR #1004): a new `fuzz/` crate **excluded** from the root workspace (root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace] exclude = ["fuzz"]` + its own empty `[workspace]` table), so the root resolver never builds these nightly/libFuzzer-only binaries — verified via `cargo metadata --no-deps` (`autumn-harvest-fuzz` is not a member) and a clean `cargo build -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features` with `fuzz/` present. Four targets over the functions where raw-bytes coverage-guided fuzzing genuinely beats structured proptest: `fuzz_workflow_event_deser` (`serde_json::from_slice::<WorkflowEvent>` totality — every history read path deserializes this append-only enum), `fuzz_det_check_source` (`det_check::check_source` totality — the highest-value target given the historical parity churn against the proc-macro determinism lint; a hand-rolled line/brace scanner run over user code in CI/editors), `fuzz_validate_target_url` (`completion_callback::validate_target_url` totality under the most-permissive SSRF policy — issue #605 security boundary), `fuzz_failure_signature` (`dlq::failure_signature` totality + `<= SIGNATURE_MAX_LEN`; `db`-gated, so the fuzz crate enables the `db` feature). `fuzz/smoke.sh` runs each target ~15s for local/manual use. In-sandbox `cargo +nightly fuzz build` built all four; each ran ~9s clean (hundreds of thousands of executions, zero crashes). **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): (1) a new **"Run db-gated property suites"** step in the existing `test` job (`cargo test -p autumn-harvest --features db --test property`) — `build_routing_props`/`dlq_props` were previously only *compiled* (never executed) by the `--no-run`/`--lib` db steps; they need no Docker. (2) A new opt-in **`fuzz-smoke`** job gated `workflow_dispatch`-only (never push/PR — Actions minutes are tight and fuzzing needs nightly), 30s per target, plus a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger added to `on:`. (Rebased onto current trunk: the line-186 `if:` YAML indentation fix already landed independently in #988, so this branch adds only the two CI items above and requires no ci.yml re-indent.) **Docs**: `docs/testing/property-and-fuzz.md` — how to run both layers (incl. the db-featured line and `PROPTEST_CASES` deep runs), the target-selection rationale (pure functions / parsers / totality), and a per-subsystem follow-up backlog including the two deferred items **C12** (det_check ↔ macro-guardrail differential — needs a proc-macro test harness since `determinism_lint.rs` isn't an invocable `pub fn`) and **C13** (`WorkflowReplayer`-based replay-determinism property under `--features testing`, reusing the #476 1000-ordering precedent), plus scheduler cron parsing, `resolve_concurrency_key`/`project_json_path`, `throttle::parse_rate`, rendezvous shard-routing stability, and `validate_against_schema`-vs-serde candidates. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change, no replay/determinism impact, no product-code change** — test/tooling/docs/CI only. Local verification: property suites `21 passed` (no-db) / `26 passed` (db), both sub-second; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- **Phase 3.47** (implemented): SSRF guard — block `0.0.0.0/8` and `198.18.0.0/15` callback targets (issue #605 hardening / PR #1004 review notes). Closed two IP-literal SSRF bypasses in the completion-callback URL validator (`completion_callback::validate_target_url` → `is_ipv4_non_routable`), surfaced by the `validate_target_url` internal-IP property/fuzz coverage added in PR #1004. **Before:** the classifier blocked the bare `0.0.0.0` (via `is_unspecified()`) but not the rest of `0.0.0.0/8` ("this host on this network", RFC 1122) — on Linux the whole range routes to localhost, so `http(s)://0.0.0.1/`, `http(s)://0.1.2.3/`, `http(s)://0.255.255.255/` all passed the callback host allowlist. It also missed the entire `198.18.0.0/15` benchmarking range (RFC 2544), so `198.18.0.1` … `198.19.255.255` validated. **After:** both ranges are rejected as `SsrfRejection::IpNotRoutable` (the existing machine-readable code — no new variant), alongside the previously covered loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`), private (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`), link-local (`169.254/16`), CGNAT/shared (`100.64.0.0/10`), unspecified, multicast, documentation, and broadcast ranges. IPv6 v4-mapped forms (`::ffff:0.0.0.1`, `::ffff:198.18.0.1`) inherit the fix through the existing `to_ipv4_mapped()` canonicalization. **Blast radius / call sites that inherit the fix for free** (all four reuse the one pure `validate_target_url`): builder-default callback registration (`try_build`), the per-start HTTP registration route (rejects with `422`), enqueue-time re-validation (defense in depth), and the scanner's fire-time re-validation before each POST. The inbound webhook receiver (`autumn-harvest-plugin`) does **not** reuse this guard — it verifies inbound deliveries via autumn-web's `[security.webhooks]` — so it is unaffected. **Scope:** validator + tests only. No new `SsrfRejection` code, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no API/wire change. TDD red→green: the two new range tests and the v4-mapped test failed against the old classifier (addresses returned `Ok`); the fix makes them pass while the added already-covered-range audit tests and the just-outside-`198.18.0.0/15` neighbor tests (`198.17.255.255`, `198.20.0.0` still pass validation) stay green. Verified with `cargo test -p autumn-harvest {--no-default-features,--features db} ssrf_tests` (33 passed), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings` and `-p autumn-harvest-plugin` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- **Phase 4** (implemented, testing infra): Loom concurrency model checking for the in-process state machines. Bootstraps a [loom](https://github.com/tokio-rs/loom) model-checking workstream that exhaustively explores the thread interleavings of harvest's two genuinely-concurrent, in-process, `Mutex`-guarded data structures — the per-activity circuit breaker (`circuit_breaker.rs`) and the worker session-slot registry (`sessions.rs`). Loom `= "0.7.2"` was already an (unused) dev-dependency; this wires it up. **No production behavior change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — the entire change is test infrastructure plus a `cfg`-gated sync-primitive alias. **Contained `cfg(loom)` shim.** New `src/loom_sync.rs` re-exports `Arc`/`Mutex`/`MutexGuard` — `std::sync` under a normal build (byte-for-byte identical to before), `loom::sync` under `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom"`. Only `circuit_breaker.rs` and `sessions.rs` import from it; the swap is deliberately **not** swept across the crate. Loom's `Mutex::lock()` returns the same `std::sync::LockResult` and never poisons, so the existing `.unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)` call sites compile and behave identically under both configs with no `cfg`-gating of the lock call. `std::time::Instant` is deliberately left as std (loom does not model time; real `Instant`s are passed through). **Models (`tests/loom_models.rs`, `#![cfg(loom)]`-gated so `cargo test` never runs them).** Four models, each two `loom::thread` threads / ≤2 ops, driving the real types: (1) `circuit_breaker_stale_failure_cannot_retrip_a_reset_breaker` (headline) — a generation-stamped `DispatchToken` captured before an operator reset races the `force_close`; the stale retryable failure is fenced under every interleaving (breaker ends CLOSED, empty window), proving the generation fence + `forced_open` guard compose under concurrency; (2) `circuit_breaker_admits_at_most_one_half_open_probe` — two dispatches race for the single half-open probe slot; exactly one is admitted; (3) `session_slot_bound_admits_at_most_one_at_capacity_one` — the capacity bound holds under a concurrent acquire race; (4) `session_slot_acquire_release_balances_and_never_underflows` — concurrent acquire/release drains the registry to empty. **Build wiring.** loom is moved to `[target.'cfg(loom)'.dependencies]` (not `[dev-dependencies]`) because the shim references `loom::sync::*` from the *library* sources (the `SessionSlotRegistry` type alias is production code), and dev-deps are not available to the normal library build the integration test links against. Under a global `--cfg loom`, tokio's `net` module is compiled out (`#![cfg(not(loom))]`), so every `tokio::net` consumer must be kept out of the loom graph: the run uses `--no-default-features` (drops `db`→`tokio-postgres`) and `testcontainers` is gated to `[target.'cfg(not(loom))'.dev-dependencies]` (it pulls `hyper-util`). `cfg(loom)` is registered in `[workspace.lints.rust]` `check-cfg` so `unexpected_cfgs` does not fire under normal `-D warnings` builds. **No interleaving bug found** — all four models pass. Run manually: `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features --test loom_models --release`. **CI.** New `.github/workflows/loom.yml` runs the suite on `workflow_dispatch` **only** — never in the required-status matrix, so zero added cost on normal PR/push runs (respecting #999). **Docs.** `docs/testing/loom.md` (what loom can/can't do, the module include/exclude rationale, an honest coverage caveat that the majority of harvest's concurrency lives in Postgres and is out of loom's reach, run instructions, how to add a model, and model-size/preemption-bound guidance) and `docs/testing/concurrency-model-checking.md` (an honest loom/Shuttle/Turmoil evaluation: loom adopted now; Shuttle recommended fast-follow for the async `slot_tuner.rs` semaphore-accounting invariant loom structurally cannot reach — backlogged rather than shipping a non-running PoC; Turmoil recommended against, since harvest coordinates through Postgres and has no custom peer networking for Turmoil to simulate — verified by repo search — with a recommendation matrix).
- **Continue-as-new run-chain timeline API** (implemented): expose the complete, ordered continue-as-new succession for a workflow, resolvable from **any** member run (head, middle, or latest) in one call — see issue #701. Before this change, an operator holding a workflow's *latest* continue-as-new run had no way to see its predecessors: continue-as-new successors are inserted with `parent_id: None` and carried no backward link, so the sole forward link (the `WorkflowContinuedAsNew` event) could not be walked backward, and there was no single API for the whole chain — reconstructing a succession meant manual database spelunking.
