The private `deadline_fraction_reached()` returns `false` (recording nothing) when there is no timeout, a non-positive budget, or an overflowing deadline, else trips when `remaining <= (1 - fraction) * total` (a deadline already in the past trips). `should_continue_as_new()` combines the two triggers as `by_events || by_deadline` with **both bound before the `||`** — the deadline branch is evaluated unconditionally so a timeout-bearing workflow's recorded side-effect stream is a pure function of "has a deadline" (constant across the run's life) rather than the task-varying event count. **Cross-version replay safety (the tolerant clock read).** `should_continue_as_new()`'s deadline branch does **not** call the strict public `time_until_deadline()`/`system_now()`; it uses an internal **tolerant** clock read, `deadline_clock_read()`, backed by the new three-state `HistoryMatcher::match_side_effect_now_tolerant() -> SideEffectNowMatch` (`Matched{millis}` / `NotRecorded` / `Frontier`, re-exported from `lib.rs`). This closes a cross-version replay hazard two reviewers converged on: an execution recorded under a **pre-#772 binary** carries no `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` at the `should_continue_as_new()` call site, so when it resumes under the new binary the strict `system_now()` would hit whatever real event is recorded at the cursor (a `TimerStarted`/`ActivityScheduled`/`ChildWorkflowStarted` — the canonical `should_continue_as_new()`-then-`ctx.timer()` shape, the shipped example's shape) and record a `SideEffectDrift` non-determinism error → #603 nd-block, wedging a healthy long-lived workflow on a routine upgrade. The tolerant read instead: at the **live frontier** records a fresh `Now` and pushes the `RecordSideEffect` command exactly as `system_now()` does; on a **matching recorded `Now`** consumes it (identical to strict); on **any other recorded event** returns `None` **without consuming the cursor and without diverging**, so `deadline_fraction_reached()` degrades to history-count-only for that run's pre-upgrade recorded portion. It is replay-safe by construction (for a new execution, identical to strict; for an old one, a pure/stable function of the event at the cursor — a non-`Now` event always → `None`), and once the run executes live past its pre-upgrade frontier it records `Now`s normally and picks the deadline feature up. The only "masking" is fail-safe: a genuine control-flow reordering that lands a deadline clock-read on a recorded non-`Now` event degrades to a missed checkpoint *suggestion* rather than nd-blocking — it can never emit a wrong command, and any real divergence still nd-errors at the next real command. The public `system_now()`/`time_until_deadline()` stay **strict** (any direct call is new author code subject to normal versioning rules). `WorkflowHistoryPolicy` gains `continue_as_new_deadline_fraction: f64` (default `DEFAULT_CONTINUE_AS_NEW_DEADLINE_FRACTION = 0.8`, re-exported from `lib.rs`) with a `continue_as_new_deadline_fraction()` accessor and a `with_continue_as_new_deadline_fraction(f64)` setter that **clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]`**. Because `f64` is not `Eq`, the struct's derive dropped from `PartialEq, Eq` to just `PartialEq` (a repo-wide grep confirmed no `Eq`/`HashMap`-key/whole-struct-`assert_eq!` usage — only accessor-level asserts). Builder: `HarvestBuilder::history_continue_as_new_deadline_fraction(f64)`. **Threading**: the effective `execution_timeout: Option<chrono::Duration>` (the same value the execution row carries, so `deadline = start_time + execution_timeout` derives purely from the recorded start) is a new field on `WorkflowContext`, set via the new `with_execution_timeout` builder. It is threaded from `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta` (new `execution_timeout` field, populated by the worker from `prepared.execution.execution_timeout`) into `run_workflow_with_state_history_policy_and_caps` (worker path) and `run_workflow_with_state_advancing_clock` (test-env path), and as a new trailing parameter on `run_workflow_strict` / `run_workflow_strict_advancing_clock` / `run_workflow_canary` (replayer path, which has no span_meta). `WorkflowReplayer::with_execution_timeout(chrono::Duration)` and `WorkflowTestEnv::with_execution_timeout(chrono::Duration)` expose it to the harnesses. **Determinism contract**: a history that crossed the deadline replays to the same `ContinueAsNew` command on every worker, because the deadline is derived from the recorded start time and the clock read reuses the existing `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` event — the frozen-once, replayed-verbatim capture from #384. Proven by the falsifiable `deadline_triggered_can_replays_deterministically_1000x` replayer fixture, which pins the **decision** across 1000 **distinct** fixtures — varied frozen `system_now()` capture and budget, **mixing trip (≥0.85 of budget consumed) and not-yet (≤0.40 consumed) cases**, both well clear of the 0.8 boundary — via a branch probe that schedules `checkpoint_now` when it trips and `keep_working` otherwise: because the recorded activity fixes the expected decision, a **broken fraction comparison schedules the other activity and diverges**, so this bar actually falsifies a wrong decision rather than passing regardless (the earlier completing probe completed identically no matter the decision — a tautology). `replay_deadline_crossed_history_yields_continue_as_new` separately proves the actual `ContinueAsNew` command replays via a single `continue_as_new` fixture. Docs: "Checkpoint before the deadline kills you" note in `docs/getting-started/07-reliability-knobs.md` (next to the SLA/`execution_timeout` material), plus a **call-once-per-decision-cycle** guidance line (each `should_continue_as_new()` records one `Now` when a timeout is set) and a **graceful-rollout** note (old in-flight executions degrade to history-count-only for their pre-upgrade portion and pick the feature up once they run live past their frontier — no "upgrade the fleet first" sequencing). Example `autumn-harvest/examples/long_lived_entity_deadline.rs` (a subscription entity with `#[workflow(execution_timeout = "24h")]` + embedded `WorkflowTestEnv`/`WorkflowReplayer` tests), now run in CI via a dedicated `--example long_lived_entity_deadline` step (its 4 embedded tests previously never ran). **Post-review hardening (P2 — effective `deadline_at`, not a stale start+timeout recompute).** The initial cut derived `ctx.deadline()` purely from `start_time + execution_timeout`, but for a run that has been **paused/resumed (#383) or redriven** the row's hard deadline is no longer that value: `resume_workflow_execution` explicitly pushes `deadline_at` forward by the pause span, and redrive re-anchors it to `now + timeout`. Recomputing from the original start time therefore made the deadline branch of `should_continue_as_new()` see a **stale/past** deadline after a long pause — so a healthy run could continue-as-new immediately even though the timeout scanner honours the shifted `deadline_at`. Fixed by threading the **authoritative absolute `deadline_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`** from the execution row into `WorkflowContext` (new field + `with_deadline(...)` builder, mirroring `with_execution_timeout`; new `deadline_at` field on `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta`, populated by the worker from `prepared.execution.deadline_at` and threaded into both real `run_workflow_*` construction sites). *(The next paragraph refines what `deadline()` itself returns: this round briefly made the **public** `deadline()` return the shifted value; the split below reverts that so the public accessor stays replay-stable nominal while only the internal budget check reads the shifted value.)* **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs` change.** **Post-review hardening, round 2 (P2 split — replay-stable public deadline + live internal continue-as-new budget).** Codex flagged that round 1 overcorrected: reading the LIVE mutable `deadline_at` from the **public** `ctx.deadline()`/`time_until_deadline()` accessors is not replay-safe — a run that is paused/resumed or redriven has `deadline_at` mutated by `execution.rs`, so replaying earlier history after the shift would see a different `deadline()` than the value seen when those earlier commands were recorded, and workflow code that branched on `ctx.deadline()` (or embedded it in an activity/child input) could take a different branch or fail strict input checks even though the code did not change. Fixed with a deliberate **split**: (a) the PUBLIC `ctx.deadline()`/`time_until_deadline()` now return the replay-STABLE **nominal** deadline `start_time + execution_timeout` — `start_time` is fixed in `WorkflowStarted` and `execution_timeout` is a fixed row value that pause does **not** mutate (pause shifts `deadline_at`, never `execution_timeout`), so the nominal deadline is identical on every replay cycle and every worker (no new recorded event — the append-only/AC6 contract is intact); (b) the INTERNAL `should_continue_as_new()` deadline branch reads a new private `effective_deadline_live()` (the pause/resume/redrive-shifted `deadline_at`, falling back to `start_time + execution_timeout`), so the continue-as-new budget matches the deadline the timeout scanner actually enforces and a healthy long-paused run does **not** spuriously checkpoint the moment it resumes. The internal live read is replay-safe by construction: pause/redrive only move `deadline_at` **forward**, and the documented contract is that `should_continue_as_new() == true` ⇒ the workflow calls `continue_as_new` (CONTINUED_AS_NEW terminates the run, so no later replay re-evaluates the branch), while a live `false` recomputed on any later replay is evaluated against an equal-or-larger deadline (a smaller consumed fraction) and stays `false`. The recorded `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` clock read matches via the frozen side-effect regardless. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs` change.** Pinned by `context.rs` unit tests `deadline_public_accessor_is_nominal_not_shifted_deadline_at` (a +120s resume shift → public `deadline()` returns the nominal value, **not** the shifted `deadline_at`) and `should_continue_as_new_uses_live_effective_deadline_not_nominal` (nominal budget fully consumed / in the past, but the shifted `deadline_at` is far in the future ⇒ the internal check does NOT trip — the still-open original P2 "no premature CAN after a long pause"; a control run with no threaded `deadline_at` DOES trip, proving the live read is what makes the difference), both red→green-verified against 4f32bd4; and by the DB e2e `worker_surfaces_nominal_deadline_not_shifted_deadline_at` (`tests/integration/integration_e2e.rs`), which starts a run with `execution_timeout = 30m`, directly shifts the row's `deadline_at` +2h (exactly what resume's SQL does), runs a real worker, and asserts the echoed public `ctx.deadline()` equals the NOMINAL start+timeout and is far from the shifted `deadline_at` — compile-checked in this sandbox (Docker/testcontainers unavailable), run Docker-backed in CI's integration step. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (P2 — DB replay threads per-row `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at`).** Codex flagged that `WorkflowReplayer::replay_from_db` and the replay canary (`run_canary`) loaded only the workflow name/headers and reused the replayer-wide `self.execution_timeout` (usually `None`, and never the row's shifted `deadline_at`), so replaying a row whose deadline branch had recorded a `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` would leave that `Now` unmatched → **false non-determinism**. **Blast radius**: in this codebase the "replay canary" (`run_canary`, reached only via the admin `POST /admin/workflows/replay-canary` handler) is an **advisory, read-only deploy-verify** endpoint — it returns a verdict + audit row and does NOT nd-block, redrive, or mutate real executions (the production worker path is separate and already threads `deadline_at`). So the finding here only meant a false-negative deploy verdict for a deadline-aware-CAN workflow, not a wedged live run — but per-row threading is still correct and cheap. Fixed by loading each replayed execution row's own `execution_timeout` and live `deadline_at` (via the extended `load_workflow_name_and_headers` → `DbReplayMeta` for `replay_from_db`, and the extended `query_running_executions` → `SampledExecution` for `run_canary`) and threading them into that execution's `WorkflowContext` through new private `replay_from_snapshot_effective`/`replay_canary_snapshot_effective` methods (the public `replay_from_snapshot`/`replay_canary_snapshot`/`replay_from_events` still delegate with the global `execution_timeout` and no live `deadline_at` — a documented limitation of the file/JSON path, since a raw snapshot carries neither). The executor's `run_workflow_strict`/`run_workflow_strict_advancing_clock`/`run_workflow_canary` gained a trailing `deadline_at` parameter. Pinned by the DB integration test `replay_from_db_threads_per_row_execution_timeout_for_deadline_branch` (`tests/integration/replayer_integration_tests.rs`): a row with `execution_timeout = 30m` + a shifted `deadline_at` whose history recorded the deadline branch's `Now` replays `ReplaySucceeded` via `replay_from_db`, while replaying the SAME events with no per-row timeout threaded (the pre-fix global-option path) diverges on the unmatched `Now` — **executed green against a real local Postgres 16** in this sandbox (Docker/testcontainers unavailable; the equivalent test logic run directly against a local PG instance, then discarded), and run Docker-backed in CI's integration step. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed as `SideEffectDrift` nd-block / assertion failure against the strict pre-fix path, then green): `context.rs` unit tests — the original 8 (`deadline` with/without timeout, `time_until_deadline` recorded-clock / none-without-deadline + zero-side-effect, deadline-fraction trips / not-yet, no-timeout-records-nothing, event-count trigger preserved) plus **Finding-1** `deadline_read_tolerates_non_now_cursor_event_no_divergence_no_command` (pre-#772 cursor event → no trip, no command, **no deferred nd error**) and `deadline_read_records_live_at_frontier`; **Finding-3** `default_fraction_does_not_trip_at_0_6_consumed` + `configured_fraction_shifts_the_boundary` (a 0.5 fraction trips the same 0.6-consumed history the 0.8 default does not — pins the default's effect *and* catches a silent default change); **Finding-4** edge cases `deadline_in_the_past_still_trips`, `fraction_clamp_endpoints_behave` (0.0 trips on any consumption; 1.0 only at/past the deadline), `deadline_overflow_returns_none_and_does_not_trip`, `deadline_reanchors_for_continue_as_new_successor`; the policy default/clamp test; a `builder.rs` fraction-override test; 4 `replay.rs` matcher unit tests for `match_side_effect_now_tolerant` (matches recorded `Now`, `NotRecorded` (leaves cursor) for a non-`Now` event and for a different `SideEffectKind`, `Frontier` past end); the two replayer fixtures above plus **Finding-1** `should_continue_as_new_tolerates_pre_772_history_without_nd_block` (a pre-#772 fired-timer history replays `ReplaySucceeded` under the deadline-aware binary — the exact divergence the fix eliminates); and the 4 example tests. All no-DB and run in the existing `--no-default-features --features testing --test integration` CI step and the new `--example` step. **Finding-2 DB e2e** `worker_threads_execution_timeout_into_ctx_deadline` (`tests/integration/integration_e2e.rs`) proves the production worker→executor→context threading end-to-end: a start with `execution_timeout = 30m` runs a real worker; the workflow returns `ctx.deadline()`, asserted to equal `WorkflowStarted.timestamp + execution_timeout` exactly (cross-checked within µs against the row's `deadline_at`) — a `None` output would mean the timeout was never threaded. Compile-checked in this sandbox and **executed green against a real local Postgres 16** (Docker/testcontainers unavailable; run via a temporary local-URL point, since integration_e2e uses testcontainers), and run Docker-backed in CI's existing integration step. **Post-review hardening, round 4 (P2 — name the deadline-probe clock read so migration never consumes a user `Now`).** Codex flagged that the tolerant deadline read (round-1 fix above) matched *any* `SideEffectRecorded { kind: Now, name: None }` at the cursor as its own read — but that is exactly the shape `ctx.system_now()`/`ctx.sleep_until()` record. When a pre-#772 history has `should_continue_as_new()` (deadline branch, `execution_timeout` set) sitting **immediately before** a user `ctx.system_now()` call, the pre-upgrade history carries no probe `Now` but *does* carry the author's own `Now` at the cursor. The tolerant matcher stole that user `Now`, advanced the cursor, and the subsequent `ctx.system_now()` then replayed against the following event (e.g. `TimerStarted`/`ActivityScheduled`) and reported false non-determinism (`SideEffectDrift`) on the upgrade — a genuine migration-path bug, not a live-run wedge for the strict path but a false nd-block for exactly the "check-then-`system_now()`" shape. Fixed by making the probe's clock read **self-identifying** via a reserved side-effect name: the deadline branch now records/matches its `Now` as `SideEffectRecorded { kind: Now, name: Some(DEADLINE_PROBE_SIDE_EFFECT_NAME) }` (`"__harvest_deadline_probe"`, a new `pub const` re-exported from `lib.rs`, following the `__harvest_*` / `__signal_timeout:` reserved-name convention). `HistoryMatcher::match_side_effect_now_tolerant` now resolves to `Matched` **only** for the probe's sentinel-named `Now`; a bare user `{Now, name: None}`, a differently-named `Now`, or any non-`Now` event all resolve to `NotRecorded` with the cursor **untouched**, so a pre-#772 history's user `Now` is left for the workflow's own strict `system_now()` read to consume. The two paths compose cleanly because the existing side-effect matcher is already `(kind, name)`-keyed: the strict `system_now()` matcher matches `{Now, name: None}` and never the probe's sentinel-named `Now`, and vice versa. This **strictly improves** the round-1 tolerant read — a pre-#772 history (no probe event at all) still degrades the deadline branch to history-count-only for its recorded portion, and now additionally never steals a user `Now`. Because the feature is unmerged, no production #772 histories exist, so changing the probe's recorded `name` from `None` to the sentinel is safe; the test fixtures on this branch that hard-coded a name-`None` probe `Now` were updated. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs`/`SideEffectKind` change** (the `name` field of the existing `SideEffectRecorded` variant carries the sentinel; the enum shape is untouched). Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed as `NonDeterminismDetected(kind=SideEffectDrift, event_index=2)` against 763b42cc, then green): the scenario replayer test `deadline_probe_does_not_consume_a_user_system_now` (`tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`) — a `should_continue_as_new()`-then-`ctx.system_now()`-then-`ctx.timer()` workflow replays a pre-#772 history `[WorkflowStarted, {Now, name: None}(user), TimerStarted, TimerFired]` as `ReplaySucceeded`; the forward case (a `#772` history with a sentinel-named probe `Now` followed by a user `{Now, name: None}` — the existing `deadline_probe_history`/`recorded_now` fixtures, updated to record the sentinel name) still matches both `Now`s in order; the pre-existing tolerant-read regression `should_continue_as_new_tolerates_pre_772_history_without_nd_block` (no probe `Now`, `TimerStarted` at the cursor) stays green; plus `replay.rs` matcher unit tests `match_side_effect_now_tolerant_matches_recorded_probe_now`, `..._does_not_consume_a_user_now`, `..._does_not_consume_a_differently_named_now`, and `context.rs` `deadline_read_records_live_at_frontier` (now asserts the sentinel-named command). All no-DB and run in the existing `--no-default-features --features testing --test integration` and `--example long_lived_entity_deadline` CI steps; the DB-gated `persist_deadline_probe_history` (`replayer_integration_tests.rs`) probe fixture was likewise updated to the sentinel name (compile-checked here, run Docker-backed in CI). **Post-review hardening, round 5 (P2 — `TestRunOutcome::replay_check` carries the test env's `execution_timeout`).** Codex flagged that `WorkflowTestEnv::with_execution_timeout` fed only the LIVE run: the returned `TestRunOutcome` did not retain the timeout, so `TestRunOutcome::replay_check()` built its `WorkflowReplayer` with `execution_timeout: None`. Any history a deadline-aware workflow produced under a test env with a timeout carries the round-4 sentinel `SideEffectRecorded{Now, name: "__harvest_deadline_probe"}` (recorded by `should_continue_as_new()`'s deadline branch — even for a far-future deadline, since the clock is read before the fraction is compared), but `replay_check` disabled the deadline branch and left that probe **unconsumed** → a FALSE non-determinism report (`NonDeterminismDetected(TimerMismatch, ...)` for the canonical check-then-`ctx.timer()` shape) for an otherwise valid deadline-aware test history. Fixed by carrying the effective `execution_timeout: Option<chrono::Duration>` from `WorkflowTestEnv` into `TestRunOutcome` (a new field, threaded through all four `TestRunOutcome { .. }` construction sites in `run`/`finish_terminal_outcome`) and re-applying it in `replay_check()` (`replayer = replayer.with_execution_timeout(execution_timeout)` when `Some`, mirroring how the live run threads the same value through `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta`). The `WorkflowTestEnv` carries **only** the timeout — it has no absolute `deadline`/`with_deadline` field (its `span_meta` sets `deadline_at: None`, so `ctx.deadline()` falls back to `start + execution_timeout`), so there is nothing else to carry; a `None` timeout leaves the replayer's deadline branch off, matching the live run byte-for-byte. This is purely the test harness carrying a value it already has — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs`/`SideEffectKind` change, no production code change**. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed as `NonDeterminismDetected(kind=TimerMismatch, event_index=1, expected="TimerStarted(cycle)", actual="SideEffectRecorded(now:__harvest_deadline_probe)")` against 0faecc88, then green): `deadline_aware_run_replay_check_carries_execution_timeout` (`tests/integration/workflow_test_env_tests.rs`) runs a deadline-aware workflow (`should_continue_as_new()` then `ctx.timer(...)`) through `WorkflowTestEnv::with_execution_timeout(24h)`, asserts the live run recorded the sentinel deadline probe, and asserts `outcome.replay_check(...)` reports `ReplaySucceeded`. Runs no-DB in the existing `--no-default-features --features testing --test integration` CI step. **Post-review hardening, round 6 (P2 — thread the execution deadline into ALL remaining replay contexts: query + terminal-query).** Codex flagged that the query hydration paths still built their replay `WorkflowContext` **without** `.with_execution_timeout()` / `.with_deadline()`. A workflow with an `execution_timeout` records the reserved `SideEffectRecorded { kind: Now, name: "__harvest_deadline_probe" }` sentinel on every `should_continue_as_new()` call; a query replay context that does not thread the row's `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` returns from the deadline guard **before** `deadline_clock_read()`, so the recorded probe stays **unconsumed** at the cursor — the next replayed command (running / in-process query) or the terminal-query drift check (`has_unconsumed_history` → spurious `410`) then treats an otherwise valid history as divergent. Rather than fix one more path and get flagged again, **every remaining replay-context construction site was audited in one pass** and the two production sites that load the execution row and were still un-threaded were fixed: (1) `WorkflowHandle::execute_query_in_process` (`handle.rs`, the in-process typed-client query path) and (2) `hydrate_ctx_for_query` (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, the HTTP query API path — covers `POST/GET /workflows/{id}/query/{name}`, `GET /workflows/{id}/queries`, `/history` replay, and the terminal-query drive/drift classification). Both now append `.with_execution_timeout(execution.execution_timeout).with_deadline(execution.deadline_at)` — mirroring the worker/replayer paths (`executor.rs`) already fixed in rounds 2–5. **Audit result** (grep for `for_replay*`, `with_execution_timeout`, `with_deadline`, `hydrate_ctx_for_query`, `execute_query_in_process`, `drive_query_replay`, `run_workflow*`, `WorkflowReplayer::` across both crates): the only production replay-context sites are `executor.rs` (worker/strict/canary — already threaded from `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta`), `handle.rs:execute_query_in_process`, and `api.rs:hydrate_ctx_for_query`; the last two are this round's fix. `reset.rs` builds no replay context (pure DB manipulation, no workflow-code execution). Every other `for_replay*` call site is a `#[cfg(test)]` fixture with no execution row (pure histories, no deadline probe possible) and the JSON/events `WorkflowReplayer` fixture path keeps its global `with_execution_timeout` option (a documented limitation of the file/JSON path — a raw snapshot carries no row `deadline_at`). So after this round **no replay path leaves the deadline probe unconsumed**. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs`/`SideEffectKind` change** — the threading reuses the existing `with_execution_timeout`/`with_deadline` builders and the existing `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` sentinel. Tests, TDD red→green: **pure** (no-DB) mechanism tests in `tests/integration/query_terminal_tests.rs` — `deadline_probe_history_replays_and_serves_when_budget_is_threaded` (a terminal history carrying the probe drives to `Poll::Ready` and `Serve`s the reconstructed count when the budget is threaded, exactly as the fixed hydration sites do) and `deadline_probe_history_diverges_when_budget_is_not_threaded` (the same history with **no** budget threaded leaves the probe unconsumed and does **not** `Serve` — pinning why threading is required); **DB-backed HTTP** tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/query_integration.rs` — `deadline_probe_running_query_serves_reconstructed_state` and `deadline_probe_terminal_query_serves_not_gone` (a RUNNING and a COMPLETED execution whose seeded history carries the probe, plus `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` on the row, are queried over the real `hydrate_ctx_for_query` HTTP path and must serve `200` with the correct count — pre-fix they returned non-`200` (a `500` divergence / spurious `410`), red→green-verified against ae13a763 on a real local Postgres 16 in this sandbox, run Docker-backed in CI). The two DB tests register a new `deadline_probe_wf` (`execution_timeout = 24h`, calls `should_continue_as_new()` before processing items). **Post-review hardening, round 7 (three P2s — thread the execution deadline into the LAST remaining paths: JSON/export replay, update handlers, and the test-env virtual clock).** A final review pass found three more sites where the deadline budget (`execution_timeout`/`deadline_at`) was not threaded, each leaving the reserved `SideEffectRecorded{Now, name: "__harvest_deadline_probe"}` probe unconsumed (a false non-determinism) or the deadline branch silently disabled. All three fixed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs`/`SideEffectKind` change** — the fixes reuse the existing `with_execution_timeout`/`with_deadline` builders, the existing `SideEffectRecorded{Now}` sentinel, and the existing advancing virtual clock. **(1) Carry deadline metadata in JSON replays / history exports (`testing.rs` + `history_export.rs` + plugin `api.rs`).** The advertised replay-compatible JSON / `harvest-replay` path (`WorkflowReplayer::replay_from_json` → `replay_from_snapshot`) supplied only the replayer's process-wide `with_execution_timeout` (normally `None`) and no `deadline_at`, and neither `testing::HistorySnapshot` nor the full-history-export envelope (`history_export::HistoryExportDocument`) carried those row values — so an exported deadline-aware history replayed with the deadline branch disabled, leaving the recorded probe unconsumed and false-reporting non-determinism. Fixed by adding two **additive** fields — `execution_timeout: Option<chrono::Duration>` (serialised as top-level integer milliseconds via a new shared `history_export::opt_duration_millis` serde adapter, since `chrono::Duration` has no serde impl) and `deadline_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>` — to **both** `HistorySnapshot` and `HistoryExportDocument` (both `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, backward-compatible: a legacy JSON without the fields deserialises to `None`). Because the export envelope serialises them at the same top-level names, an exported history round-trips into a `HistorySnapshot` verbatim. `replay_from_snapshot`/`replay_canary_snapshot` now **prefer the per-snapshot values** (`snapshot.execution_timeout.or(self.execution_timeout)`, `snapshot.deadline_at`), falling back to the replayer's global option for a legacy snapshot — so `replay_from_json` and the CLI `--workflow` override path both thread the deadline automatically. The metadata is populated on capture from the execution row: `HistoryExportRequest` gains the two fields, and the single-execution export handler (`export_history_for_execution` in plugin `api.rs`) fills them from `execution.execution_timeout`/`execution.deadline_at`. It is **non-payload operational metadata — never redacted** (carried verbatim under both `Full` and `Redacted` policy). *(The two `HistoryExportDocument` producers this round left populating `None` — the batch export candidate query and the retention archival snapshot — are closed in round 8 below; those were real bugs, not "documented" behavior.)* Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed as a `NonDeterminismDetected` false report against the pre-fix `replay_from_snapshot`): `json_replay_threads_snapshot_execution_timeout_for_deadline_history` (the money test — a deadline-crossed history whose `execution_timeout` lives ONLY on the JSON snapshot, no replayer global, replays `ReplaySucceeded` via `replay_from_json`) and `json_replay_legacy_snapshot_without_fields_falls_back_to_global_timeout` (backward compat — a legacy snapshot with the fields omitted deserialises and replays via the global fallback) in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`; `full_export_carries_deadline_metadata_round_tripping_into_a_snapshot` (`history_export.rs`, no-DB — a full export serialises `execution_timeout` as top-level `1800000` millis and deserialises back into a `HistorySnapshot` carrying both fields verbatim); the existing `history_export_integration` DB suite (plugin) stays green (the change is additive), executed green Docker-backed against local PG16 in this sandbox. **(2) Propagate deadlines into declarative update-handler contexts (`context.rs`).** `register_declarative_update_handler` builds each handler's context via `new_for_handler`, which initialised `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to `None` and never copied them from the parent — so `ctx.deadline()`/`time_until_deadline()` inside a declarative `#[update]` handler always returned `None` for a running workflow that has an `execution_timeout` (the workflow body and query handlers already saw them; update handlers were the missed path). Fixed by inheriting the parent's `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` in both the registration path and the `invoke_update` declarative-fallback path (mirroring how `workflow_id`/`workflow_name`/`context_headers` are already threaded). Tests, TDD red→green: `update_handler_inherits_parent_deadline` (a handler on a workflow with `execution_timeout` observes `ctx.deadline() == Some(..)`) and `update_handler_inherits_parent_shifted_deadline_at` (`context.rs` unit tests). **(3) Use the advancing virtual clock for deadline probes under the test harness (`context.rs`).** In a live `WorkflowTestEnv::with_execution_timeout` run that advances time via durable timers (`run_workflow_with_state_advancing_clock`), the deadline probe's frontier read used the host `Utc::now()` instead of the context's advancing/virtual clock — so a workflow that sleeps past its deadline fraction via durable timers then calls `should_continue_as_new()` saw ~zero consumed budget in tests and never tripped the deadline branch, leaving the test-env timeout support unable to validate the long-lived low-event workflows the feature targets. Fixed by a new private `deadline_frontier_now_millis()` helper: in the test harness (advancing clock enabled) it reads the ADVANCING clock (`start_time + elapsed`, mirroring `ctx.now()`); the virtual-clock arm is `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))]`, so **production builds are byte-for-byte unchanged** (`Utc::now()`) — the `system_now()` #384 host-wall-clock contract is untouched, this internal probe is the only reader that consults the virtual clock. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed as the branch NOT tripping when it should): `deadline_probe_reads_advancing_clock_and_trips_in_test_env` (advancing 90s of a 100s budget past the 0.8 fraction trips `should_continue_as_new()` in the test env) and the control `deadline_probe_does_not_trip_below_fraction_in_test_env` (10s of 100s does not trip — stable across the fix, guards against an always-true regression) in `tests/integration/workflow_test_env_tests.rs`. **Post-review hardening, round 8 (two P2s — thread the execution deadline into the last two `HistoryExportDocument` producers: batch history exports and retention archives).** Round 7 item (1) added `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to `HistoryExportDocument`/`HistoryExportRequest` and populated them on the single-execution export, but deliberately left the other two producers writing `None`. Codex correctly flagged both as real bugs (a deadline-aware history exported/archived through those paths replays with the deadline branch disabled → the recorded `SideEffectRecorded{Now, name: "__harvest_deadline_probe"}` probe is left unconsumed → false non-determinism; and for the archive, after the row is deleted there is no source left to recover the values from). A comprehensive sweep of **every** producer and consumer of `HistoryExportDocument`/`HistorySnapshot`/replay-context construction across both crates confirmed these two were the only remaining un-threaded paths; both are now fixed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `event.rs`/`SideEffectKind` change** — the fixes only add two already-existing columns to a read query + struct and populate two already-existing request fields. **(A) Retention archive (`retention.rs`, Codex Finding A).** The retention janitor writes the LAST cold-storage copy (`export_history` → `HistoryExportDocument`) immediately before permanently deleting a terminal execution row, and it hardcoded `execution_timeout: None, deadline_at: None` on the archive request with the (now-corrected) rationale that deadline metadata is "irrelevant for a finished execution" — but a completed/continued run can carry a recorded deadline probe before its next command or terminal event, so replaying the archive later with no deadline strands that probe unconsumed, and after deletion there is no row to recover from. Fixed by adding `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to the `db`-gated `CandidateExecution` `QueryableByName` struct (`Nullable<Interval>` → `Option<chrono::Duration>`, `Nullable<Timestamptz>` → `Option<DateTime<Utc>>`), SELECTing both columns in both candidate-query string variants (the WHERE-clause bind numbering is untouched — the SELECT column list is independent of it), and populating `req.execution_timeout = candidate.execution_timeout` / `req.deadline_at = candidate.deadline_at`. **(B) Batch history export (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, Codex Finding B).** `GET /admin/history/exports` builds each candidate's document via `export_history_for_candidate`, which hardcoded `execution_timeout: None, deadline_at: None` because `HistoryExportCandidate`/`HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL` did not select those columns — so every batch export dropped the deadline budget even though the single-execution export already carried it. Fixed by adding `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to the `HistoryExportCandidate` `QueryableByName` struct, SELECTing `w.execution_timeout`/`w.deadline_at` (and adding them to the `GROUP BY`, harmless since they are functionally dependent on the grouped PK `w.id`) in `HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL`, and populating `execution_timeout: candidate.execution_timeout` / `deadline_at: candidate.deadline_at` in `export_history_for_candidate`. **Comprehensive closure of the deadline-threading theme.** With rounds 6–8 the entire producer/consumer surface is threaded; the theme is closed. - **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission gate authoritative across all workflow-start producers — see issue #618. **Make the admission gate authoritative across all workflow-start producers** (implemented) — see issue #618. The admission gate (#377) lets an incident operator halt new workflow starts fleet-wide or by name/queue/shard/owner while in-flight work drains, but it was **not** authoritative: three in-process producers started workflows without consulting it. It is now either gated or **explicitly, observably exempt** on every in-process producer. New bounded `admission_gate::StartProducer` enum (`Api`/`BatchStart`/`CompletionTrigger`/`WebhookDelegate`/`Scheduler`/`Debounce`/`Throttle`/`Outbox`, `as_str()` + `ALL`) plus the discoverable `producer_contract()` (`ProducerContractEntry { producer, status: ProducerGateStatus::{Gated, ExemptByDesign}, rationale }`). **Completion triggers (AC1) — the main gap, now closed:** `completion_trigger::evaluate_triggers_for_execution` reaches the shared `AdmissionGateCache` through a new process-global `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` static (mirroring `GLOBAL_WORKFLOW_METADATA`/`GLOBAL_CALLBACK_CONFIG`), published by the plugin at boot with the **same `Arc`** the management API and background refresh loop use — so no cache is threaded through the ~17 call sites and gate creates/lifts propagate automatically. The gate is checked **inside the source workflow's terminal-commit transaction**, before the fires-row insert, evaluating every scope (routing + owner resolved up-front). A block is a **clean skip that never rolls back the source terminal** (mirroring the #810 `condition_unmet` resolved-skip shape): it records `record_admission_blocked` (the *same* `AdmissionBlocked` outcome a direct API start records) and writes an exactly-once resolved-skip row in `harvest_completion_trigger_fires` with the new `outcome = 'admission_blocked'` through the existing `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` PK path, so cascade re-entry dedupes it and this terminal never retries the start. A blocked completion-trigger start is therefore **dropped, not deferred** — identically to a direct API start being refused during an incident. When no gate cache is installed (standalone integrations, or the plugin's brief boot window) the check is skipped and behaviour is **byte-identical to pre-#618** (no extra DB read on the no-gate path). **Webhook delegate (AC2):** the inbound webhook receiver (#344) delegates `Starts`/`SignalsWithStart` straight to `api::start_workflow`/`signal_with_start_workflow`, which already check the gate — so a scoped gate blocks a matching webhook-triggered start and lets a non-matching one through, by construction. **Outbox relay (AC3) — exempt-by-design + observable:** `outbox::dispatch_workflow_start_request` relays workflow-start requests durably committed *before* any gate was raised; gating them would drop already-accepted in-flight work (the opposite of the gate contract, "halt **new** starts while in-flight work drains"). It is left un-gated but now increments the new `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer="outbox"}` counter on every relayed start so the exemption is never silent. **New metric (AC4)** via the standard 3-touchpoint recipe: `METRIC_ADMISSION_BYPASSED = "harvest.admission.bypassed"` + `METRIC_LABEL_PRODUCER = "producer"` (telemetry.rs), a no-op-default `MetricsRecorder::record_admission_bypassed(producer)` trait method, and the `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge (`execution.id` is never a label, ADR-0001 §7). **Discoverable contract (AC5):** `GET /admin/gates` now returns a `producers` block alongside `gates` listing each producer's `gated`/`exempt_by_design` status and rationale, so the contract is discoverable without reading source; documented in `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md` and `docs/api-contract.json`. **Known-gaps note removed (AC6):** the stale "Known gaps — ungated workflow producers" comment in `src/admission_gate.rs` is replaced by a "Start-producer contract" section since all three gaps are resolved. Scheduler already gated (`scheduler.rs` `check_admission`); debounce/throttle are gated at admission time on the HTTP start route (their scanners only relay already-admitted work), so they are classified `gated` in the contract. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no change to event JSON tagging, NO migration, no `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path change (AC7)** — the `admission_blocked` outcome reuses the existing nullable `harvest_completion_trigger_fires.outcome TEXT` column from #810; the gate cache is an in-process static; the whole change is start-path policy resolution + telemetry + a read-only API field. **Success metric:** with a `Fleet` gate raised, 100% of workflow-start attempts across the in-process producers this PR touches (API start, completion trigger, outbox) are either blocked-and-counted or bypassed-and-counted — measured by the `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` integration test, which drives all three with a gate active, asserts exactly one target execution (the exempt outbox one) is created, and asserts every start attempt landed in either the blocked or the bypassed counter (zero un-counted admissions), verified against a shared `CapturingMetrics` recorder. **Tests, TDD red→green:** core unit tests in `admission_gate.rs` (`StartProducer::as_str` bounded/unique, `producer_contract` covers every producer + outbox exempt, `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` set/get shared-Arc round-trip), `telemetry.rs` (constant name + no-op default), `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` (bridge does-not-panic); core DB integration `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/admission_gate_authoritative_tests.rs` (Fleet gate blocks a completion-trigger start with the block counted + `admission_blocked` fires row + source terminal not rolled back; no-gate-cache backward compat starts the target with a NULL-outcome fire; scoped `WorkflowName` gate match blocks / miss proceeds); plugin HTTP+outbox integration `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/admission_gate_authoritative_localpg.rs` (`GET /admin/gates` producer contract; outbox relay exempt + bypass counted under a live Fleet gate; scoped gate blocks/passes the start route the webhook delegate forwards to; the zero-un-counted-admissions success-metric test). **All DB/HTTP tests were actually executed against a real local Postgres 16** (the core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite via `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite over the real axum router + real outbox relay), not merely compile-checked. Out of scope (per issue): new gate scopes/matching semantics, gating starts from outside the plugin process, auto-lifting/scheduling gates, rate-limited recovery replay. **Post-review hardening (four-reviewer pass, all fixed TDD-style):** (F1) the four deferred-fire producers that could relay a start past a gate raised *after* admission are now exempt-with-bypass-counter, mirroring the outbox: `debounce`/`throttle`/`event_batch` scanner fires and the completion-trigger **cross-shard** relay (`enforce_completion_triggers_outbox`, now threaded a `metrics` recorder from `enforce_timeouts_once`) each increment `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer=…}` with a distinct label. (F2) `StartProducer` gains `EventBatch` + `CompletionTriggerOutbox` variants (now 10), and `ProducerGateStatus` gains a `GatedAtAdmission` variant so the contract distinguishes the deferred-fire producers' split behaviour (gated at HTTP admission; scanner fire exempt-with-counter) from a flat `gated`. (F3) `AdmissionGateCache::check()`'s fail-closed sentinel (`Uuid::nil()`, now single-sourced via `admission_gate::sentinel_gate_id()`) no longer permanently drops a completion-trigger start on a transient gate-DB blip: the completion-trigger path distinguishes the sentinel from a real operator gate and **proceeds** (no block, no fires row, no count) rather than dropping already-committed in-flight continuation; a real gate still blocks + drops + counts. (F4) the `admission_blocked` block is counted exactly once — the fires-row `inserted` count now gates the `record_admission_blocked` call, and cascade re-entry records a `deduped` outcome instead of a second block. (F5) `set_global_admission_gate_cache` warns on a divergent re-publish, and `stop_harvest_runtime` clears the global (ptr-eq guarded so a stopping plugin never clobbers a live sibling's cache). (F9) the target queue is resolved at most once on the gate-present completion-trigger path. (F10) the global-cache accessor/setter recover a poisoned lock (`into_inner`) rather than failing to `None`. (F11) the global cache is published *before* `HarvestRunner::start` spawns the workers/scanners (safe now that F3 makes a boot-window fail-closed sentinel proceed). (F12) the event-batch HTTP gate pre-check's bounded TOCTOU window is documented (it shares the debounce path's non-atomic check-then-admit shape); a start that slips it is durably deferred and its scanner fire is counted as a bypass, so no un-counted admission results. (F13) the module docs and `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md` gain an explicit **out-of-scope — in-flight continuation** section (workflow-level retry #523, continue-as-new, child/detached-child spawn, reset forks, in-process client handle), and the ops doc is linked from `docs/runbooks/contain-runaway-execution.md` and `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`. **Deferred (noted, not fixed):** a completion-trigger evaluation on the cancel/terminate path passes `metrics: None`, so a block there is gated-but-uncounted (pre-existing `None`-passing pattern; correctness unaffected). **F6:** the `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` success-metric test now drives all seven in-process producers (API + completion-trigger blocked-and-counted; outbox + CT cross-shard relay + debounce + throttle + event-batch bypassed-and-counted) under a live Fleet gate and asserts zero un-counted admissions; the plugin local-PG suite is dual-mode (`HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` preferred, testcontainers fallback) and runs Docker-backed in CI. New core DB tests cover the F3 sentinel-proceeds and F4 no-double-count paths. All DB/HTTP suites executed against a real local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (two Codex findings on commit `956178c`):** (F1, P1 — `plugin.rs` boot ordering) the F11 change published the gate-cache `Arc` to the process-global static *before* `HarvestRunner::start` spawned the workers/scanners, but the boot-time `load_active_gates` that populates the snapshot ran **after** the runner started — so a scanner tick or completion trigger firing in the startup window ran `check_cached()` against an EMPTY snapshot and PROCEEDED, bypassing persisted Fleet/queue/name gates uncounted at boot. Fixed by reordering `start_harvest_runtime`: the boot-time `load_active_gates` → `refresh` now runs on `harvest_pool` **before** it is moved into `runner_resources` — i.e. before the cache is published to the global and before the runner spawns — so the published `Arc` (and the one workers see) already carries the persisted gates. A genuine gate-DB outage at boot is unchanged: the snapshot stays empty and completion triggers proceed (the same bounded caveat as a mid-run fail-closed with no cached match), never converted into a permanent block-drop; the direct HTTP start path still fails closed via `check()`. (F2, P2 — `completion_trigger.rs` cross-shard queue resolution) for a cross-shard trigger (target hashing to a shard other than the source's, no explicit trigger queue), the inline gate check called `resolve_target_queue(conn, …)` on the SOURCE transaction connection — which for a `target_shard == 0` target queries the source shard's `harvest_schedules`, missing the target's schedule and falling back to the default queue, so a `Queue(q)` gate scoped to the real target queue was MISSED (and the outbox relay, which resolves the real queue on the target connection at fire time, is exempt-with-counter, so nothing downstream caught it). Fixed with the new `pub` `completion_trigger::resolve_cross_shard_target_queue`, which — for a cross-shard target — resolves the queue on the **target shard's** connection (mirroring how `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox` resolves it at fire time), falling back to the source connection only when the target-shard pool is unavailable (Fleet/name gates still match; only a Queue gate could be missed in that unreachable-pool edge). Same-shard targets keep the single-connection (no extra DB read) path. Tests, TDD red→green: `boot_load_of_persisted_gate_blocks_completion_trigger` (persist a Fleet gate, run the exact `load_active_gates` → `refresh` boot-load path, evaluate a matching trigger → blocked + counted + `admission_blocked` fires row — the behavioural guarantee the reordering provides; the private-`start_harvest_runtime` ordering itself is verified by code reading); `cross_shard_gate_check_resolves_target_queue_on_target_shard` (a genuine two-database multi-shard setup — shard 0/target owns the `ag_target_wf -> ag_priority_q` schedule, shard 1/source does not — proving `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` resolves on the target shard where the pre-fix `resolve_target_queue(source_conn, …)` missed it; needs only `harvest_schedules`, so it runs against a fresh `INIT_SQL` DB). Both new tests plus the full core suite (9/9) and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite (4/4) executed green against a real local Postgres 16. **CI-correctness gap fixed in round 4 (below):** the suite's curated `INIT_SQL` was incomplete for `start_or_load`, so its Docker-backed CI step would have failed; round 4 replaces it with the full migration set. **Post-review hardening, round 4 (three items in one pass — CI-correctness gap + two more Codex findings on `90f4f76`):** **(INIT_SQL — CI-correctness, the actual merge-blocker for this new suite.)** The suite is new in this PR, so its `INIT_SQL` const IS this PR's code, and the "Docker-backed admission-gate authoritative" CI step boots a fresh Postgres seeded from ONLY that const (no `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, no Postgres service, no `diesel migration run` anywhere in `ci.yml` — verified). The curated const omitted `harvest_build_policies`/`harvest_build_compat` (`build_routing`) **and** — schema had drifted further — `harvest_workflow_executions.legal_hold_set_at` (a much later migration), both read by `start_or_load_workflow_execution`, so all six `start_or_load`-calling tests would panic in CI (`relation "harvest_build_policies" does not exist`, then `column ... legal_hold_set_at does not exist`). **Reproduced exactly** against a fresh DB seeded with only the const's bytes. Fixed by replacing the hand-picked subset with the **COMPLETE 72-migration set in timestamp order** (identical to `diesel migration run`) — drift-proof by construction: a hand-picked subset silently rots every time the start path gains a column read, whereas the applied superset never over-constrains a test. **Proof (the exact CI Docker reproduction):** a fresh DB seeded from ONLY the const → the ENTIRE suite runs **9/9 green**, including `deferred_scanner_fires_are_counted_as_bypass` (the test that failed distinctly on the pre-F2 code) and the new cross-shard fallback assertions. (Executed against local Postgres 16 via a TCP `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` matching the testcontainer URL shape — Docker/testcontainers is unavailable in this sandbox; the const's exact byte-content was independently confirmed to apply cleanly to a fresh DB with every required table/column present.) **(Finding A, P1 — the outbound webhook delegate was ungated; the "authoritative" contract was FALSE.)** There are two webhook producers: the INBOUND receiver (`webhook_receiver.rs`, already gated — it delegates to `api::start_workflow`/`signal_with_start_workflow`), and the OUTBOUND `WebhookDelegateExt` (`plugin.rs`), which started the `webhook_delivery` workflow directly via `client.start_or_load` **without consulting the gate cache** — so a Fleet/queue/workflow gate did not stop these fresh in-process starts, and they weren't counted. This is one of the three original ungated producers issue #618 names ("the Autumn webhook delegate"). Fixed by gating the outbound start: before `start_or_load`, the delegate consults `global_admission_gate_cache()` via the new tested helper `webhook_delivery_admission_block(cache, shard, owner)` (fixed match inputs `workflow_name = "webhook_delivery"`, `queue = "webhooks"`, resolved `shard`/`owner`; `check_cached` honours the last-known snapshot even under a transient fail-closed blip and never returns the sentinel). A matching gate **blocks** the start (record `record_admission_blocked` with the same `(scope_kind, reason)` the API path records, then return an error — a `webhook_delivery` start is a fresh start and the operator's gate halts new starts, so block, not exempt); a non-matching gate proceeds unchanged. The `producer_contract()` entry + module-doc table now accurately describe BOTH webhook paths as gated. The generic embedder `WorkflowHandle::start_or_load` stays out-of-scope (an embedder's own start) — only the internal webhook-delivery producer is gated. Tests (RAN under `--features webhooks`): 5 unit tests in `plugin::webhook_admission_tests` (Fleet / `WorkflowName("webhook_delivery")` / `Queue("webhooks")` gates block; a different-workflow and different-queue gate and an empty cache proceed) exercising the exact helper the delegate calls. **CI coverage closed:** the `webhooks` feature had ZERO CI steps (its receiver tests never ran; `--all-targets` clippy without the feature never even compiled the gated code), so this PR adds a `webhooks`-feature plugin clippy step and a `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-plugin --features webhooks --lib` step to `ci.yml` — otherwise the new tests would be CI-dead. The full delegate-driven start-blocking (return `Err` + record on a match) is verified by code reading, since wiring the whole `webhook_outbound` + `AppState` + DB path in a unit test is impractical. **(Finding B, P2 — F2's connection-failure fallback resolved on the wrong shard.)** F2's `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` fell back to `resolve_target_queue(source_conn, …)` when the target-shard connection was unavailable; for `target_shard == 0` that path queries `harvest_schedules` on the connection it holds — the SOURCE connection — reintroducing the exact wrong-shard bug F2 fixed, in the connection-failure edge. Fixed by removing the `source_conn` parameter from `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` entirely (so a wrong-shard read is now **structurally impossible** from it): on a target-shard connection failure it falls back to the shard-INDEPENDENT `default_workflow_queue()` (the process-global registered default, else `"default"`) — never the source connection. `WorkflowMetadata` carries no per-workflow queue, so the only queue answer that genuinely needs the target shard is the schedule-level override; the documented bounded double-fault edge is that a `Queue(schedule-override)` gate can be missed only while the target shard is unreachable (strictly better than returning a wrong-shard queue). Fleet/name/owner/shard gates don't depend on the queue and still evaluate correctly. `default_workflow_queue()` also single-sources the two prior inline default-queue copies in `resolve_target_queue`. Test: the `cross_shard_gate_check_resolves_target_queue_on_target_shard` test gains a fallback leg — it seeds the SOURCE shard with a WRONG `ag_target_wf -> ag_source_wrong_q` schedule, installs a sharded pool mapping ONLY shard 1 (so `exact_pool_for(0)` is None → fallback), and asserts the resolver returns `"default"`, NOT `ag_source_wrong_q` (proving it never queried the source connection's schedules) and not the unreachable target's `ag_priority_q`. All five CI-mirror checks green (fmt; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings`; plugin `--all-targets` default/`webhooks`/`mcp`/`metrics` clippy `-D warnings`; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 533/533) and the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **9/9 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB**, all executed against local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (Codex P1 on PR #1014):** the round-1 F3 fix over-corrected. `AdmissionGateCache::set_fail_closed()` retains the cached gates snapshot (it only flips the `initialized` flag), but the completion-trigger path collapsed *every* fail-closed result onto the nil sentinel and PROCEEDED — so a real Fleet/name/queue gate already loaded into the cache, followed by a failed refresh (fail-closed), would let completion-trigger starts BYPASS the active gate uncounted while direct API starts still blocked: a gate leak during exactly the incident the gate exists for. Fixed by adding `AdmissionGateCache::check_cached()` (runs the pure `check_admission` matcher against the current snapshot regardless of the initialized flag, returning only a REAL matching gate, never the sentinel) and rewriting the completion-trigger branch to use it: a real cached gate matching the start → block + drop + count (keeping the F4 `inserted > 0` no-double-count guard); no cached gate matches → proceed (transient-blip / boot-window case, still avoiding a permanent drop). The `sentinel_gate_id()` special-casing was removed from `completion_trigger.rs` (the helper stays — `check()` still returns it for the API block-everything path). Deliberate, documented divergence: when initialized-and-healthy the API and triggers see identical gates; under fail-closed the API blocks everything (caller retries) while triggers honour only known-cached gates (they cannot retry). Bounded caveat (documented in `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md`): a gate ADDED during a gate-DB outage — never loaded into the snapshot — won't block completion triggers until the next successful refresh; strictly better than either permanent-drop or unconditional-bypass. Tests, TDD red→green: new core DB `completion_trigger_fail_closed_with_cached_gate_blocks` (a real Fleet gate loaded then `set_fail_closed()` → target NOT started, `admission_blocked` counted, fires row present — confirmed FAILING against the round-1 code, then green); the former `completion_trigger_fail_closed_sentinel_proceeds` renamed to `completion_trigger_fail_closed_no_cached_gate_proceeds` (empty snapshot → proceeds); unit tests `check_cached_honours_snapshot_under_fail_closed` / `check_cached_returns_none_on_empty_snapshot`. Executed against local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (two Codex P2s on `34a6ac5`):** **(Finding A, P2 — the outbound webhook delegate must fail CLOSED.)** Round-4's `webhook_delivery_admission_block` used `check_cached()`, which deliberately ignores the fail-closed/uninitialized sentinel — a semantic chosen for COMPLETION TRIGGERS (in-flight continuation of already-committed work, where a permanent drop is worse than a brief bypass). That rationale does NOT apply to an outbound `webhook_delivery` start, which is a FRESH, retryable workflow start equivalent to an HTTP API start: after a boot-time gate-load failure or a refresh outage (`check_cached` returns `None`), the webhook delivery would start while the HTTP start path fails closed and blocks — an inconsistency and an uncounted bypass. Fixed by switching the helper to the sentinel-aware `check()` (mirroring the HTTP start path): under fail-closed, `check()` returns the synthetic block → the delegate blocks the `webhook_delivery` start and records `record_admission_blocked` (as it already does for a real match). Failing closed here can never permanently drop anything (the delivery is retryable). Tests (RAN under `--features webhooks`): 2 new webhook unit tests — `uninitialized_cache_fails_closed_and_blocks` (`AdmissionGateCache::new_fail_closed()` → blocks with the `"fleet"` sentinel scope) and `set_fail_closed_reverts_to_blocking` (a populated cache reverted via `set_fail_closed()` blocks regardless of its cached gates) — plus the existing match/no-match tests and `initialized_empty_cache_lets_the_outbound_start_proceed` (an *initialized* empty cache is fail-open, so it still proceeds). **(Finding B, P2 — count completion-trigger blocks on the cancel/terminate/parent-close-cascade paths.)** A gate-blocked completion-trigger start inserts the durable `admission_blocked` fires row but emitted `harvest.admission.blocked` only inside `if let Some(m) = metrics`. The cancel/terminate/parent-close-cascade paths in `execution.rs` call `evaluate_triggers_for_execution(..., None)`, so a cancelled/terminated source with a completion trigger under an active gate was blocked-and-dropped but NEVER counted — a hole in the issue's "zero un-counted blocks" bar. **Least-invasive fix (a global recorder fallback, mirroring `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` established earlier in this PR):** `apply_parent_close_cascade` alone has 16 callers, so threading a recorder through the cancel/terminate/cascade signatures would cascade widely; instead a new `admission_gate::GLOBAL_ADMISSION_METRICS` static (`set_global_admission_metrics`/`global_admission_metrics`, poison-recovering `into_inner` like the gate-cache global) is published by the plugin at boot with the SAME `Arc<dyn MetricsRecorder>` the workers/scanners use, and cleared on stop (ptr-eq guarded against this runtime's recorder so a stopping plugin never clobbers a live sibling's). The block-count path in `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` resolves an effective recorder = the explicit `metrics` param when supplied, else the global fallback (a tuple `match` so the `&dyn MetricsRecorder` → annotated `+ Send + Sync` coercion applies at the expression site, matching how the worker passes `registry.telemetry().metrics.as_ref()`; a plain `if let/else` tripped `clippy::nursery`'s `option_if_let_else`). Still guarded on the fires-row `blocked_inserted > 0` so cascade re-entry records `deduped` instead of double-counting — the invariant holds: a completion-trigger start blocked by an active gate is counted on `harvest.admission.blocked` **exactly once** regardless of whether the source reached terminal via completion, cancel, or terminate. This also fixes every other `None`-passing caller uniformly. Test (TDD red→green, red confirmed): `completion_trigger_block_counted_via_global_recorder_on_cancel_path` — a completion trigger on a CANCELLED source under a Fleet gate, evaluated with `metrics: None` and the recorder supplied ONLY via the global, asserts target NOT started + `admission_blocked` fires row + the capturing recorder counted exactly one block; confirmed RED (`left: 0, right: 1`) against the fallback-disabled code before the fix. Round-5 verification (all RAN, executed against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks` clippy `-D warnings` clean; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 535/535 (incl. the 7 webhook admission tests); the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **10/10 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB** (the 9 prior + the new Finding B test); and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **4/4** against a fully-migrated DB (core + plugin migrations), confirming the boot-time global-recorder publish/clear does not regress plugin startup. **Post-review hardening, round 6 (one Codex P2 on `ad37cac`): count the IMMEDIATE completion-trigger outbox relay, not just the scanner.** For a cross-shard completion trigger, `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` writes an outbox row and returns a `DeferredTriggerStart`; the normal callers immediately call `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()`, which starts the target and deletes the row on success. Round-1's `record_admission_bypassed("completion_trigger_outbox")` counter was added ONLY in the later scanner `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox` — so the COMMON successful path (the immediate `spawn()` relay) never hit the counter: a gate raised after the source commit but before the immediate relay left that intentionally-exempt start UNCOUNTED, breaking the "zero un-counted bypass" contract. Fixed by counting the bypass in `spawn()`'s `Ok(start)` arm too, via the process-global recorder (`global_admission_metrics()` — `spawn` has no explicit `metrics` param), mirroring the scanner's `record_admission_bypassed(CompletionTriggerOutbox)`. **Exactly-once (verified):** an outbox row is started by EITHER the immediate `spawn()` OR the scanner (only if the immediate spawn didn't run / failed before deleting). The immediate count is gated on the delete actually removing the row (`matches!(deleted, Ok(n) if n >= 1)`) — tightened beyond the scanner's count-on-`Ok(start)` to close the start-ok/delete-fail edge for the immediate path: if the start failed (Err arm) or the delete removed nothing, `spawn()` does NOT count and the row persists for the scanner to count once. So exactly one count per started relay across both paths, each gated on its own successful start + row removal; matches the scanner's "any successful start (incl. `AllowDuplicate` attach), not just a fresh `created`" condition. Test (TDD red→green, red confirmed): `immediate_outbox_relay_counts_the_bypass_exactly_once` — a genuine two-database multi-shard test (source shard 0 owns the outbox row, target shard 1 receives the start) inserts an outbox row, publishes a capturing recorder via the global, fires `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (fire-and-forget, so it polls for completion), then asserts the target started on shard 1, the outbox row was deleted, `bypassed == ["completion_trigger_outbox"]` exactly once, AND running the scanner afterward relays 0 (row already gone) so the count stays exactly 1 (no double-count). **Red confirmed** by removing the `spawn()` count: the test fails ("the immediate spawn relay did not complete within the poll window", bypassed stays empty), then green after restoring. Round-6 verification (all RAN, local Postgres 16, Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks` clippy `-D warnings` clean; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 535/535; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **11/11 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB** (the 10 prior + the new immediate-relay test). **Post-review hardening, round 7 (two Codex P2s on `2411fc4`):** (Finding A, P2 — `plugin.rs`: clear the admission globals on a startup failure.) `start_harvest_runtime` published `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` and `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_METRICS` *before* `HarvestRunner::start`; if start (or any later step) returned `Err`, the process-global statics were left pointing at a half-started runtime's `Arc`s, so a later boot attempt or an in-flight scanner saw stale gate/metrics state. Fixed with an RAII `AdmissionGlobalsGuard` that owns the published `Arc`s: on `Drop` it clears whichever globals it published, each **ptr-eq-guarded** against *this* runtime's `Arc` (so a concurrent healthy sibling's cache is never clobbered — the same guard `stop_harvest_runtime` uses); the guard is defused with `.commit()` on the success path immediately before `Ok(())`. Publishing the gate cache and the metrics recorder are two separate guard calls (`publish_gate_cache`/`publish_metrics`), so a failure *between* them clears only the gate cache and leaves the never-published metrics slot untouched. Unit tests (`admission_globals_guard_tests`, serialized on a dedicated lock): drop clears both; drop before the metrics publish clears only the gate cache; `.commit()` keeps both; drop does not clobber a sibling cache published under a different `Arc`. (Finding B, P2 — `completion_trigger.rs`: gate the cross-shard relay AUTHORITATIVELY at relay time.) The inline gate check in `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` runs on the SOURCE terminal-commit connection and can only *approximate* a cross-shard target's real queue (round-3's `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` reads the target shard, but a transiently-unavailable target pool falls back to the source connection and can MISS a `Queue(real-q)` gate). Rather than chase a perfect inline approximation, the relay is now gated **authoritatively at relay time on the target shard**, where the real resolved queue is known — in BOTH `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (the immediate path) and the scanner `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox`. New `relay_gate_block(workflow_name, resolved_queue, target_shard, owner)` helper consults the process-global cache via `check_cached` (NOT `check()` — the relay materializes a *pre-committed* in-flight-continuation start, so a fail-closed sentinel must not permanently drop it; only a real known-cached gate blocks). Gate matches → **BLOCK**: drop the outbox row and record `record_admission_blocked` (via the explicit scanner `metrics` recorder, or the global recorder in `spawn()`); no gate → start + count the bypass. The inline check is kept as a best-effort fast path (it can still short-circuit a same-shard block before writing the row). `StartProducer::CompletionTriggerOutbox`'s `producer_contract()` status changes from `ExemptByDesign` to the new `ProducerGateStatus::GatedAtRelay` variant; module docs, `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md`, and `docs/api-contract.json` updated accordingly. **Exactly-once / block-vs-bypass never double-counts:** an outbox row is processed by exactly one path (immediate `spawn()` OR scanner — the scanner only claims rows the immediate spawn didn't delete). BOTH the block count and the bypass count are gated on the delete actually removing the row (`matches!(deleted, Ok(n) if n >= 1)`), so a given row is counted EITHER `record_admission_blocked` (gate matched → drop) OR `record_admission_bypassed` (no gate → start → drop) — never both, exactly once, and a start-ok/delete-fail edge leaves the row for the other path rather than double-counting. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed): `immediate_outbox_relay_blocks_on_real_queue_gate` — a genuine two-database multi-shard test (source shard 0, target shard 1) where the target schedule sets `queue_name = 'real-q'` (inserted on the DEFAULT shard, since `resolve_target_queue` for a nonzero target reads the default shard's `harvest_schedules`) and an active `Queue('real-q')` gate; `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` must relay-block (target NOT started, outbox row dropped, exactly one `fleet`/`queue` block recorded, zero bypass), and a follow-up scanner relays 0. The pre-existing `deferred_scanner_fires_are_counted_as_bypass` (core) and `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` (plugin) were updated for the behaviour change: under a Fleet gate the CT cross-shard relay now BLOCKS (one fleet block, its target does not start) rather than bypassing — the pure deferred-fire scanners (debounce/throttle/event-batch) and the workflow-start outbox stay exempt-with-bypass-counter. Round-7 verification (all RAN, executed against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **12/12 against a fresh full-migration INIT_SQL-only DB** (11 prior + the new immediate-relay-block test) and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **4/4**; the `admission_globals_guard_tests` unit set 4/4; fmt/clippy clean across all crates and features (incl. `webhooks`). **Post-review hardening, round 8 (one Codex P2 on `1027eb6`): the workflow-start outbox bypass could double-count on a mark-delivered retry.** The same exactly-once-on-durable-completion issue round 6 fixed for the completion-trigger relay, now for the ORIGINAL workflow-start outbox (round 1's `record_admission_bypassed("outbox")`, untouched since). `dispatch_workflow_start_request` (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/outbox.rs`) incremented the `"outbox"` bypass counter as soon as the Harvest start succeeded, but the caller `drain_workflow_start_outbox_batch` marks the app outbox row delivered only AFTERWARDS. If the start succeeded and `mark_outbox_row_delivered` then FAILED, the row stayed eligible past its claim TTL; the retry re-entered dispatch, `start_or_load` returned the SAME existing execution, and the counter fired AGAIN — one committed outbox start reported as multiple admission bypasses. Fixed by moving `record_admission_bypassed("outbox")` out of `dispatch_workflow_start_request` to the caller, right AFTER the `?`-guarded `mark_outbox_row_delivered` returns `Ok` (the recorder is fetched once before the loop, from the same `HandlerRegistry` telemetry the dispatch path uses). **Exactly-once:** start-ok + mark-ok → count once, row gone (no retry); start-ok + mark-Err → `?`-returns BEFORE counting, row persists → retry → `start_or_load` returns the existing execution → mark retried → count only when the mark finally succeeds — so exactly one bypass per committed outbox start across any number of mark retries, mirroring round 6's "gate the count on the row delete actually removing the row." Tests: round 1's `outbox_relay_is_exempt_and_counts_the_bypass` still passes (a successful relay marks delivered → counts once); new `outbox_bypass_counted_exactly_once_across_reflush` drives the observable half — one relay counts once and durably marks the row delivered (`delivered_at IS NOT NULL`), and a SECOND flush (the delivered row now ineligible) never re-counts and never re-starts (`target_exec_count == 1`). The start-ok/mark-Err window itself is closed by the count's placement strictly after the `?`-guarded mark (verified by reading — a genuine mark-DB-error cannot be injected through the public flush path in the harness). Round-8 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks,mcp,metrics,unified-dag-execution` clippy `-D warnings` clean; the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **5/5** (the 4 prior + the new reflush guard) against a fresh full-migration INIT_SQL-only DB. **Post-review hardening, round 9 (two Codex P2s on `6b61cea`, both fallout from earlier fixes):** (Finding A, `plugin.rs`) don't gate idempotent webhook-delivery RETRIES. Round 5's fail-closed change gates the outbound `webhook_delivery` delegate BEFORE `client.start_or_load`, but the delegate's workflow id is deterministic (`webhook-delivery-{log.id}`) and its start params use `AllowDuplicate` — so when the delegate is invoked again for the same webhook log after the `webhook_delivery` execution ALREADY EXISTS (a retry), `start_or_load` idempotently LOADS the existing run rather than admitting a fresh one. The round-5 pre-check nonetheless returned an error + counted a block, wrongly blocking a non-admission and inflating the block counter. Fixed by mirroring the #808 HTTP path's committed-replay bypass: the delegate now acquires the target-shard connection first and does a read-only `execution::try_load_by_key(conn, "webhook_delivery", workflow_id)` existence check — the exact `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` key `start_or_load` reuses (`try_load_by_key` excludes only the sealed CONTINUED_AS_NEW/TERMINATED states that would themselves force a fresh start, so `Some` ⟺ idempotent load and `None` ⟺ fresh admission). The gate is consulted only for a genuinely fresh delivery via the new pure `webhook_delivery_gate_decision(already_exists, cache, shard, owner)` helper: `already_exists` → `None` (skip the gate, no block, no count); fresh + matching gate → block+count; fresh + fail-closed (uninitialized) cache → block via the synthetic sentinel (round-5 behavior intact); fresh + no matching gate / no cache → proceed. (Finding B, `plugin.rs`) clear the admission globals AFTER the runner stops. `stop_harvest_runtime` cleared `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` (and `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_METRICS`) while the runner was still alive — `runtime.runner.stop().await` ran LATER — so during shutdown/restart under an active gate, an in-flight worker/timeout scanner could still evaluate a completion trigger in that window, see `global_admission_gate_cache() == None`, skip the gate, and start a target unblocked + uncounted. Fixed by reordering: cancel the gate-refresh + outbox tasks, `runtime.runner.stop().await` (all worker + timeout-scanner tasks stopped), THEN clear both globals — each still ptr-eq guarded so a stopping plugin never clobbers a concurrently-live sibling's cache/recorder. The metrics recorder Arc is captured before `HarvestRunner::stop(self)` consumes the runner. The no-runtime early-return path clears only the gate cache (no runner is running, so it is safe; there is no runtime recorder Arc to ptr-eq against). The lock closes the window: a live run cannot seal under the held lock (so it is attached, `created=false`, gate skipped) and a sealed/absent run cannot gain a live row under the lock (so a fresh create is correctly gated — a matching gate blocks, else it proceeds).
