So a successfully-started target was reported and counted as dropped by the gate (a false block + a corrupted durable audit). **Fix — route the relay's start/block decision through the round-12 existence-aware `execution::gate_checked_start_or_load` primitive, in BOTH relay paths.** New shared `completion_trigger::relay_gate_checked_start(target_conn, source_conn, params, gate_workflow_name, gate_resolved_queue, gate_owner, target_shard, outbox_id, source_exec_id, trigger_id, metrics)` builds the gate closure `move |locked_live| if locked_live { None /* a LOCKED live target already exists → this is a delivery/idempotent-load, NOT a fresh admission → skip the gate */ } else { check_cached(real_resolved_queue, target_shard, owner) }` and calls `gate_checked_start_or_load`, which locks the target's existence on the TARGET shard through the gate/start decision (the same `try_load_active_execution_for_update` `FOR UPDATE` seam round 12 added). Routing by outcome: **target already exists** (`Started { created: false }`, the stale-row case) → DELIVERED: delete the source outbox row + count the `completion_trigger_outbox` bypass, leaving the fires row `NULL`/fired — NOT blocked, NOT marked `admission_blocked`; **fresh + matching gate** (`Blocked`) → `relay_block_drop_outbox` on the source shard (delete outbox + mark fires `admission_blocked`) + count the block; **fresh + no gate** (`Started { created: true }`) → delete outbox + count bypass. The two-shard split is preserved (target-shard existence-lock + gate + start atomic; source-shard outbox delete + fires mark), and exactly-once is still gated on the source-shard delete actually removing the row (block XOR bypass, never both, across the immediate-xor-scanner relay paths). Both `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (uses the process-global recorder + a fresh source-shard connection from `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL`) and the scanner (passes its own `conn` as the source connection + the `shards`-scoped `target_shard` assignments) now funnel through this one helper; the now-dead round-7 `relay_gate_block` free function was removed. Round-13 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks,mcp,metrics,unified-dag-execution` clippy `-D warnings` clean; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **16/16** against `ag_r7` AND against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB (`ag_r13_init`, built by applying exactly the test's `INIT_SQL` migration bundle to an empty database — 15 prior + the new stale-row-delivered test); the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **5/5**; and the core `completion_trigger::` lib unit tests **26/26**. **Post-review hardening, round 14 (one Codex P2 on `fa87c93`): publish the admission metrics recorder BEFORE starting workers.** An earlier round moved the process-global gate *cache* publish ahead of `HarvestRunner::start` (so a scanner tick / completion trigger firing in the boot window sees the persisted gates), but the process-global *metrics recorder* publish stayed **after** `HarvestRunner::start` — it read `runner.api_runtime().registry().telemetry().metrics`, which only exists once the runner is built. The change stays inside the RAII `AdmissionGlobalsGuard`: an early-return error after either publish still clears BOTH globals, and `.commit()` on success still keeps both; the round-9 shutdown ordering (clear the globals only AFTER `runtime.runner.stop().await`) is untouched. A completion-trigger outbox row is a **one-shot delivery marker** ("trigger T fired; start deterministic target W exactly once, then delete the row"); the scanner only re-sees a stale row after the immediate relay STARTED W but then failed to delete the source row (transient source-pool/delete failure), so a stale row implies W was created. If W has since sealed/completed, the active-only lock saw no live run → under a matching gate the relay `Blocked` and marked the fires row `admission_blocked` (re-doing a delivered fire as a block), and with **no** gate a *sealed* target (released from the `harvest_we_workflow_name_workflow_id_active_key` partial unique index) let `start_or_load` create a **SECOND** W. Both are wrong — the fire was already delivered. **Fix — any-state existence = delivered, completion-trigger relay ONLY:** `relay_gate_checked_start` now, BEFORE calling `gate_checked_start_or_load`, runs a new read-only any-state existence check on the target shard — `execution::execution_exists_by_key(target_conn, workflow_name, workflow_id)` (a `SELECT EXISTS(... WHERE name AND id)` with NO state filter, so it sees sealed AND completed rows the active-only lock hides). W exists in ANY state → DELIVERED: delete the source outbox row + count the `completion_trigger_outbox` bypass, leave the fires row a real fire (`NULL`) — never block, never mark `admission_blocked`, never create a second W. W does not exist at all → genuinely fresh → proceed via `gate_checked_start_or_load` exactly as round 13 (its active-lock is correct there since no W exists; gate matches → block, else create + bypass). The orthogonal pending-*throttle*-row bypass disjunct (issue #607) is preserved unchanged. **#808 keyed replay, and the debounce/batch/throttle mutual-exclusion `400`s, are untouched** — the keyed committed-replay probe still short-circuits to the `200` no-op *above* the gate, and the mutual-exclusion checks run before this block; the only behavioral change is that the *explicit-`workflow_id`* attach bypass is now policy-aware. **TOCTOU decision — policy-blindness fixed robustly; the residual bounded window was subsequently CLOSED in round 21 (below).** The round-20 pre-check reads the prior state on a throwaway connection released before the start runs later on its own transaction, so a prior that seals (e.g. a live run → `FAILED`) in the read→start gap could turn an `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly` attach decided here into a replacement that slips the gate. TDD red→green (RED confirmed by `git stash`-ing only the `api.rs` fix): three new plugin-localpg HTTP tests in `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg.rs` — `gate_blocks_terminate_if_running_start_over_a_live_prior` (503 + one `fleet` block counted + no replacement row), `gate_blocks_allow_duplicate_failed_only_start_over_a_failed_prior` (503 + counted + no replacement), and `gate_skips_allow_duplicate_attach_regardless_of_prior_state` (the #808 non-regression: `AllowDuplicate` over both a `RUNNING` and a `COMPLETED` prior → `200` attach, zero blocks counted, no new execution). **RED confirmed** with the fix stashed: the two block tests return `200`/non-503 (gate wrongly skipped) and fail their `503` assertion, while the attach test passes under both (old code also skips for `AllowDuplicate`); **GREEN** with the fix: all three pass. Round-20 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; core + plugin `--all-features`/`--tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; the **full** no-DB `--test integration` suite **801/801**; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **23/23** against the freshly-rebuilt INIT_SQL-only DB (`ag_r16_init`); the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **8/8** (5 existing + 3 new) against `ag_localpg`. **Post-review hardening, round 21 (one Codex P2 on `e1cb326`): CLOSE the round-20 residual TOCTOU on the HTTP `start_workflow` route by deciding the gate under the same `FOR UPDATE` lock as the create.** Round 20 made the HTTP route's gate-skip pre-check reuse-policy-aware, but the *decision* was still read from an UNLOCKED pre-read of the prior's state that was released before the real `start_or_load` transaction — a genuine un-counted-admission window in the PRIMARY producer of a containment control, and exactly the residual the webhook (round 12) and completion-trigger relay (round 19) paths had already closed via locking, so the HTTP path keeping it was the wrong inconsistency. Two leak races: default `AllowDuplicate` sees a `RUNNING` prior (→ attach → skip gate) but it seals to `TERMINATED`/`CONTINUED_AS_NEW` before the start → `start_or_load` CREATES fresh under the active gate, uncounted; `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly` sees `RUNNING` (→ attach → skip) but it becomes `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` → `start_or_load` REPLACES → fresh execution under the gate, uncounted. **Fix (PREFERRED approach — route through the existing locking primitive, no fork of the #808/debounce/throttle layering):** the pure-plain explicit-`workflow_id` start under an active gate now runs through `execution::gate_checked_start_or_load` (the round-12/18/19 primitive) at the plain start call, which opens a transaction, takes a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the non-sealed prior via `try_load_active_execution_for_update`, computes `will_create` from that stable LOCKED state via the shared `start_will_create_new_execution` matrix, applies the gate **iff** a fresh execution will be created, and runs `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect(..., in_outer_transaction=true)` in the SAME transaction — so the gate decision and the create-vs-attach decision can never see two different prior states. The leak is impossible by construction: a prior sealing in the old read→start gap is now observed *under the lock* as sealed/terminal → `will_create=true` → BLOCK + count, no replacement. **Scope kept surgical (the finding's races are both pure-plain; the coordinator scoped keyed/throttle as untouched):** the gate is now CAPTURED once (`active_gate`) but the *authoritative decision* is deferred to the locked start ONLY for the pure-plain path (`explicit_workflow_id && idempotency_key.is_none() && !throttle_applies`). Every other path keeps its inline round-20 pre-read decision because each takes an early exit *before* the locked plain start and so cannot borrow the primitive's atomicity: the KEYED (#808) path runs its own `_idempotent` primitive and returns (the committed-replay `200` short-circuit stays above the gate); the THROTTLE (#607) path must be BLOCKED at admission (not silently deferred to a 202 the exempt scanner later fires), so its gate decision stays inline; an auto-generated `workflow_id` has no prior so its create is unconditional (block early, no lock, no race). Those two paths retain a bounded pre-read residual, explicitly out of this finding's scope; a future round can route `_idempotent`/the throttle-reserved start under a lock too. **Preserved:** #808 idempotency-key committed-replay bypass (still `200` above the gate); debounce/throttle/batch mutual-exclusion `400`s (run before the gate); the round-1 API gate for a genuinely fresh start (now decided under the lock, same `503`); response status codes (201 created / 200 attached / 503 blocked); audit + `record_admission_blocked` metric (the under-lock `Blocked` arm emits the same metric, the same `admission blocked by gate` audit row, and the same `503 {error, gate_id, reason}` body the inline pre-check produced; a throttle token, if any, is refunded on block mirroring the `AlreadyExists`/`Err` arms). Minor, documented consequence: a pure-plain explicit-`workflow_id` fresh start that is *also* invalid now runs input-schema/delay validation before the (now-locked) gate, so an invalid-and-gated request yields the validation `400` rather than the `503` — atomicity requires the gate to sit at the start, and `400` for a malformed body is defensible. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new metric, no schema change** — the change is a call-site rewiring plus reusing the already-tested locking primitive. TDD red→green with a deterministic race reproduction (lock-holding harness): new plugin-localpg HTTP test `http_start_blocks_a_prior_that_seals_between_read_and_start` (multi-thread) seeds a `RUNNING` prior, raises a Fleet gate, holds `FOR UPDATE` on the prior and seals it to `FAILED` (uncommitted), spawns the HTTP `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly` start, waits for it to queue on the prior's lock, then commits the seal — under the fix the start observes `FAILED` under the lock → `503` BLOCKED + counted (`fleet`), and exactly ONE row remains (the sealed prior, no replacement). **RED confirmed** by `git stash`-ing only the `api.rs` fix: the round-20 unlocked pre-read (a plain SELECT) observes the committed `RUNNING` state, skips the gate, and `start_or_load` replaces the freshly-sealed prior → `201 CREATED`, no block counted, 2 rows — the test fails its `503` assertion; **GREEN** with the fix restored. The round-20 deterministic tests (`gate_blocks_terminate_if_running_start_over_a_live_prior`, `gate_blocks_allow_duplicate_failed_only_start_over_a_failed_prior`, `gate_skips_allow_duplicate_attach_regardless_of_prior_state`) all still pass under the locked path (the primitive re-derives their block/attach outcomes under the lock). Round-21 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; core `--all-features --tests` + plugin `--all-targets --features webhooks,mcp,metrics,unified-dag-execution` clippy `-D warnings` clean; the **full** no-DB `--test integration` suite **801/801**; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **23/23** against a freshly-rebuilt INIT_SQL-only DB (`ag_r16_init`); the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **9/9** (8 prior + the new race test) against `ag_localpg`. **Post-review hardening, round 22 (one Codex P2 on `5fa00b1`, refining the round-16 write-through decision): fail closed for `check()` when the post-mutation full refresh fails.** Round 16 made the create/lift gate handlers apply the just-persisted change to the in-memory snapshot as a write-through delta (`apply_created`/`apply_lifted`) **and** dropped the post-mutation `set_fail_closed()` for BOTH `check` paths — an over-correction. On a post-mutation `load_active_gates` failure, this replica kept serving `check()` from an *initialized* snapshot that reflected only the LOCAL write-through delta: in a multi-replica deployment whose cache was already stale for ANOTHER operator's gate (e.g. a Fleet gate created on replica B just before this replica creates a narrower gate and then fails its own full reload), fresh starts that don't match this local gate were ADMITTED until the next successful refresh — instead of failing closed while the gate table is unreadable. Same stale-snapshot risk on the lift path. **Fix — restore `set_fail_closed()` on a failed post-mutation reload; the round-3 `check`/`check_cached` split makes it safe.** Round 3 already makes `check_cached` IGNORE the fail-closed sentinel and read the current snapshot, so re-arming fail-closed does NOT reintroduce the round-16 problems: `check()` (the API / fresh-admission path, which CAN retry) returns the synthetic block under fail-closed → the caller retries → no fresh start slips while the gate table is unreadable (protecting against a missing other-replica gate) — Codex's ask and the correct conservative behaviour for a containment control; `check_cached` (completion triggers / in-flight continuation, which CANNOT retry) still honours the snapshot + the round-16 write-through delta → the just-created gate is still matched, the just-lifted gate is still removed → NO permanent drop. So round 16's completion-trigger goal is preserved **via round 3**, not via dropping fail-closed. The round-16 write-through (`apply_created`/`apply_lifted`) is kept exactly as-is — it is what makes `check_cached` accurate for the mutated gate. **Superseding the round-16 "drop fail-closed" rationale explicitly:** the round-16 objection that keeping fail-closed re-blocks the just-unblocked work on the lift path is now ACCEPTED as the correct conservative behaviour for a safety control during a gate-table outage (over-block briefly rather than risk leaking a start past another replica's still-active gate this replica's local snapshot cannot see), bounded by the ≤1s background refresh interval — Codex explicitly wants the lift path to fail closed too. Fail-closed is **transient**: a SUCCESSFUL post-mutation reload calls `refresh()` → sets `initialized = true` → recovers and reconciles the authoritative active-gate list, so `check()` fails closed only while the reload is failing. **Implementation:** the duplicated `Ok(refresh)+record-metric / Err(warn)` match in both handlers is extracted into one pure, testable helper `reconcile_gate_cache_after_mutation(cache, op, reload_result) -> Option<i64>` (`Ok` → `refresh()` + return the active-gate count for the `admission_gates_active` metric; `Err` → `set_fail_closed()` + warn + `None`), used by both create and lift. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no schema change, no new metric** — a re-arm of an existing cache method plus a DRY refactor of the two handlers. TDD red→green (genuine source-level RED via the extracted helper): two new plugin-lib unit tests in `api.rs` — `reconcile_gate_cache_fails_closed_on_create_reload_error_keeps_check_cached_delta` (drives the cache directly with a queue-scoped gate: applies the write-through delta, calls the helper with a synthetic `Err`, then asserts `check("other_wf","ungated-q")` returns the fail-closed **sentinel** block for a NON-matching start, while `check_cached` still MATCHES the just-created gate by its real id AND lets a non-matching start proceed; a follow-up `Ok` reload asserts `check()` recovers from fail-closed) and `reconcile_gate_cache_lift_fails_closed_but_check_cached_drops_the_lifted_gate` (the lift path: `check()` fails closed / over-blocks even the just-lifted target's matching start, while `check_cached` no longer matches the lifted gate — in-flight continuation unaffected). The first test also asserts the round-21 leak as a precondition (delta applied but fail-closed NOT armed → `check()` admits the non-matching start). **RED confirmed** by commenting out the helper's `cache.set_fail_closed()`: both tests fail their `check() must fail closed (sentinel)` assertion (check admits the non-matching start → `None`, not the sentinel); **GREEN** with it restored. The round-16 write-through unit tests (`apply_lifted_..._check_cached...`, `apply_lifted_without_fail_closed_stops_check_blocking_the_lifted_target`, `apply_created_is_idempotent_by_id`, `apply_lifted_absent_id_is_a_noop`) all still pass (they exercise the cache methods directly and are unaffected by the handler's fail-closed re-arm). Round-22 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; core `--all-features --tests` + plugin `--all-targets --features webhooks,mcp,metrics,unified-dag-execution` clippy `-D warnings` clean; the **full** no-DB `--test integration` suite **801/801**; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **23/23** against a freshly-rebuilt INIT_SQL-only DB (`ag_r16_init`); the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **9/9** against `ag_localpg`; the two new plugin-lib unit tests **2/2**. **Post-review hardening, round 23 (ROOT FIX — move gate enforcement INTO the core start primitive; subsume the per-path pre-checks and the `gate_checked_start_or_load` wrapper).** Rounds 1–22 accreted admission-gate enforcement as an *unlocked pre-read* at each producer plus a shared `gate_checked_start_or_load` wrapper for the two paths (webhook delegate, CT relay) that needed the locked decision. That left a whole *class* of TOCTOU — a prior sealing between an unlocked pre-read and the later start — open on the batch, keyed-#808, and throttle paths (round 21 only closed the pure-plain HTTP path), and it duplicated the create-vs-attach reasoning at every call site. This pass makes the gate authoritative in **one** place: `execution::start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect` gained a trailing `gate: Option<admission_gate::GateMode>` parameter and enforces the gate at the exact points where — under its own `FOR UPDATE` lock on any prior run — it decides it will CREATE a new execution. **Two enforcement points:** (1) for `TerminateIfRunning` (always creates, state-independent), the gate is applied UNLOCKED at the top of `_collect`, *before* the pre-check cancellation, so a blocked start never cancels the prior first; (2) for every other policy, the transaction takes the `FOR UPDATE` lock on the non-sealed prior via `try_load_active_execution_for_update` FIRST — before the `on_conflict_do_nothing` INSERT — computes `will_create` from that one stable locked state via the shared `start_will_create_new_execution` matrix, and blocks iff a new execution will be created (an idempotent ATTACH admits nothing and is never gated). The empirically-verified reason this must pre-lock rather than gate at the post-INSERT branch: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` does **not** wait on a concurrent `FOR UPDATE` holder of a committed conflicting row (it no-ops immediately against the committed-visible RUNNING prior), so the seal-race would otherwise fall through to a `NotFound` rather than reach a post-INSERT gate — the pre-lock (identical to what `gate_checked_start_or_load` did) is what makes the seal land on a clean TERMINATED-excluded read. A blocked start returns the pre-existing `HarvestError::AdmissionBlocked { gate_id, reason }` (rolls the transaction back — no fresh row, no events) and records `harvest.admission.blocked` exactly once via the new module-private `record_start_gate_block` helper (caller recorder, else the process-global recorder — so a block on a metrics-less internal terminal path is still counted); `evaluate_start_gate` selects `check` (fail-closed `GateMode::Check`) vs `check_cached` (snapshot-only `GateMode::CheckCached`). **New `admission_gate::GateMode` enum** (`Check`/`CheckCached`), re-exported from `lib.rs`. **`gate` threaded through** `start_or_load_workflow_execution`, `_with_metrics`, and `_idempotent` (the #808 keyed path — it forwards the gate into `_collect` under the reservation transaction, so a blocked keyed start rolls the idempotency reservation back and is retryable). **Removed/consolidated:** `gate_checked_start_or_load` + the `GateCheckedStart` enum are DELETED; the plugin `start_workflow` route's large unlocked `active_gate` pre-check block is removed (plain + keyed now pass `Some(Check)` and the primitive gates; `Err(AdmissionBlocked)` maps to `503 {error, gate_id, reason}` on both, with any reserved throttle token refunded); the batch item start passes `Some(Check)` so the batch TOCTOU is closed at Phase 2 under the lock while the Phase-1 pre-check is kept for its atomic-preflight abort (no double-count — Phase-1 blocks non-idempotent items that never reach Phase-2, Phase-2 gates the policy-blindly-skipped ones); the webhook delegate and the CT cross-shard relay call the primitive directly with `Some(CheckCached)` (the relay drops the outbox row + marks the fires row `admission_blocked` on `Err(AdmissionBlocked)` and no longer re-records the metric — the primitive records it, so the block stays exactly-once); the pure `webhook_delivery_gate_decision`/`webhook_delivery_admission_block` helpers + their test module are deleted (subsumed). **Opt-in — continuation paths stay ungated (`None`):** child/detached-child spawn, continue-as-new + workflow-level retry (#523), reset forks, the transactional workflow-start Outbox relay, the in-process client handle, and signal-/update-with-start internal starts all pass `gate = None` (in-flight continuation of already-committed work, out of the finding's scope). **Deferred-fire scanners stay `None` and keep their existing `record_admission_bypassed`** (debounce #499, throttle #607, event-batch #357) — passing a gate would BLOCK them and break the round-6 "zero un-counted admissions" contract. **Scheduler tick / backfill / manual-trigger / Vantage-UI manual start stay `None`** (they already gate authoritatively at their own inline tick check and are not in the finding's TOCTOU class; over-gating would double-count and add an unhandled error path — a documented deviation from an earlier "scheduler → Some(Check)" sketch, made to preserve `scheduled_start_blocked_by_gate_records_admission_blocked`). **The multi-runtime `AdmissionGlobalsGuard` save/restore fix is included** (a failed second-runtime startup in the same process now RESTORES the previous global gate cache + metrics recorder — a live sibling's — on drop-without-commit, instead of clearing to `None`; guarded on `Arc::ptr_eq`), with its unit test `guard_drop_restores_the_previous_sibling_globals_not_none`. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new metric, no schema change** — a signature widening plus one authoritative locked gate point, replacing N unlocked pre-reads. **TDD red→green** (RED confirmed by reverting the three `Some(Check)` gate args to `None`, which makes all new + existing gate-block tests admit uncounted): the 5 core `gate_checked_start_or_load` tests were rewritten to call `_with_metrics(..., Some(Check))` and assert `Ok`/`Err(AdmissionBlocked)` (incl. the deterministic seal-under-lock `gate_checked_start_blocks_a_run_that_seals_under_the_lock` and the ADFO/TIR replacement + AllowDuplicate-attach matrix); three NEW plugin-localpg tests close the batch/keyed/throttle TOCTOU class — `batch_item_blocks_a_prior_that_seals_between_phase1_and_phase2` (multi-thread lock-holding harness: a batch item's prior seals to TERMINATED between Phase-1's policy-blind skip and Phase-2's locked start → block counted once, no replacement), `keyed_start_blocked_by_gate_is_counted_and_rolls_back_reservation` (fresh #808 keyed start under a gate → 503 + counted + zero `harvest_start_idempotency` claims persisted), and `throttle_reserved_start_blocked_by_gate_refunds_token_and_counts` (fresh #607 throttled start reserves a token, falls through to the gated plain path → 503 + counted + token refunded to full burst). **Every prior round preserved** (all still green): #808 idempotency committed-replay bypass, debounce/throttle/batch mutual-exclusion `400`s, exactly-once block/bypass counting (the success-metric `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` — debounce/throttle/event_batch/outbox still in the `bypassed` list, api/CT/CT-relay in the `blocked` list), CT relay delivered-if-exists + `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` source claim, attach-vs-create matrix (`start_will_create_new_execution` retained), fail-closed `check()`/`check_cached()` split + write-through, fires-row `admission_blocked`, scheduler/event-batch counting, response codes (201/200/503), the producer contract at `GET /admin/gates`, and the round-20/21 HTTP seal-race tests. **Round-23 verification (all RAN against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox):** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; core `--all-features --tests` + plugin `--all-targets` (plain) + plugin `--all-targets --features webhooks,mcp,metrics,unified-dag-execution` clippy `-D warnings` all clean;
