- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Child-or-deadline waits for bounded sub-orchestrations — see issue #779. `WorkflowContext::execute_child_workflow_timeout::<O>(info, input, timeout) -> HarvestResult<Option<O>>` (typed) and the untyped sibling `spawn_child_workflow_timeout(name, input, timeout) -> HarvestResult<Option<Value>>` bound a **child-workflow** await with a durable deadline — the primitive for a sub-orchestration that must not run past an SLA. It mirrors `receive_signal_timeout` (#476) one level up: instead of racing a signal against a timer, it races a child workflow's terminal outcome against a timer. `Ok(Some(output))` = child terminal **success** before the deadline; `Ok(None)` = deadline fired first (the still-running child is **request-cancelled**); `Err(_)` = child **failure** before the deadline, with the typed failure preserved end-to-end (issue #767 — `err.workflow_error_type()`/`workflow_details()`/`is_workflow_non_retryable()` all readable on the parent side). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, core-only.** The race composes the existing `ChildWorkflowStarted`/`ChildWorkflowCompleted`/`ChildWorkflowFailed` events with the existing `TimerStarted`/`TimerFired` events; the winner is decided by **recorded history order** (order-stable across workers and replays), via the new `HistoryMatcher::match_child_or_timer` returning the new `ChildOrTimerMatch` enum (exported from `lib.rs`). The matcher positionally matches **both** `ChildWorkflowStarted` (capturing the `child_id`) and `TimerStarted`, then forward-scans for the earliest-recorded resolution: a child-win consumes the stray `TimerFired` transparently; a timer-win genuinely consumes the loser child's terminal (so `has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed` stays clean) and returns a `child_already_terminal` flag used to gate the on-deadline cancel to exactly one live cycle. Reserved-signal-events machinery is untouched — child-timeout timers use a `__child_timeout:{seq}:{name}` id namespace disjoint from `__signal_timeout:`. **Worker path (additive):** the two-phase "spawn child then arm the timer in a later batch" shape was rejected — it deadlocks if the child hangs (the parent is never woken until the child terminates, so the deadline would never arm). Instead the primitive spawns the child and arms the deadline in **one** mixed `StartChildWorkflow + StartTimer` suspension batch via a dedicated `extract_child_timeout_race` (accepts exactly one child + one timer + bookkeeping; any extra command falls through to the generic "unsupported commands" failure) and a new `persist_child_timeout_race` transaction (child new-vs-existing resolution + `ChildWorkflowStarted`, then the durable timer arm + `reschedule_task(fires_at)`, factoring shared helpers out of `persist_all_started_child_workflows`/`persist_started_timer`), plus a child-terminal **self-wake re-check** after commit so a child that reaches terminal in the park window is not missed. A new dispatch branch is inserted before the timer branch and a matching branch added to the history-cap event-count predictor. On-deadline request-cancel reuses `ctx.race()`'s existing `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { children }` → `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (synchronously seals the awaited child and appends its terminal in the same transaction; benign no-op on replay). Per-context `child_timeout_seq` counter added to `WorkflowContext` and initialised in all three constructors. **Composition caveats** (mirroring #476): cannot share a single suspension batch with a *new* `ScheduleActivity`/`StartChildWorkflow` — the child is spawned+raced in this call's own single mixed batch, so `tokio::join!`-ing two child-timeouts or racing a child-timeout against other new work is rejected fail-loud; the deadline default is request-cancel (no "abandon" variant — a follow-up); detached children are out of scope; and on a child-win the deadline timer is **proactively torn down** (see the post-review note below). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** on a child-win (both the `ChildCompleted` and `ChildFailed` branches) the still-armed `__child_timeout:{seq}` durable timer is now proactively torn down via a `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { timers: [...] }` bookkeeping command (`queue::delete_pending_timer`), mirroring `ctx.race()`'s `race_timer_signal_impl` signal-won branch. Left armed, the unfired `harvest_timers` row (`fired = false`) is treated as an in-flight dependency by `retention::has_inflight_dependencies`, which would **pin the terminal parent forever** (retention never collects it). The delete appends **no event**, so pushing it on every replay cycle (not just the first) is strict-replay-safe — the executor's completion-time drain-command check already excludes `CancelRaceLosers` from the "new commands beyond recorded history" divergence check, so the child-win replayer fixture still reports `ReplaySucceeded`. Verified end-to-end by the new DB e2e `child_win_tears_down_deadline_timer_no_retention_pin` (child completes → parent COMPLETED → no unfired `__child_timeout:` row remains) and the updated context unit tests (child-completed / child-failed both assert exactly one `CancelRaceLosers` targeting the race timer). **Follow-up:** `wait_for_signal_timeout` has the same latent retention leak on signal-win (its timer is still left armed) — tracked separately, out of scope for this PR. **Post-review hardening (Codex P1) — order a due deadline ahead of an out-of-band child terminal:** a child that completes/fails **after** its deadline appends its terminal to the parent history out-of-band (via `wake_parent_for_child_completion`/`wake_parent_for_child_failure`), while the deadline `TimerFired` was otherwise only ingested at parent claim (`ingest_due_timers_and_signals`). If the parent was claimed late, the child terminal landed in history *before* the overdue `TimerFired`, so the pure recorded-order `match_child_or_timer` declared the child the winner and the primitive returned `Some`/`Err` instead of `None` — even though the deadline genuinely elapsed first (confirmed reproduced against real Postgres 16). Fixed in the wake path: a new `worker::materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines(conn, parent_exec_id)` materializes every currently-due `__child_timeout:` deadline as a `TimerFired` event **before** the child terminal is appended, in **both** wake functions, so the recorded order becomes `[.., TimerFired, ChildWorkflowCompleted|ChildWorkflowFailed]` and the race resolves to the timeout branch (`None`) — restoring the #476 "deadline reached ⇒ deadline won regardless of when the parent is claimed" guarantee for the child case. Correlation to the completing child is deliberately not required (this child's own due deadline lands before its terminal; an unrelated sibling race's due deadline landing early is resolved by that race's own scan). Scope is strictly the escaped-LIKE `\_\_child\_timeout:%` prefix, so unrelated `ctx.timer()` rows are never fired or reordered, and a child with no due deadline (plain child-await, or a child that beat its deadline) materializes nothing — **byte-identical** to the pre-fix wake path. Double-fire vs the parent-claim ingest is prevented by selecting the due rows `FOR UPDATE` (EvalPlanQual re-evaluates `fired = false` against the latest committed version, so a deadline already fired-and-committed by ingest is excluded, and a deadline this path fires blocks ingest's `SET fired = true` until the wake transaction commits). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to `match_child_or_timer` or `ingest_due_timers_and_signals` — the fix is contained to the child-wake path.** `match_child_or_timer`'s existing timer-win branch already consumes a loser child terminal recorded after the fire (via `consume_loser_child_terminal`, which handles both `ChildWorkflowCompleted` and `ChildWorkflowFailed`) and reports `child_already_terminal`, so no cancel command is pushed for the already-sealed loser. Tests, red→green (red confirmed by temporarily disabling the fix — the ordering assertion fails and the primitive returns `Some`): DB e2e `over_deadline_child_completion_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` + `over_deadline_child_failure_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (drive the REAL doc-hidden-`pub` wake functions over a hand-built overdue-timer prefix, assert the `[TimerFired, terminal]` history order + `None`), the focused helper test `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines_fires_only_due_child_timeout_timers` (fires exactly the due `__child_timeout` timer, leaves a not-yet-due one alone, ignores a due non-`__child_timeout` timer), and two context replay-determinism unit tests (`..._over_deadline_completion_loser_is_none`/`..._over_deadline_failure_loser_is_none` — the post-fix `[TimerFired, loser-terminal]` order resolves to `None` across 3 independent replay cycles). Verified green against a real local Postgres 16 (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox); Docker-run in CI. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — preserve the canary-at-frontier exception for in-flight replay:** the deploy replay canary (`run_workflow_canary`) samples still-running executions and expects a workflow parked at the recorded-history frontier to *suspend* → `ReplaySucceeded`. A workflow parked on `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` replays to `ChildOrTimerMatch::InProgress` at the frontier (the `ChildWorkflowStarted`/`TimerStarted` pair is recorded, but neither resolution is), and the primitive's `InProgress` arm unconditionally reported non-determinism whenever `strict_replay` was set — so healthy in-flight child-timeout workflows surfaced as *false* canary failures and could block deploy verification. Fixed by mirroring `check_strict_replay_no_match`'s existing canary-at-end exception exactly in the `InProgress` arm: the hard error is now suppressed only when `self.canary_mode && position >= len` (the recorded-history frontier), letting the arm fall through to re-park (which suspends). Genuine-divergence detection is untouched — a real code-vs-history divergence resolves as `ChildOrTimerMatch::Diverged` (a different arm that always nd-errors, never canary-excepted), and strict `WorkflowReplayer` runs (non-canary) still treat an unresolved race as a fixture problem. Contained to the context suspend branch: `match_child_or_timer`, `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`, `merge_wake_events`, and the Codex-P1 wake-path fix are all untouched; no new event variant, no migration. Tests, red→green (red confirmed as the exact `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildOrTimerResolved", actual="ChildOrTimerInProgress")` at the frontier): the money test `child_timeout_in_flight_canary_replays_succeeded` (in-flight history in canary → `ReplaySucceeded`) plus two mandatory guards — `child_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism` (same history in strict/non-canary → still non-determinism, the exception must not weaken strict) and `child_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary` (a child-input mismatch replayed in canary → still non-determinism, the exception must not mask real divergence) — all in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`. **Note:** `wait_for_signal_timeout` (#476) has the same latent behavior in its own `InProgress`/strict arm; left untouched here (a separate, shipped feature) and tracked as a follow-up. Verified via the no-DB `--features testing` replayer suites (Docker/testcontainers for the DB child_timeout suite unavailable in the implementing sandbox; the fix is pure replay and touches no worker/DB path). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — shard-encode the fresh child id:** the timeout child id was minted via `ExecutionId::new()` (the `ShardId::UNENCODED` sentinel), even though the child row is inserted into the **parent's** shard database (`persist_child_timeout_race` uses the parent's `conn` and stamps the parent `shard_id`). Shard-aware APIs route from `ExecutionId::shard()`, so a later lookup of that child id by shard (an unencoded sentinel → default shard) would target the wrong database on a non-default-shard parent. Fixed by minting the fresh id with the parent shard — `ExecutionId::new_for_shard(self.exec_id.shard())` — exactly as `spawn_child_workflow_detached_raw` already does. Replay-safe: the id is only minted on the first-live `NoMatch` path; on replay `match_child_or_timer` recovers the recorded `child_id` verbatim, so pre-fix in-flight children keep their unencoded ids and replay unchanged (both `new()` and `new_for_shard()` produce fresh v4 UUIDs, so determinism is identical). **Note:** the regular awaited `spawn_child_workflow_raw` shares the same latent unencoded-id minting (line ~4936) via the same `persist_all_started_child_workflows` insert; left untouched here (pre-existing, out of scope for #779) and flagged as a follow-up. **Post-review finding (Codex P2) — atomic child-timeout timer fire: REFUTED, no change.** The finding hypothesised that the P1 wake-path materializer (`materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines`), as a *second* deadline-fire path alongside the parent-claim ingest (`ingest_due_timers_and_signals`), could append a **duplicate** `TimerFired` when an overdue child completion races the parent being claimed. Confirmed against the real code and **refuted**: both fire paths append `TimerFired` **and** set `fired = true` **atomically in one transaction**, and `harvest_events` carries `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)`. When the ingest's unlocked `WHERE fired = false` SELECT sees the timer unfired, the materializer has not yet committed (its append + `fired = true` are atomic), so the ingest's stale `start_id` (= old `MAX + 1`) *equals* the materializer's own `MAX + 1` append id → the second append aborts on the unique constraint; when the materializer commits first, the ingest's `fired = false` SELECT (and a second materializer's `FOR UPDATE` re-select) excludes the row and appends nothing. A durable duplicate `TimerFired` is therefore impossible without any compare-and-set on the shared ingest path. Empirically verified against real Postgres 16: the finding's exact two-connection interleaving (materializer holds an uncommitted `TimerFired` at `event_id = K+1`; ingest, seeing `fired = false`, tries to append at its stale `start_id = K+1`) fails with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key"` and the ingest transaction aborts, leaving **exactly one** durable `TimerFired`; the exclusion ordering (`fired = true` first) leaves both writers' `WHERE fired = false` reads empty. The shared ingest/signal path is therefore **not** modified (a CAS there would risk the #476 signal / normal-timer fire path for zero observable benefit, since the event-id collision already coordinates). Regression guard added: `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines_is_idempotent_no_duplicate_timerfired` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) — a second materialize over an already-fired timer returns `0` and appends no second `TimerFired`. *(Observation, out of scope: the racing-collision ordering makes the ingest transaction roll back, which propagates through `fail_execution_on_error`; this is the pre-existing coordination shared with any concurrent `append_single_event` child-terminal writer, predates #779, and is not a duplicate.)* **Post-review hardening (Codex P2-C) — the extractor must require the reserved `__child_timeout:` prefix:** `extract_child_timeout_race` previously matched **any** batch of one `StartChildWorkflow` + one `StartTimer` + bookkeeping regardless of the timer id, so a hand-rolled `tokio::join!(ctx.spawn_child_workflow(..), ctx.timer("mytimer", n))` (one plain child + one ordinary timer) was silently treated as the child-timeout primitive — bypassing the previous fail-loud "unsupported commands" behavior, and on a child-win no `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` teardown would run to delete that ordinary timer row, so the parent could complete with an unfired `harvest_timers` dependency. Fixed: the extractor now additionally requires the `StartTimer`'s `timer_id` to begin with the new shared `context::CHILD_TIMEOUT_TIMER_PREFIX` (`"__child_timeout:"`, the exact prefix `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` stamps, now referenced by both the context's timer-id `format!` and the extractor so the two can't drift). A batch whose timer lacks the prefix returns `None` → falls through to the generic fail-loud path, exactly as before #779. The real primitive still matches (its timer always carries the prefix). Tests (extractor unit tests, `worker.rs`): a new `extract_child_timeout_race_requires_reserved_timer_prefix` asserts (a) a `__child_timeout:`-prefixed batch still matches and (b) a `child + ordinary-timer` batch is rejected, alongside the existing 2nd-child / 2nd-timer / extra-activity / WaitForSignal reject cases. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2-D) — materialize a due deadline before ALL out-of-band child-terminal appends, not just the worker wake path:** the P1 fix only ordered the overdue `__child_timeout:` deadline ahead of the child terminal in `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion`/`_failure`, but three OTHER out-of-band paths append a child terminal to a parent without going through those, so the over-deadline bug (returns `Some`/`Err` instead of `None`) persisted for them. **Full enumeration** of real DB append-to-parent child-terminal paths (child terminal recorded on the *parent's* history): (1) `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion` and (2) `worker::wake_parent_for_child_failure` — already fixed by P1; (3) `execution::notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` — the awaited-child operator **cancel** *and* **terminate** paths (its two callers, `cancel_workflow_execution` and `terminate_workflow_execution`); and (4) `timeout::wake_parent_for_child_timeout` — the child hitting its **own** execution timeout (its three callers: `commit_workflow_execution_timeout` + the two activity/external-timeout scanners). *(Read/simulation/replay sites in `simulator.rs`/`testing.rs`/`analyzer.rs`/`history_export.rs`/`timeline.rs`/`reset.rs` and the `context.rs` test fixtures do not append to a live parent's DB history and are out of scope.)* Fixed by calling the **same** helper `crate::worker::materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines(conn, parent_exec_id)` immediately before the child-terminal `append_single_event` in (3) and (4), under the same parent-row `FOR UPDATE` + `MAX(event_id)` discipline the P1 wake paths use — so an over-deadline child that is operator-cancelled, operator-terminated, or hits its own execution timeout also records `[.., TimerFired(deadline), ChildWorkflowFailed]` and the parent's `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` resolves to `None`. The helper was already `#[doc(hidden)] pub` in `crate::worker`; no move needed (minimal-churn visibility choice). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; the shared `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`/`merge_wake_events` fire path and `fail_execution_on_error` boundary are untouched.** Tests, red→green (red confirmed by temporarily neutralizing both new `materialize` calls — the ordering assertion fails, tail is `[.., ChildWorkflowFailed]` with no `TimerFired`): three DB e2e tests in `tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs` drive the REAL out-of-band entry points over a hand-built overdue-timer prefix with a real parent-linked child row — `over_deadline_child_operator_cancel_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `execution::cancel_workflow_execution`), `over_deadline_child_operator_terminate_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `execution::terminate_workflow_execution`), and `over_deadline_child_execution_timeout_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `timeout::enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts`) — each asserting the `[TimerFired(deadline), ChildWorkflowFailed]` tail order and that the primitive replays to `None`. Verified green (red→green) against a real local Postgres 16 (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox — the committed DB tests are compile-checked here via `cargo clippy --all-features --tests` and Docker-run in CI). **Post-review hardening (coordinator-approved, shared-path) — requeue the parent on a transient wake-event-ingest event-id conflict instead of terminally failing it:** the worker's wake-event ingest (`worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals`) appends `TimerFired`/`SignalReceived` at a `next_event_id` **precomputed from an earlier `load_history`**, with no execution-row lock and no `MAX(event_id)` recompute. When a concurrent `store::append_single_event` writer commits an event at that same `event_id` first, the ingest's batch insert hits `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` (`harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key`). That `Err` previously flowed through `fail_execution_on_error` and **terminally FAILED a healthy execution** on a transient, self-inflicted conflict — with no retry. This is a **pre-existing shared-path hazard** (the ingest's own comment already acknowledged it): it already affected the concurrent-`append_single_event` racers in `timeout.rs` / `external_task.rs`, and #779's `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` (the P1 fix) newly exercises it — a child completing late while the parent is claimed for its due `__child_timeout` deadline. **Fixed** by a precise classification at the ingest boundary: a UNIQUE violation on the events `(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` constraint is now treated as a **transient conflict → re-drive the parent workflow task** (park + wake, the existing pause/resume re-pend mechanism), not a terminal failure. No event is appended, no state is changed, no retry attempt is consumed. **Convergent in one retry, no hot loop:** the winner's event is already committed, so the re-driven task's fresh `load_history` advances `next_event_id` past it and an already-`fired` timer is excluded from the next ingest — the same conflict provably cannot recur. **Precise, non-over-broad classification:** new `HarvestError::is_event_id_unique_violation()` matches **only** that exact constraint name (verified on real Postgres 16 to be carried in the `HarvestError::Database` message) — a genuine/unrelated database error, or a UNIQUE violation on any *other* constraint, is unmatched and still fails as before (`error.rs` unit tests cover other-constraint / genuine-error / non-`Database`-variant rejection). The interception is scoped to the two ingest call sites (`load_workflow_replay_state` cache-miss + `prepare_workflow_task_with_cache` cache-hit), threaded up as an `Option` (`None` = requeued) so `process_workflow_task` returns `Ok(())` (task handled, re-claimed on the next poll) — mirroring the #383 pause and #603 nd-block re-park precedents. It uniformly protects the #476 signal fire, the normal `ctx.timer()` fire, and the #779 child-timeout fire — a transient event-id conflict should never terminally fail any run. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; the shared `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`/`merge_wake_events` fire logic and `fail_execution_on_error` boundary are otherwise untouched.** Tests, red→green (RED = with the classification reverted, the raw conflict propagates as a genuine `Err` and the parent is terminally FAILED; GREEN = requeued + clean re-drive): DB e2e `transient_event_id_conflict_requeues_parent_instead_of_failing` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) drives the REAL ingest at a stale `next_event_id` after a concurrent `append_single_event` committed that id, asserting (a) the raw error is classified as the transient conflict — the exact input the pre-fix path failed on, (b) `ingest_wake_events_or_requeue` returns `None` (re-driven, not failed), (c) the execution stays `RUNNING` with no `WorkflowFailed` event and the timer un-fired (ingest rolled back), (d) the parent task is re-pended `PENDING` and immediately claimable, and (e) a fresh re-claim + re-drive completes the ingest cleanly (`Some`, the due timer fires). Verified red→green against a **real local Postgres 16** (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox — the committed DB test is compile-checked here via `cargo clippy --all-features --tests` and Docker-run in CI); `error.rs` classifier unit tests RAN. `WorkflowTestEnv` exercises both branches deterministically without real sleeping (a resolving child mock → child branch; omitting it auto-fires the deadline timer). Example `examples/child_with_timeout.rs` (both branches via `WorkflowTestEnv`). Tests: `match_child_or_timer` matcher unit tests in `replay.rs` (child-win / timer-win / `child_already_terminal` / typed-child-failure / diverged / in-progress / interleaved-sibling transparency), context unit tests in `context.rs`, `extract_child_timeout_race`/predictor unit tests in `worker.rs`, `WorkflowReplayer` fixtures in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` (incl. 1,000 randomized child-vs-timer orderings, parallel to #476), `WorkflowTestEnv` harness tests, and Docker-backed DB e2e (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`: child completes before deadline → `Some`; child hangs → `None` + child sealed `CANCELLED`; child fails → typed `Err`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — advance `next_event_id` by the materialized-deadline count in the race-loser child-cancel path:** the P2-D deadline-materialization fix made `notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` append a **variable** number of events onto the parent's own history — the `ChildWorkflowFailed` terminal PLUS zero or more preceding `__child_timeout` `TimerFired` deadlines — but `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (the `ctx.race()` loser-teardown path, issue #600) still advanced its in-memory `next_event_id` cursor by a hardcoded `+1` after each genuinely-cancelled loser child. When a race loser child is cancelled **while another child-timeout deadline is due in the same workflow task**, the materializer appends the overdue `TimerFired` before the child terminal (N+1 events), so the caller's cursor was left short by N; the winner-marker / terminal-outcome / synthetic-loser `store::append_events` that the winner-persist path (`persist_terminal_outcome_commands` and the four other `apply_race_loser_cancellations` call sites) performs next then reused a consumed `event_id` and aborted on `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` (`harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key`) — rolling back and **wrongly failing the otherwise-healthy race-winning parent**. **Per-call-site audit** of every `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` caller: `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion`, `worker::wake_parent_for_child_failure`, and `timeout::wake_parent_for_child_timeout` all append the child terminal via `store::append_single_event` (which re-reads `MAX(event_id)+1` under the parent-row lock) and maintain **no** subsequent in-memory cursor → **safe**; `execution::notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` is itself internally safe (same `append_single_event`), but its only caller that both maintains a cursor *and* can append-to-self is `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (a race loser is always an awaited child of the racing execution) → **the single affected site**. The other four `cancel_workflow_execution_collect` callers (`persist_external_signal_inline`, the external-cancel outbox, and the two `TerminateIfRunning` pre-cancels) either cancel an arbitrary external target whose parent is not the cursor-maintaining execution, or are structurally unreachable for append-to-self (a parent parked on an awaited child cannot simultaneously be running its own decision cycle) → **safe**, no path outside the audited sites is affected. **Fixed** by replacing the hardcoded `+1` with a re-read of the true next id — new `store::next_event_id_for(conn, exec_id)` (`MAX(event_id)+1` under the same `FOR UPDATE` row lock `append_single_event` uses, which `notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal`'s append already holds), so the cursor re-synchronises to however many events were appended (1 + N), self-correcting for any future change to the child-terminal append count. **Byte-identical when N = 0** (a child race with no due deadline appends exactly the `ChildWorkflowFailed`, so the re-read returns the same value the `+1` did) — only the bug case (child-race loser + a concurrently-due `__child_timeout` deadline) changes. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; `match_child_or_timer`, the extractor, the payload-cap reorder, and the transient-conflict requeue are all untouched** — the fix is event-id accounting in the one race-loser call site plus a read-only store helper. Tests, red→green: DB e2e `race_loser_child_cancel_materializing_deadline_advances_event_id_past_all_appends` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) drives the REAL `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (now `#[doc(hidden)] pub`) over a parent with an overdue `__child_timeout` deadline + a real awaited RUNNING loser child, then performs the real subsequent winner-terminal `append_events` at the returned cursor — RED (revert to `+1`): the cursor is `4` (still pointing at the `ChildWorkflowFailed` id) and the terminal append fails on `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key"`; GREEN: the cursor is `5` and the parent history is gap-free `[WorkflowStarted, ChildWorkflowStarted, TimerStarted, TimerFired, ChildWorkflowFailed, WorkflowCompleted]`. Verified red→green against a **real local Postgres 16** (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox; Docker-run in CI). **Test-infra fix shipped alongside:** the P2-D real-child helper `setup_parent_racing_overdue_real_child` inserted the parent and child with the *same* hardcoded `workflow_id` (via two `insert_workflow_execution` calls), colliding on the partial `UNIQUE(workflow_name, workflow_id)` active index — so the three P2-D real-child DB tests (operator-cancel/terminate/execution-timeout) could never actually execute. Added `insert_workflow_execution_with_id(conn, workflow_id)` and gave the child a distinct id, unblocking those three tests (now confirmed green on real PG 16) plus the new one; the whole `child_timeout_tests.rs` DB suite (15 tests) was pointed at the new env-honoring `setup_test_database_url_or_env` helper (identical container path when `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset, per the `retention_overrides_tests.rs` precedent) so it runs locally and Docker-backed in CI. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — check the child-input payload cap BEFORE the replay matcher so cap-failure histories replay deterministically:** `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` previously called `match_child_or_timer` first and only enforced the child-input cap inside the `NoMatch | InProgress` arm. On a live **over-cap** call the child is never dispatched, so no child/timer events are recorded and the run terminates as `WorkflowFailed` (propagate) or continues after catching the error. On **replay** of that history the cursor sits on the next real event (`WorkflowFailed`, or a caught-and-continued activity/completion), not a recorded `ChildWorkflowStarted`, so `match_child_or_timer` returned `Diverged` and the call reported a spurious `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildWorkflowStarted", actual="WorkflowFailed")` instead of reproducing the same `PayloadTooLarge`. Fixed by moving the cap check to the **top** of the method, before the matcher — the cap decision is a pure function of the deterministic input size + the (normally stable) `payload_max_workflow_input`, so it must run first. The check is gated to a fresh dispatch via a new **read-only** `HistoryMatcher::peek_child_start_at_cursor` (mirroring the fan-out's `peek_fan_out_count` marker peek, and its skip set — consumed indices + leading early-drainable signal/external-signal/external-cancel/update events — so it agrees with where `prepare_match` will land): an already-recorded child (under-cap at record time) is never re-judged against a possibly-changed cap, and the redundant inner cap check was removed. **For every under-cap input this is byte-identical to the prior behavior** — the top cap check is a no-op and the matcher proceeds exactly as before; only over-cap inputs change, now failing fast before the matcher on both live and replay. Scope (config-stable, honest): the cap decision reads the live `payload_max_workflow_input`, so replay-consistency holds when the cap is stable (the normal case) — this does **not** claim replay-safety across a cap change, matching the documented fan-out `validate_child_payload_caps` limitation. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; `match_child_or_timer` resolution logic, the extractor, the deadline-materializer, and the transient-conflict fix are all untouched** — the change is a pure reorder within `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` plus one read-only matcher helper. Tests, red→green (red confirmed by reverting the reorder — both new tests fail with the exact `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildWorkflowStarted(process_order)", actual="WorkflowFailed")`): `child_timeout_oversized_input_caught_replays_succeeded` (fresh over-cap input caught + continued → `ReplaySucceeded`, reproducing `PayloadTooLarge` instead of diverging on the `WorkflowCompleted` at the cursor) and `child_timeout_oversized_input_propagated_replays_deterministically` (fresh over-cap input propagated → deterministic `WorkflowFailed` carrying the `PayloadTooLarge` message across 2 cycles, asserting the error is NOT a history-matcher divergence) in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`; the existing `child_timeout_oversized_input_rejected` (cap fires before any command on a fresh live call) and all child-win / timer-win / canary fixtures stay green. Verified via the no-DB `--features testing` replayer/lib suites (the fix is pure replay and touches no worker/DB path).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Address existing workflows by business `workflow_id` over HTTP — see issue #805. Embedders assign their own business `workflow_id` at start (e.g. `order-12345`, `subscription:user-42`), but every act-on-existing management route (`GET /workflows/{id}`, `/result`, `POST .../signal/{name}`, `/query/{name}`, `/cancel`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/stack`, `/children`) previously accepted only the internal `exec_id` UUID (`parse_execution_id` rejects anything else). Acting on a workflow you already named required a list-then-act round-trip, and a cached `exec_id` is a **stale handle** — continue-as-new and reset fork a **new** `exec_id` under the **same** `workflow_id`, so code that pinned an `exec_id` can silently signal or read a terminal predecessor instead of the live run. This shipped a **business-id form** addressed by `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` alongside the existing `exec_id` routes, which stay **byte-for-byte backward compatible**. **New routes** (prefix `P = /workflows/by-id/{workflow_name}/{workflow_id}`): `GET P` (describe), `GET P/result`, `GET P/stack`, `GET P/children`, `POST P/signal/{signal_name}`, `GET P/query/{query_name}`, `POST P/query/{query_name}`, `POST P/cancel`, `POST P/pause`, `POST P/resume`. Each **resolves** `(workflow_name, workflow_id) → ExecutionId` then **delegates** to the existing `exec_id` handler (no existing handler body changed), so admin posture and audit classification mirror the `exec_id` counterparts exactly: `cancel`/`pause`/`resume` carry the same `require_admin` route layer and `OP_WORKFLOW_CANCEL`/`OP_WORKFLOW_PAUSE`/`OP_WORKFLOW_RESUME` audit ops; `signal` is `OP_WORKFLOW_SIGNAL`; describe/result/stack/children/query are `ReadOnly` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. **Resolution rule (AC2):** the single **active** (non-terminal — `RUNNING`/`PAUSED`) run if one exists; otherwise the **most recent terminal** run by `started_at`; otherwise `404` (never `500`). Well-defined because at most one active run exists per `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` (the per-shard partial unique index). `workflow_name` is **required** (AC3): both path segments are mandatory, so a bare `workflow_id` never matches a by-id route. **AC4 — the resolved `execution_id` is always returned:** every by-id response carries it in the `X-Harvest-Execution-Id` header (uniform, covers empty-body cases like `/result`'s `204`), and in the JSON body wherever one exists — `signal`/`query` responses are re-wrapped to add a top-level `execution_id`; `cancel`/`pause`/`resume` already carry it; `describe`/`stack` carry it nested; `result`/`children` surface it via the header. **Shard strategy — always fan out.** `resolve_workflow_by_business_id` (plugin) fans out across `iter_shards()` rather than trusting a single rendezvous-hash fast path: `ShardRouter::pick_for_new_workflow` can drift from where a run actually lives once the writable shard subset changes, so a fast-path-then-miss design could resolve a live run to `404`. Resolution is not a hot path and the single-shard default is exactly one query. Per-shard candidates are merged by the pure `select_resolved_run`. **Core (`autumn-harvest/src/execution.rs`, db-gated), no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — resolution is read-only over the existing `UNIQUE (workflow_name, workflow_id)` index. New `ResolvedRun { exec_id, state, started_at }`; pure, no-DB, unit-tested `select_resolved_run(Vec<ResolvedRun>) -> Option<ResolvedRun>` (active-first, else most-recent-terminal, using `erase::is_terminal_state` so classification cannot drift — guarded by `resolve_terminal_states_matches_is_terminal_state`); shard-local `resolve_execution_id_by_workflow_id(conn, name, id)` (active-first query, else most-recent overall). Both re-exported from `lib.rs`. **Registration surfaces:** all 10 routes registered in `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_request_fields()` (signal free-form, query POST `args`, cancel/pause `reason`, resume empty), `management_api_response_fields()` (describe/result/stack/children free-form; signal/query/cancel/pause/resume structured incl. `execution_id`), `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` + `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` for the read-only ones). Docs: new "Addressing workflows by business id" section in `docs/management-api.md` (resolution semantics, required-name rule, always-present `execution_id`, shard-aware note, continue-as-new note). **Tests:** pure `select_resolved_run` unit tests in `execution.rs` (empty/single/active-wins-over-terminals/most-recent-terminal/paused-active/sealed-terminal/two-actives-defensive/drift-guard); plugin HTTP integration `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/by_id_integration.rs` (describe 200 + header/body execution_id match, unknown `(name,id)` → 404 not 500, malformed exec-id on the old route still 400, signal lands + execution_id in body/header, cancel + `401` unauthenticated, **continue-as-new correctness** — resolves to the RUNNING successor not the sealed predecessor, all-terminal resolves to the COMPLETED run, exec-id route unchanged); `contract_regression.rs` `*_route_is_classified` pins for every by-id route; one sorted line in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`. DB/HTTP integration tests are compile-checked in-sandbox and executed against a local Postgres 16 where available; the pure unit tests run under `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --lib`.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission gate authoritative on the single-start throttle route — see issue #607. **Post-review hardening (Codex P1):** the committed-prior idempotent-retry bypass added below was **policy-blind** — it treated *any* non-sealed prior as an attach, matching `AllowDuplicate` unconditionally. But `reuse_policy = allow_duplicate_failed_only` over a `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` prior, and `terminate_if_running` over any prior, actually **create** a fresh (replacement) execution, so bypassing the gate on the token-empty `Deferred` path let a fresh replacement start slip an armed gate (the deferred row fires gate-less at the next scanner tick). Fixed by making the committed-prior bypass **reuse-policy-aware**: it now loads the prior's *state* (same non-sealed filter the authoritative locked gate uses) and bypasses only when `execution::start_will_create_new_execution(prior_state, reuse_policy)` is `false` (attach or `AlreadyExists`) — the exact predicate the core locked gate (`GateMode::Check`) keys on. A create-on-retry policy now correctly faces the gate → `503`. The `has_pending_throttle_for_workflow_id` bypass (an already-durably-deferred retry) is unchanged (it is orthogonal to the reuse policy). Regression test `armed_gate_blocks_fresh_creating_start_under_reuse_policy_on_empty_bucket` (armed gate + empty bucket + `allow_duplicate_failed_only`/FAILED and `terminate_if_running`/RUNNING → `503` + zero pending throttle rows; plus an `allow_duplicate`/attach no-over-block guard). The **batch route** (`POST /workflows/batch`) inherits the same policy-blind heuristic and is tracked separately in **#1053** (out of scope for this PR). Production bug fix. The single-start workflow-start route (`POST /workflows/{name}/start`) has a throttle branch (issue #607) that, when a throttled workflow's token bucket is empty, durably **defers** the start and returns `202 Accepted` — and it did so **before** any admission-gate check. The admission gate (#377 / #618, PR #1014) is a "halt starts during an incident" control that must win over throttle's "pace starts" control (`"halt beats pace"`): PR #1014 wired `gate_cache().check()` into the debounce branch and the batch route, and made the plain/keyed start gate-check authoritatively inside the core start primitive (`GateMode::Check`), but a throttle DEFER returns `202` from this branch and never reaches that core create path — so a genuinely-new throttled start submitted while a gate was armed silently slipped it (`202` instead of `503`). The fix adds the gate check in the single-start throttle branch, **before `reserve_or_defer`**, mirroring the batch route exactly — including its two idempotent-retry bypasses (an explicit caller-supplied `workflow_id` whose start already committed as an active execution, matching `AllowDuplicate`; or one already durably deferred in `harvest_start_throttle`, via `throttle::has_pending_throttle_for_workflow_id`) — so #808 keyed-replay and idempotent retries are **not** regressed (a retry of a committed or already-deferred start still gets its idempotent `202`, only a genuinely-new fresh start under an armed gate becomes `503`), reusing the same `record_admission_blocked` + `503 {"error":"admission blocked","gate_id","reason"}` response the debounce/batch branches emit. **Behavior change:** a fresh throttled start under an armed admission gate now returns `503` instead of `202`. Throttle semantics are otherwise unchanged (gate open → defer `202` exactly as before). `start_throttle_integration` was moved off the `ci_run_coverage` allowlist onto a `linux` CI run row in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`, so the throttle-vs-gate contract now runs against live Docker Postgres. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no test changes** (the existing `retry_with_a_pending_throttle_row_bypasses_the_admission_gate` test was already correct). Surfaced by the #1045 diagnosis of the 202-vs-503 discrepancy on this route.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Fix race-primitive canary replay false-positive on interleaved bookkeeping siblings — see issue #1048. A canary replay of an in-flight `wait_for_signal_timeout` (#476) or `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` (#779) race started concurrently with a bookkeeping side effect — e.g. `tokio::join!(race, async { ctx.side_effect(...) })` — incorrectly reported the run as `NonDeterminismDetected`, spuriously failing deploy-safety canary checks even though the workflow is fine and merely still parked on the race. Root cause: both race primitives carried a byte-identical inline "canary-frontier guard" that decided non-determinism from inside the race matcher by reading whether the cursor was at the frontier (`!has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed()`). But on an `InProgress` result the matcher **rewinds** the cursor to the interleaved sibling command so the sibling's own matcher can consume its event — so the guard read "not at frontier" (the sibling's `SideEffectRecorded` was momentarily unconsumed) and false-fired, poll-order-dependently, before the sibling future ran. Fixed by deleting both inline guards in `context.rs` **symmetrically** (avoiding the twin↔sibling asymmetry the issue calls out) and deferring the `InProgress` decision to the executor's already-wired end-of-cycle authority: `history_has_unconsumed_events()` in `run_workflow_canary`, and `outcome_to_report`'s `Suspended` mapping for strict replay. That authority runs *after* all joined siblings have consumed their rewound events, so a clean parked race reads no unconsumed events (→ `ReplaySucceeded`) while a genuine leftover is still caught (→ `NonDeterminismDetected`). The `Diverged` arms are untouched — a real divergence always errors. **Live-worker no-op:** the guards' load-bearing `return Err` was `strict_replay`-gated, so the live worker / crash-recovery replay (`strict_replay = false`) never executed it; the guard's `match_history` read that did run live was a redundant duplicate of the race matcher's own post-hook `pump_signal_handlers`, so its removal drops no signal-handler dispatch. **Diagnostic granularity:** a genuinely-parked race under strict `WorkflowReplayer` now surfaces the generic executor `NonDeterminismDetected` ("workflow suspended before all history events were replayed") rather than the old specific `SignalOrTimerResolved`/`ChildOrTimerResolved` message (status unchanged; no test asserted the old strings). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no production/live-worker behavior change.** Tests (all no-DB, `--features testing`, in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`): AC1 canary-plus-interleaved-bookkeeping-sibling → `ReplaySucceeded` for both primitives (`signal_timeout_in_flight_with_bookkeeping_sibling_canary_replays_succeeded`, `child_timeout_in_flight_with_bookkeeping_sibling_canary_replays_succeeded`, both new red-first repros); AC2 strict-parked-race still errors (`signal_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism`, `child_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism`), genuine `Diverged` under canary still errors (`signal_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary`, `child_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary`), and the deferral does not blind canary to a genuine `InProgress` leftover (`signal_timeout_in_flight_genuine_leftover_event_still_detected_in_canary`, `child_timeout_in_flight_genuine_leftover_event_still_detected_in_canary`, both new); AC3 fixed symmetrically (both inline guards deleted identically, every test row present for both twins). Full local CI mirror green: fmt, clippy `--all-features --tests -D warnings` and `--no-default-features --features testing`, `--test integration` (949 passed), `--lib` (1563 passed).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission-gate hardening: throttle fire-time gate + reuse-policy-aware batch bypass — see issue #1053. Consolidated admission-gate (#377 / #618 / #1014) hardening follow-up split out of PR #1051's review. Two pieces, each carrying its own contract decision. **(1) Throttle scanner now honors the admission gate at fire time — deliberate contract change.** A deferred throttle start (issue #607) creates no execution at defer time — it persists a `harvest_start_throttle` row and returns `202`. The actual create-vs-attach commits later in the scanner (`throttle::fire_claimed_throttle_row`), which previously called `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect(..., gate: None)` — gate-exempt by construction (the deliberate #618-F1 `GatedAtAdmission` exemption). **Before:** a throttled start deferred while no gate was armed would fire the instant its tokens refilled, *even if an operator had since armed an admission gate on its scope* — the last deferred-fire leak past an active gate. **After:** the scanner passes `Some(GateMode::CheckCached)` and re-checks the gate on the workflow's real queue immediately before firing. When a gate matches it **blocks and RE-DEFERS** the row: it leaves the `harvest_start_throttle` row in place, **refunds** the token it reserved for the attempt, starts nothing, counts `harvest.admission.blocked`, and bumps the row's `deferred_at` forward by a modest backoff (`GATE_REDEFER_BACKOFF`, 5s) — so the held start fires the instant the gate opens. This reverses the #618-F1 exemption: the throttle deferred-start `202` now means *"will run when tokens allow **AND** the admission gate is open at fire time"*, not merely *"will run when tokens allow"* — the correct halt-beats-pace semantics for an operator slamming a gate mid-incident. **A gate block never drops a start** — the row is re-deferred, not deleted. **One pre-existing, orthogonal caveat holds unchanged:** a start given a `schedule_to_start` deadline (issue #607 AC-c) that is held under a gate *past that deadline* is still dropped as stale (the row is deleted, a `warn!` is logged) exactly as it would be for any other reason it missed its deadline — the gate does not exempt a start from its own staleness bound, and (because the gate can hold a start until its deadline elapses) a long-armed gate makes such staleness drops materially more likely. The staleness drop is emitted on a `warn!` log only (no dedicated metric today). **Re-defer backoff — cross-key fairness (review finding B-G1).** A gate is **queue-scoped**, so the SQL candidate pre-filter that selects the tick's fire batch cannot see it (it only knows token levels and `schedule_to_start` expiry). Without bumping `deferred_at`, a gate-blocked-but-tokened row keeps its original (older) `deferred_at`, stays the oldest candidate in the `ORDER BY deferred_at ASC` fire ordering, and is re-selected every tick; ≥100 such rows gated together (a queue-wide incident gate over many tenant keys on one shard) would monopolize the fixed-size fire batch and **starve newer un-gated throttle keys on other queues** until the gate lifts — reopening the exact cross-key fairness pathology the per-key cap + token pre-filter (#607) closed. Bumping `deferred_at` forward on re-defer rotates a gated row *behind* every un-gated row, so un-gated keys fire first and a gated row is re-attempted less often. Because the re-defer is per-tick, `harvest.admission.blocked` for throttle reflects re-defer **attempt volume** (at-least-once per gated row per tick), not distinct blocked rows — unlike the completion-trigger cross-shard outbox relay, which drops on block and so counts once per row (the block log was also demoted to `debug!` to avoid a per-tick flood). **Producer contract flip.** `throttle` moves from `gated_at_admission` to `gated_at_relay` at `GET /admin/gates` (`admission_gate::producer_contract`). It shares the `check_cached` relay-time mechanism with the completion-trigger cross-shard outbox (also `GatedAtRelay`) but **differs in disposition**: the completion-trigger outbox **drops** its row on block (its source terminal decision has already fired, so a permanently gated relay must not accumulate forever); the throttle scanner **re-defers** its row (its `202` "nothing lost" promise). A blocked fire counts `harvest.admission.blocked` and a genuinely-fired start counts `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer="throttle"}` — never both (block-vs-bypass never double-counts). `debounce` and `event_batch` **remain** `gated_at_admission` — #1053 scopes only throttle. **Coverage.** Closes BOTH (a) the pre-existing looseness where ANY deferred throttle start fires gate-exempt if the gate arms after deferral, and (b) the narrow PR-#1051 residual — an attach-policy bypass whose prior is force-terminated between the unlocked read and the scanner fire, so the deferred fire becomes a fresh CREATE. (b) is a subset of (a): every deferred fire now faces the fire-time gate; force-terminate is merely what turns a would-be attach into a would-be CREATE. **(2) Batch route reuse-policy-aware bypass (structural / defensive).** The batch-start Phase-1 idempotent-retry pre-check (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) previously bypassed the admission gate on a bare "any non-sealed prior exists" existence boolean. **After:** it loads the prior's *state* and decides the bypass with `execution::start_will_create_new_execution(prior_state, AllowDuplicate)`, mirroring the single-start route fixed in #1051. **No behavior change today** — the batch route starts every item under `AllowDuplicate` (`BatchStartItem` has no reuse-policy field), so the predicate agrees with the old existence boolean for every prior state — but it stays correct if a per-item reuse policy is ever added, and the throttled batch item's real residual is closed by (1) since a deferred batch item fires through the same `fire_claimed_throttle_row` scanner. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** A blocked fire rolls the start transaction back (no row, no events), so there is no replay surface. The metrics recorder is now threaded through `fire_claimed_throttle_row` / `fire_due_on_conn` (mirroring `debounce` / `event_batch`) so the fire-time block is counted on the passed recorder rather than only the process-global fallback. Tests: `throttle_scanner_re_defers_under_a_closed_gate_and_fires_when_open` (money — block+re-defer under a closed gate, fire once open), `throttle_row_deferred_before_gate_is_held_when_gate_arms_before_fire` (coverage (a)), `throttle_deferred_fire_over_a_force_terminated_prior_faces_the_gate` (coverage (b)), `batch_gate_bypasses_an_attaching_item_but_blocks_a_would_be_fresh_create` (batch gate-bypass decision regression-lock; renamed + strengthened by the #1085 heal — was `batch_bypass_uses_start_will_create_predicate_not_bare_existence`, whose runtime assertion never ran under Docker-only CI); four existing tests flipped from the old "fires despite the gate" contract to the new fire-time-gate contract.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Read-only operator role for least-privilege triage access — see issue #776. Promotes `autumn_harvest::audit`'s route classification from "used for audit" to also "used for authz": a **read-only operator role** an embedder enables in **one builder call**. A principal the embedder marks read-only reaches **100%** of `RouteClass::ReadOnly` routes but receives **403 Forbidden** on **every** `Mutating` management route **and every mutating MCP tool** (see *Post-review hardening* below) — for exposing triage/status dashboards to support/on-call users without granting the mutate-everything credential, replacing "write a custom reverse proxy" with a single call. **Enforcement = one opt-in, class-aware tower layer** (`enforce_read_only_class`, `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) installed on `harvest_api_router` **only** under the new `HarvestPlugin::api_with_role_auth(path, middleware)`. Driven **purely** by `autumn_harvest::audit::CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` — the single source of truth, so there is no second hand-maintained mutating-route list to drift (AC3). Keys on `request.method()` + the nest-stripped `request.uri().path()`, matched via **`matchit`** (the radix-tree matcher axum itself uses) built once into a per-method `HashMap<Method, matchit::Router<RouteClass>>` with **positional param normalization** (`{id}`→`{p0}`) so a single router accepts the full template set without a name conflict, preserving **static-beats-param precedence** (`POST /workflows/batch_start` is never mistaken for the `ReadOnly` `/workflows/{id}` — a privilege-escalation bug if wrong). Deliberately **not** `axum::extract::MatchedPath`, which is unreliable when read from a layer on a nested router (axum #1441) — the exact position this layer occupies. Classification keys on the route class, **never the HTTP verb**: the two `ReadOnly` POST routes (`POST /workflows/{id}/query/{query_name}`, `POST /admin/build-routing/retire`) are correctly reachable. **Pure decision fn (core `audit.rs`):** `deny_readonly_mutation(is_readonly, class) -> bool` = `is_readonly && !matches!(class, ReadOnly | PublicSafe)`. **Fail closed by construction:** the matcher resolves an unmatched path / unknown method to `RouteClass::Mutating`, so a route a contributor forgot to classify is denied to read-only principals — never silently exposed (AC4). Pinned by a truth-table unit test. **Read-only principal predicate (`has_harvest_readonly_access`):** true iff the autumn-web `Session` carries an explicit read-only marker (`role` ∈ {`harvest_readonly`,`harvest_operator`,`operator`,`readonly`,`read_only`} or a truthy `is_harvest_readonly`/`is_harvest_operator`) **and** no explicit admin marker (`role` ∈ {`admin`,`harvest_admin`} or truthy `is_harvest_admin`/`is_admin`). Admin marker present, no session, or no marker → `false` (full access — the read-only restriction is opt-in per principal, preserving existing boundary semantics; documented contract that the embedder must explicitly mark a principal read-only). **Opt-in (`HarvestPlugin::api_with_role_auth`):** mirrors `api_with_auth` (sets `api_path` + the embedder auth middleware, which makes `admin_auth_boundary = true`) **and** sets a new `role_auth_enabled` flag on `HarvestApiState` (mirrored from the plugin builder in `build()`, same `Arc<Mutex<bool>>` setter/getter pattern as `set_decode_payloads_on_read`). In `build()`, when role-auth is enabled the class layer is installed on the combined router **before** the embedder middleware wraps it, so the request order is: embedder auth mw (sets `Session`) → class layer (enforce) → per-route `require_admin` (a no-op under the boundary) → handler. **Because `admin_auth_boundary = true`, per-route `require_admin` and the SSE in-handler admin check pass for the read-only principal → AC1 is satisfied with NO router/SSE surgery.** This is safe: the class layer 403s a read-only principal at the route boundary *before* any handler's in-handler admin write-gate runs, and every state-writing handler sits on a `Mutating` (or unclassified→fail-closed→`Mutating`) route. The only extra capability the boundary grants a read-only principal is **READS** (payload decode #608, the SSE event stream) — explicitly scoped out by the issue (verb restriction, not field/row restriction). **`api_with_auth` and the default `api(path)` mount are byte-for-byte unchanged (AC6):** the class layer is installed *only* under `api_with_role_auth`; `role_auth_enabled` defaults off. **403, not 401 (AC2):** a read-only principal on a `Mutating` route gets `403 Forbidden` (`{"error":"read-only principal: mutation not permitted"}`), distinct from the anonymous `401` the admin gate returns, built directly (no dependency on an autumn-web `forbidden` helper). **Observability (AC7):** every denial emits `tracing::warn!(method, path, "harvest: read-only principal denied mutation (403)")`; a best-effort DB audit row is deliberately *not* written (the layer runs before a pooled connection is acquired; forcing a write on every probe would be a DoS vector). The stable 403 body marker is also a distinguishable signal. **Classification scope (the largest work item):** 31 routes were mounted in `harvest_api_router` but had drifted without a `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` entry — **8 Mutating** (`update-with-start`, `dag runs/{}/retry`, circuit `force-open`/`force-close`, `POST /admin/completion-triggers`, `POST /calendars`, `PUT /calendars/{name}`, `DELETE /calendars/{name}`) and **23 ReadOnly** (`batches/pending`, `workflows/registered`(+/`{name}`/schema), the two `workflows/by-id/{workflow_name}` 400-stubs, `workflows/types/{name}/handlers`, `dead-letters/aggregate`, `admin/circuits`(+/`{name}`), `admin/queues/scaling`, `admin/metrics`, `admin/completion-triggers` GET, `admin/schedules/{id}`(+/runs+/decisions+/preview), `admin/schedules/decisions`, `POST /admin/schedules/preview`, `calendars` GET(+/`{name}`), `workers/{id}/pinned`, `admin/queues/{queue}/eligibility`, `admin/tasks/{id}/eligibility`). Each Mutating handler was verified to write state; each ReadOnly handler verified not to (privilege-escalation guard). The 4 circuit/dag/update ops reuse pre-existing constants (`OP_WORKFLOW_UPDATE_WITH_START`, `OP_DAG_RETRY`, `OP_CIRCUIT_FORCE_OPEN`, `OP_CIRCUIT_FORCE_CLOSE`) that had never been registered in `AUDITED_OPERATIONS` — now wired, with `Some(op)` manifest entries; the calendar + completion-trigger CRUD (no op constant, audit wiring out of scope) use `None` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` and `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` stay size-synced (137 each); the 3 router-only routes (`/handlers` + the two by-id missing-id stubs) were added to `management_api_routes()` and `docs/api-contract.json` so the coverage sweep and contract parity cover them. **Deviation from the issue's literal wording:** AC8 says the change is "confined to the `autumn-harvest-plugin` auth/router layer", but `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`/`ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES`/`AUDITED_OPERATIONS`/`EXCLUDED_ROUTES` live in the **core crate** `autumn-harvest/src/audit.rs`, so classifying the drifted routes necessarily edits core (const arrays + `#[cfg(test)]` tests). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism impact, no `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path change** — so it is allowed, but the "plugin-only" claim is inaccurate (flagged for spec-owner review). **Known limitation (documented follow-up):** the nested `/ui` sub-router's paths are not in `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`, so under fail-closed enforcement a read-only principal receives 403 on `/ui`. Admins reach `/ui` unchanged. Classifying the UI routes so read-only principals can view (but not act through) the dashboard is a follow-up. **Read-capability breadth** is also out of scope by design: a read-only principal, mounted behind the auth boundary, gets admin-level *reads* (payload decode #608, the SSE stream) — this slice restricts verbs, not fields or rows. **Post-review hardening (three-reviewer pass):** **BLOCKER (F1) — MCP mutating tools were an unguarded write surface.** The generated MCP tool routes (issue #597) are registered app-level (via `AppBuilder::routes`), **outside** the nested management router the `enforce_read_only_class` layer wraps, so under `mcp_tools() + api_with_role_auth()` a read-only principal could start / signal / update / dag-start a workflow through a tool — via the tool's direct HTTP path OR the `/mcp` JSON-RPC `tools/call` envelope (autumn-web re-dispatches it through the same route). Closed by threading `role_auth_enabled` into `build_mcp_tool_routes` → `build_tool_route` and gating every mutating tool (`ToolKind::is_mutation()` — `Start`/`DagStart`/`Signal`/`Update`) with the new `enforce_read_only_mcp_mutation` layer (403 for read-only principals), applied *inner* of the embedder auth layer so the Session is populated before the gate reads it. Read tools (`Status`/`Watch`) stay reachable. One gate closes both invocation paths. Off when `api_with_role_auth` is not used. **F2 — read-only detection failed OPEN on case mismatch.** `has_harvest_readonly_access` matched markers case-sensitively, so `role="ReadOnly"`/`"READONLY"` fell through to full access. Now normalizes claim VALUES (trim + lowercase) and accepts `true`/`1`/`yes`/`on` case-insensitively; admin-marker detection normalized too so "admin wins" is case-robust. **F3 — HEAD/OPTIONS over-restriction.** `classify_route` now maps `HEAD → GET`'s class (axum serves HEAD via GET), and the layer lets `OPTIONS` pass, so a read-only principal can HEAD-probe reads and a cookie-bearing CORS preflight is not 403'd. **F4 — matcher build no longer panics.** A future post-normalization route collision logs an error and degrades fail-closed (the route stays unclassified → `Mutating` → denied) instead of panicking the first read-only request; a `debug_assert` keeps the build-time CI guard. **F8 / vestigial flag.** The Session `role` claim is fetched once (was twice). The write-only `HarvestApiState::role_auth_enabled` mirror (set but never read — enforcement gates on the plugin `build()` var) was removed so no misleading flag remains. **M2 — contract read_only cross-check.** `docs/api-contract.json`'s `read_only` bool was a second read/mutate source never compared to `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`. Reconciled the one pre-existing drift (`POST /admin/build-routing/retire` is `ReadOnly` but was `read_only:false`) and added `contract_read_only_flag_matches_classified_routes` to guard the two sources. - **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Workflow start provenance (`StartSource`) across every start path — see issue #740. **Implemented.** Every workflow execution now durably records *what created it, and from where* — the answer that previously required reverse-engineering `workflow_id` prefixes (`sched:…`) and hand-walking `parent_id`. A new bounded `StartSource` enum (`types.rs`, non-`db`-gated; snake_case serialization; `from_str` falls back to `unknown` and **never errors**) is threaded through `StartWorkflowParams` and `NewWorkflowExecution` and stamped at construction on every start path: schedule tick / backfill / manual trigger-now / Vantage UI trigger → `schedule` / `backfill` (both non-throttled workflow **and** DAG branches, plus the throttled/deferred branch) / manual-trigger with `start_source_ref = schedule_id` and `started_by = operator`; `signal_with_start` / `update_with_start`; completion-trigger (inline + deferred + cross-shard outbox), `start_source_ref = triggering source exec id`; child (fan-out / single / detached), `start_source_ref = parent exec id`; `continue_as_new` — records its **own** `continue_as_new` source (with `start_source_ref = predecessor`), never misattributed as a fresh `api` start (falsified in test by stamping the predecessor a *distinct* `schedule` source and asserting the successor does not inherit it); `reset` — own `reset` source + `start_source_ref = source exec id`; batch (immediate + throttle-carrier branches); generic outbox; inbound webhook (override via `StartWorkflowParams::from_webhook`); the deferred throttle / debounce / batch paths — source is captured at **admission** and restored at **fire** time from the JSONB start-options carrier; workflow-level retry — **inherits** the predecessor's source, so a retried scheduled run stays `schedule`. Pre-upgrade rows report `unknown`. **Storage.** Three additive nullable columns (`start_source`, `start_source_ref`, `started_by`) plus a partial index on `harvest_workflow_executions` (migration `20260712000000_harvest_execution_start_source`), with **no backfill**. The read struct serializes NULL `start_source` as `"unknown"` and omits `start_source_ref` / `started_by` when absent. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant** and no change to the adjacently-tagged event JSON: provenance lives on a row column that is never read on replay, so the value is **replay-safe by construction** and immutable once frozen at start. **Read / query surface.** `GET /workflows?start_source=` filter applied at **both** the standard (`load_workflows`) and stalled (`load_stalled_workflows`) loaders (mirroring the `sla_breached` / `nd_blocked` / `legal_hold` predicates), fanned across shards: an invalid value returns a `400` JSON error (never `500`, never a silent empty match); `?start_source=unknown` matches NULL/pre-upgrade rows via `IS NULL OR = 'unknown'`; a blank `?start_source=` is treated as absent (no filter), matching the `state` / `workflow_name` / `owner` siblings; omitting the param preserves today's behavior. AC4 read-path surfacing on the describe/details API and list rows is automatic (the `WorkflowExecution` read struct is serialized directly). CLI: `harvest workflow list --start-source <value>` + describe passthrough. `docs/api-contract.json` gains the `start_source` param entry. Operator triage stanza added to `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md` (find the culprit mechanism during a spawn-storm with one call). **Tests.** AC3 enumeration directly asserts the recorded `start_source` (and predecessor ref for `continue_as_new` / `reset`) for every listed start path, driven via public entrypoints where reachable and the module-local worker harness for the engine-internal insert paths (`continue_as_new`, `child`) — RED→GREEN against Postgres; backfill is asserted through `POST /admin/schedules/{id}/backfill` in the plugin suite (this direct assertion uncovered and fixed a real gap where the two non-throttled backfill branches still carried the neutral `api` placeholder). Filter/describe HTTP integration tests: filter narrows results (proves exclusion), `?start_source=unknown` matches NULL rows, invalid → `400`, absent ref/`started_by` omitted; deferred-carrier restore, webhook override, and workflow-retry inheritance each asserted end-to-end. Full local CI mirror green (`fmt`, per-crate clippy `-D warnings`, MSRV `check --workspace`, DB suites).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): with-start keyed committed-replay validation ordering — see issue #1092. `signal_with_start_workflow` and `update_with_start_workflow` (the HTTP handlers for the atomic start-or-attach + signal (#244) / + update (#479) primitives) ran their fresh-start-only validation — the #610 payload/schema gate, and for update-with-start the #373 `start_input` schema gate and the #684 semantic validator — **before** their idempotency dedup. So a retry of an *already-committed keyed with-start* — which must replay to its documented no-op — was instead rejected `400`/`422` whenever validation had **tightened** between the original delivery and the retry (a schema published/made stricter, a lowered payload cap, or a validator that would now reject the same args). At-least-once webhook/event retries broke precisely when a schema change landed. Fixed with an early, **read-only** committed-replay probe at each handler's edge (keyed requests only) that short-circuits to the documented replay response BEFORE any fresh-start-only *rejection* — validation AND the #377 admission gate; a probe MISS falls through to the untouched authoritative in-lock path, which reserves the exactly-once signal/update and remains the source of truth for the concurrent-first-delivery race. Mirrors #808 (plain start route) and #1092 (plain signal route). **Core (`execution.rs`)**: promoted the two committed-replay lookups the in-lock dedup already uses to `pub` so the probe and the authoritative dedup share one source of truth (they can never drift): `lookup_idempotent_signal_dedupe`, `lookup_idempotent_update_dedupe`, and the `UpdateDedupeRow` it returns (now a `pub` struct with `pub` fields, deriving `Debug, Clone`). **`signal-with-start` handler**: new `probe_committed_sws_replay` (plugin `api.rs`) fans out across shards via `lookup_idempotent_signal_dedupe`; on a hit it returns `200 { signal_delivered: false }` with a best-effort SUCCEEDED audit (intentional asymmetry with the fresh-start arm's 503-on-audit-failure: the original start was already audited). It runs right after signal-payload extraction, keyed-only, before the #610 signal-payload schema gate. **`update-with-start` handler**: the `update_id` derivation (UUIDv5 over the DNS namespace of the idempotency key) and `probe_committed_uws_replay` are hoisted **above the found-shard scan and the #377 admission gate** (mirroring signal-with-start, whose probe already precedes both), not merely above the #373 gate. The probe fans out via `lookup_idempotent_update_dedupe` and returns the resolved `UpdateWithStartOutcome` (`update_admitted: false`) — which flows through the handler's existing `Ok` arm (polling for the cached update result, writing the SUCCEEDED audit), giving a committed replay the SAME behavior as a fresh admission. The #377 admission gate, the #373 gate, and the #610+#684 blocks are all guarded `if probe_outcome.is_none()` (on a hit the handler short-circuits before the gate; on a miss the gate runs unconditionally for genuinely-fresh work); the authoritative call becomes `match probe_outcome { Some(o) => Ok(o), None => authoritative }`. This closes a P1 review finding: pre-hoist, update-with-start ran the admission gate BEFORE the probe, so a committed keyed replay retried while an operator had RAISED a gate returned a spurious `503` instead of the cached `200`/`update_admitted:false` — divergent from its own signal-with-start sibling and from the #808 invariant. **Fail-closed probes (P2 review finding)**: both probes previously swallowed any per-shard conn-acquire or lookup error into a dedup MISS, then fell through to fresh-start validation — reintroducing the bug under a transient owning-shard error. Both now track a `had_error` flag across the fan-out (three-state: hit / clean-miss / inconclusive): on a hit they short-circuit; a conn/lookup `Err` sets the flag and keeps scanning other shards (a later shard may hold the hit); after a no-hit loop they fail **closed** with a `503` when `had_error`, else return the clean-miss sentinel so the caller runs the authoritative in-lock path. `probe_committed_sws_replay` still returns `Option<Response>` (`Some` now also carries the `503`); `probe_committed_uws_replay` returns `Result<Option<UpdateWithStartOutcome>, Response>` (`Err` = `503`). Deliberately more conservative than #808's plain-start probe — the sibling found-shard scan in both handlers already fails closed on the same error class, and fail-closed preserves the never-reject invariant; a keyed client retries `503` idempotently. **Committed uws replay skips fresh-start shard routing (P2 review finding)**: after the admission-gate hoist above, the `update-with-start` handler still ran the storage-pool lookup, the multi-shard `found_shard` scan, AND `pick_for_new_workflow` on a committed-replay HIT before the later `match probe_outcome` — so a dedupe hit could STILL return `503` (a shard-scan `Err`, or `pick_for_new_workflow` selecting an unavailable shard, in a multi-shard partial outage or terminal-prior case), partially undoing the admission-gate hoist via fresh-start infrastructure. The `(shard, conn, exec_id)` resolution now branches on `probe_outcome.as_ref()`: on a HIT it acquires ONLY the hit execution's OWN shard connection (O(1) from `outcome.exec_id` via `db_conn_for_execution`) for the `Ok` arm's audit + result poll, skipping the scan / admission gate / `pick_for_new_workflow` entirely; on a MISS the full fresh-start routing runs byte-identically. A fresh-shard partial outage can now never `503` a dedupe hit (the #808 invariant: a committed replay is never rejected by fresh-start-only infrastructure). `signal-with-start` was already clean here — its probe returns a finished `Response` and `return`s before the routing scan, so this fix is uws-only. New RED→GREEN proof `uws_committed_keyed_replay_hit_never_503s_on_dead_fresh_start_shard` (`interface_schema_integration.rs`) builds a TWO-shard app (shard 0 live, shard 1 an unreachable URL — mirroring the `workflow_reachability_integration.rs` partial-outage harness) and seeds a TERMINATED prior + committed `UpdateAdmitted` on shard 0: the read-only probe (no state filter) resolves the hit on shard 0, but the fresh-start `found_shard` scan EXCLUDES `TERMINATED`, so pre-fix it reaches the dead shard 1 and returns `503`; post-fix the hit path resolves audit polling on shard 0 via `db_conn_for_execution` and returns `200` (`started_fresh: false`, no second `UpdateAdmitted`). The rest of the `interface_schema_integration` suite (every existing uws committed-replay hit test — attach / running / validator-not-rerun / gate-bypass) stays green, proving the hit-shard audit + polling path is unchanged. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change.** The in-lock exactly-once machinery is untouched — the probe is an additive read-only fast path for committed replays only, never a replacement (two simultaneous first deliveries both miss the probe and are serialized by the in-lock `ON CONFLICT` reserve). The non-keyed and fresh-keyed paths are byte-for-byte unchanged (the probe is keyed-only; a fresh key misses and the existing validation + authoritative path runs). Tests (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/interface_schema_integration.rs`, Docker-backed on Linux in CI, manifest line 85; ran green against local Postgres 16): the 4 committed-replay RED→GREEN proofs — `sws_committed_keyed_replay_after_attach_short_circuits_before_schema_gate`, `sws_committed_keyed_replay_after_terminal_fresh_start_short_circuits`, `uws_committed_keyed_replay_after_running_short_circuits_before_validation`, `uws_committed_keyed_replay_validator_not_rerun` — plus the two admission-gate RED→GREEN proofs `uws_committed_keyed_replay_bypasses_a_raised_admission_gate` (new; fails with `503` pre-hoist) and its symmetric guard `sws_committed_keyed_replay_bypasses_a_raised_admission_gate` (both raise a `WorkflowName` gate on the router's own `gate_cache` and assert `200`, not `503`), plus the guard tests `sws_fresh_keyed_malformed_still_400`, `uws_fresh_keyed_malformed_still_400`, `sws_uws_unkeyed_behavior_unchanged`, `uws_paused_fresh_keyed_still_409` proving the fresh/unkeyed/paused paths are preserved. Full 28-test suite green, no regression.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): workflow-type reachability follow-up: samples, orphan summary, boot gate — see issue #700. Thin follow-up on the already-shipped workflow-type reachability check (issue #520 / Phase 3.35), closing the four re-scoped ACs of #700. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new route** — this is a read-path (samples + top-level summary) plus a startup-read gate, entirely additive. **AC2 — bounded execution-id samples.** `execution::non_terminal_counts_by_workflow_name` now returns up to `REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP` (=5, documented) representative *non-terminal* execution ids per workflow type via `(ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY started_at ASC, id ASC))[1:5]` folded into the existing `GROUP BY` — so an operator can drill straight into a stuck run of an `orphaned` type instead of paginating `GET /workflows`. Terminal executions are excluded by the existing state filter (`RUNNING`/`SUSPENDED`/`PAUSED` only), so a sample never points at a completed run. New `sample_execution_ids: Vec<Uuid>` on `WorkflowTypeNonTerminalCount` (core) and `WorkflowTypeReachability` (plugin); the plugin caps the cross-shard union to the same cap in shard-iteration order — documented as *representative and bounded*, not a guaranteed global-oldest-across-shards set. Empty for `safe_to_remove` types. (The `ARRAY_AGG` slice materialises the full ordered id array per group before slicing — transient memory proportional to group size, acceptable under the < 2 s / 100k-execution budget; the drop-in fallback for very large groups is a `LATERAL (SELECT … ORDER BY started_at LIMIT n)` per group.) **AC3 — top-level orphan summary.** `WorkflowReachabilityReport` gains `orphaned: bool` (true when any type has an `orphaned` verdict) and `total_orphaned_executions: i64` (sum of `non_terminal_count` over `orphaned`-verdict types — a count of stranded *executions*, not types), so a CI/CD gate asserts "zero orphans" against a single field instead of walking `items[]`. Both reflect only the inspected shards; when `status` is `partial`/`unavailable` an unreachable shard could still host an orphaned type.
