(G) **`workflow_id` / `workflow_type` threaded through ALL replay/handler-context paths (closing the Codex P2 replay-safety surface, `context.rs:1897`).** The exact same class as finding (E)'s `parent_execution_id`: `ctx.info().workflow_type` (= the `workflow_name` column / handler-lookup key) and `ctx.info().workflow_id` (the business `workflow_id` column) live in **no** `WorkflowEvent` — the LIVE worker sets them on the context via `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta`, but the strict/canary/export/JSON/query replay paths built the context **without** them, so a pure-history replay reported `""` for both. A workflow that branched command-affecting control flow on either — or embedded either in an activity input, which the `ctx.info()` docs promise is replay-safe — then false-reported non-determinism under export/DB/canary/JSON replay. **Two mechanisms:** `workflow_type` uses **mechanism 1** (the workflow type name is the handler-lookup key already carried on every replay path — `HistorySnapshot.workflow_name`, `HistoryExportDocument.workflow_name`, `SampledExecution`/`DbReplayMeta`, the execution row — so it is now *applied* to the replayed context via `.with_workflow_name(...)`, no new field); `workflow_id` uses **mechanism 2** (a new additive `workflow_id: Option<String>` field, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, on `HistorySnapshot` and `HistoryExportDocument`/`HistoryExportRequest`, populated in **all** producers and threaded into the replayed context via `.with_workflow_id(...)`). Threaded at **every** replay/handler-context site: the three executor replay functions (`run_workflow_strict`/`run_workflow_strict_advancing_clock`/`run_workflow_canary` gain `workflow_name: String` + `workflow_id: Option<String>` params); `WorkflowReplayer` (new `with_workflow_id` global + `workflow_id` field, resolved snapshot-first-then-global mirroring the parent pattern) across `replay_from_snapshot`/`replay_from_events`/`replay_from_db`/`run_canary`; both DB queries (`query_running_executions`, `load_workflow_name_and_headers` now SELECT `workflow_id`, and `SampledExecution`/`DbReplayMeta` carry it); the history-export document + retention archive (`candidate.workflow_id`) + **both** plugin HTTP export producers (`export_history_for_execution` from `execution.workflow_id`, `export_history_for_candidate` from the new `HistoryExportCandidate.workflow_id` field — the batch candidate SELECT `HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL` now selects `w.workflow_id` and adds it to the `GROUP BY`); the plugin `hydrate_ctx_for_query` query-replay context and the `handle.rs` typed-query context (both apply `execution.workflow_name`/`execution.workflow_id` from the loaded row); and the WorkflowTestEnv advancing-clock path. The declarative `#[update]` handler contexts already inherit `inner.workflow_id`/`inner.workflow_name` from the parent context, so once the parent replay context is fixed the inheritance propagates (no change needed there). With this, `ctx.info().workflow_id` / `ctx.info().workflow_type` are the **real** values under export/DB/canary/JSON replay, not `""`. New falsifiable tests in `replayer_tests.rs` (mirroring the parent export round-trip): `workflow_type_and_id_replay_clean_through_export_document_round_trip` (the money test — a workflow embedding both identity fields in an activity input replays `ReplaySucceeded` through the export→`replay_from_json` round trip; **RED pre-fix**: recorded input `{"workflow_id":"cart-42","workflow_type":"identity_wf"}` vs replayed `{"workflow_id":"","workflow_type":""}` → `NonDeterminismDetected`, the strict-input comparison doubling as the census's DIRECT "context reports the real values not ''" assertion), `workflow_id_diverges_through_export_document_when_id_is_dropped` (mechanism-2 load-bearing proof), `workflow_type_is_applied_from_handler_key_on_raw_events_path` (mechanism-1 proof), and `workflow_id_is_applied_from_replayer_global_on_raw_events_path`. See the PR body "Field census" table for the full per-path threading verification. No CLI, scheduler, `ActivityContext`, event, schema, or migration changes. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** `WorkflowTestEnv::replay_check` now uses the producing env's configured `workflow_name` / `workflow_id` / `parent_execution_id` for the replay snapshot **and** the workflow-handler registration key — previously the snapshot `workflow_name` and the registration key were both hardcoded `"__test__"` and `workflow_id` was hardcoded `None`, so a `WorkflowTestEnv` test using `.with_workflow_name(...)` / `.with_workflow_id(...)` that recorded `ctx.info().workflow_type` / `ctx.info().workflow_id` into an activity input false-flagged non-determinism in the harness's own replay self-check (the replay context reported `workflow_type == "__test__"` / `workflow_id == ""` while the live run recorded the configured value). `TestRunOutcome` now carries the env's `workflow_name`/`workflow_id`; `WorkflowTestEnv` gains a `with_workflow_id(...)` builder and threads it into the live run's span-meta (was hardcoded empty). Both sides now use the same value (whatever it is, incl. the `""` default), so a default-env run is unchanged and a configured run replays clean. New no-DB tests in `workflow_test_env_tests.rs`: `test_configured_workflow_metadata_in_activity_input_replays_clean` (**RED pre-fix**: `ActivityScheduleMismatch`, recorded `{"workflow_id":"cart-42","workflow_type":"cart_flow"}` vs replayed `{"workflow_id":"","workflow_type":"__test__"}`) and `test_default_env_metadata_in_activity_input_replays_clean` (default-env regression guard). testing.rs-only change; no production/plugin/CLI/scheduler edits. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2 @ `testing.rs:903`):** `WorkflowReplayer` gains `with_execution_id(ExecutionId)` so raw `replay_from_events` fixtures can supply the captured original run id. `ctx.info().execution_id` is documented as replay-safe — the production / DB (`replay_from_db`) / snapshot (`replay_from_snapshot` / `replay_from_json`) / canary (`run_canary`) paths all recover the real id, and `TestRunOutcome::replay_check` threads the captured live-run id via its snapshot — but the raw-events path carries no `HistorySnapshot`, so it minted a fresh random `ExecutionId::new()`. A workflow that recorded its own `ctx.info().execution_id` in a command-affecting value (e.g. an activity input) then false-flagged non-determinism (random replay id vs recorded original run id). With this builder, **every** `WorkflowReplayer` / `WorkflowTestEnv` replay entry point now threads all four replay-stable `info()` fields — `execution_id`, `workflow_id`, `workflow_type`, `parent_execution_id` — so no `ctx.info()` field can false-flag non-determinism on any harness replay path. `None` (the default) preserves the fresh-id behaviour, so existing raw-events fixtures are unaffected. New no-DB tests in `replayer_tests.rs`: `execution_id_is_applied_from_replayer_global_on_raw_events_path` (**RED pre-fix**: divergence, recorded activity input carries the real `execution_id` vs the replay's fresh random one) and `execution_id_diverges_on_raw_events_path_without_the_builder` (the load-bearing negative control). testing.rs-only change; no production/plugin/CLI/scheduler edits. **Per-path × 4-field harness census (after this change — every cell threaded):** | Replay path | `execution_id` | `workflow_id` | `workflow_type` | `parent_execution_id` | | `replay_from_events` (raw) | ✅ `with_execution_id` global (else fresh id) | ✅ `with_workflow_id` global | ✅ handler key | ✅ `with_parent_execution_id` global | | `replay_with_reset` (delegates to `replay_from_events`) | ✅ (inherits) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `replay_from_snapshot` / `replay_from_json` | ✅ snapshot (required field) | ✅ snapshot → global | ✅ snapshot | ✅ snapshot → global | | `replay_from_db` | ✅ row | ✅ row | ✅ row | ✅ row | | `run_canary` | ✅ row | ✅ row | ✅ row | ✅ row | | `TestRunOutcome::replay_check` | ✅ captured live-run id (via snapshot) | ✅ env config (via snapshot) | ✅ env config (via snapshot) | ✅ env config (via snapshot) | | harness dir-fixture (`verify_history`) | ✅ snapshot (via `replay_from_snapshot`) | ✅ snapshot | ✅ snapshot | ✅ snapshot |
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Cause-targeted bulk DLQ replay/discard + `dlq_reason`/`error_class` facets — see issue #613. **Before:** during a DLQ flood an operator could aggregate dead-letter counts by workflow/activity/queue/failure-signature (`GET /dead-letters/aggregate`, shipped in #385) but could **not** group by *why* entries failed, and could **not** target a bulk replay/discard at a specific failure cause — `BulkDlqFilter` matched only workflow/activity/time. "Replay every poison-pilled entry" or "discard everything that failed with `CircuitOpen`" required scripting over the raw row list. **After:** a two-call incident runbook. (1) `GET /dead-letters/aggregate?group_by=dlq_reason` (or `error_class`) shows the flood's cause shape; (2) feed a facet's cause tuple back into `POST /dead-letters/replay|discard` (or `harvest dlq replay/discard --dlq-reason poison_pill`) to act on exactly that cohort. A facet's cause round-trips into the bulk filter and re-selects exactly the rows it counted. **Reconciliation with prior art (#385).** Per the #543/#593 reconciliation precedent, #613's ACs were ground-truthed against the code first: the faceted-aggregation half of #613 **already shipped in #385** (the `/aggregate` route *is* the AC1 "summary" route — reconciled name; per-group `first_seen`/`last_seen` == the AC's `earliest`/`latest`; `dlq::failure_signature`, `merge_dlq_aggregates`, cross-shard fan-out, top-N rollup, time-window narrowing, descending sort, and the CLI `dlq aggregate` command all reused verbatim). The genuine residual shipped here is the **cause dimension** #385 did not ship: the `dlq_reason`/`error_class` grouping facets (AC1 named them explicitly; #385 shipped only `failure_signature`) and the entire cause-targeted **bulk filter** (AC4/AC5/AC6), tied together by AC5's round-trip tuple `(workflow_name, activity_name, dlq_reason, error_class)`. **What shipped.** **Two pure classifiers** in `dlq.rs`, compute-on-read from the freeform `error` TEXT column (all production DLQ rows are `DeadLetterReason` tagged JSON): `dlq_reason(error)` → snake_case mechanism class (`poison_pill`/`history_cap_exceeded`/`workflow_task_timeout`/`callback_delivery_exhausted`, else `retry_exhaustion`); `error_class(error)` → typed activity `error_type` (`CircuitOpen`, …) if present, else the `DeadLetterReason` PascalCase tag, else a normalized leading token. Both bounded and deterministic. `failure_signature` reused unchanged. **Aggregate**: two new `DlqGroupDimension` variants (`DlqReason`, `ErrorClass`) plug into the existing load-and-classify pass — no new SQL. **Bulk filter**: `BulkDlqFilter` gains `error_class`/`dlq_reason`/`failure_signature` (compute-on-read Rust post-filter, applied before the limit) plus `queue_name`/`min_attempts` (SQL) so any aggregate scope is reproducible. `is_empty`/`MAX_BULK_LIMIT`/`dry_run` preserved. An empty/whitespace cause value is **rejected `400`** in both the JSON and form paths (an empty cause must never silently widen a bulk op). **CLI**: `dlq summary` (alias of `aggregate`); `--dlq-reason`/`--error-class`/`--failure-signature`/`--queue-name`/`--min-attempts` on `dlq replay`/`discard`. **Contract + CI**: `management_api_request_fields()` and `docs/api-contract.json` updated (contract-regression green); `dlq_aggregate_integration`/`dlq_bulk_integration` graduated from the CI ALLOWLIST into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` so the new tests run under Docker in CI. **Invariants.** **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no `schema.rs` column, no event-log write** (AC7) — read-mostly, plus the additive bulk-filter dimension. **Review + tests.** Multi-angle adversarial review, no P1. **P2-1** (aggregate `queue_name`/`min_attempts` scope not reproducible in the bulk filter → cross-queue over-action) fixed by adding those two SQL filters — `bulk_cause_plus_queue_round_trips_exactly` proves a queue-scoped facet no longer over-acts. **P2-2** (cause matching is a compute-on-read full-shard scan) documented — symmetric with the already-shipped aggregate's accepted cost; `MAX_BULK_LIMIT` caps rows acted-on, narrowable by time/queue/activity/workflow/min_attempts. Executed on real Postgres 16 (testcontainers): `dlq_bulk_integration` 17/17, `dlq_aggregate_integration` 14/14, `contract_regression` 22/22, core `dlq` (`--features db`) 71/71; plus the pure-unit tests `aggregate_group_by_dlq_reason_orders_by_count`, `aggregate_group_by_error_class`, `aggregate_group_by_dlq_reason_merges_across_shards`, `bulk_cause_dry_run_count_equals_aggregate_facet`, and CLI `request_mapping`/`contract_coverage` coverage.
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Bounded / windowed activity fan-out — see issue #750. Bounded-concurrency variants of the four activity fan-out shapes, so a wide fan-out applies natural backpressure to workers and downstreams instead of scheduling every input at once. This is a pure `context.rs` scheduling change — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no worker/replay/executor change.** Four new public `WorkflowContext` methods (a `max_in_flight: usize` window `W` argument added to each existing shape): `execute_activity_fan_out_windowed<I,O>(info, inputs, W)`, `execute_activity_fan_out_collect_windowed<I,O>(info, inputs, W)`, `execute_activity_fan_out_raw_windowed(activities, W)`, `execute_activity_fan_out_collect_raw_windowed(activities, W)` — the typed variants resolve queue/retry/timeout from `info` and serialize/deserialize exactly like the unbounded typed methods. Two new self-contained impls (`fan_out_raw_windowed_impl`, `fan_out_collect_raw_windowed_impl`); the four existing unbounded public methods and their impls are left byte-for-byte untouched. **Scope: activity fan-out only.** Child-workflow bounded fan-out is an explicit deferred follow-up (mirroring how #601 followed #359) — the issue's ACs, problem statement, and success metric are all activity-focused (`harvest_task_queue` rows). **Mechanics (two-phase: resume-then-dispatch).** Each windowed call runs the shared `check_cancellation()` → `next_fan_out_seq()` → `check_fan_out_count(seq, N)` prologue (the marker records **only `N`**, never `W`), including on the empty-input path so an empty windowed fan-out records `marker(count=0)` then returns `Ok(vec![])` — identical to the unbounded path. `W` is then clamped `max(1)` (never `chunks(0)`/`take(0)`). The call then runs in **two phases**. **Phase 1 (resume):** the number of this fan-out's slots already scheduled in recorded history — a contiguous input-order prefix `[0..s)` — is read via the new read-only, cursor-non-mutating `HistoryMatcher::count_pending_scheduled_activities(cap)` (called right after the count marker is consumed; `cap = N` both bounds the scan and stops a fully-completed fan-out's continuation from inflating the prefix with a later unrelated activity), and slots `[0..s)` are resumed as **one homogeneous `try_join_all` batch** — every prefix slot is in history, so each resolves to `Matched` (emits nothing) or `ActivityInProgress` (emits only `WaitForActivity`), **never `ScheduleActivity`**. **Phase 2 (dispatch):** once the prefix is fully resolved, the fresh remainder `[s..N)` is dispatched in `W`-sized waves, each `try_join_all`ed before the next is drawn. `check_cancellation()` runs before the resume batch and at the start of every fresh wave. Fail-fast: the first activity failure aborts and later waves are never dispatched (a deliberate backpressure semantic — a bounded fail-fast may process fewer items than the unbounded path would). Collect-all maps per-slot `ActivityFailed`/`Timeout` to `Ok(Err(..))` (a shared classification closure), so `try_join_all` never short-circuits and every wave dispatches / all `N` inputs are processed. **Determinism / replay (the whole point).** Because activities dispatch in input order, `ActivityScheduled` events are recorded globally in input order `0..N`, so replay is **window-independent — including across a window CHANGE**: the same recorded history replays *and resumes* to identical results regardless of the `W` the replaying code is configured with, whether that `W` is larger or smaller than the one that produced the recorded partial state (`W` governs live dispatch only and is never in history). This is the load-bearing property the two-phase resume guarantees: phase 1 isolates the already-scheduled in-flight prefix into a homogeneous batch, so a mid-flight window **increase** can no longer regroup an in-flight slot together with never-scheduled fresh slots into a mixed `[WaitForActivity + ScheduleActivity]` suspension batch — a batch the worker's `handle_suspended_workflow` cannot persist, which terminally **FAILED** the run under the original single-loop implementation. On a window **decrease**, work already scheduled under the old larger window cannot be un-dispatched, so the resume phase waits on the whole already-scheduled prefix (up to the old width) before the smaller window governs further dispatch; peak in-flight can briefly exceed the newly-lowered `W` during the resume (inherent and correct — the window bounds *new* dispatch, never work already in flight, and there is no new stampede). Every fixed-window case emits **byte-identical** commands to the unbounded path (fresh live cycle → phase 1 empty, phase 2 dispatches `[0..W)`; full-history replay → phase 1 resumes all, phase 2 empty; `W >= N` → a single wave = marker + N `ScheduleActivity`). Recorded count stays `N`; a recorded-`N`-vs-current-code-`N` mismatch still surfaces `HarvestError::NonDeterministic`, exactly as unbounded. `W == 0`/`< 1` clamps up to 1 (documented, deterministic — never a panic, hang, or silent no-op). The shared `fan_out_seq` counter is reused, so a windowed then an unbounded fan-out get `fan_out:1`, `fan_out:2`. The two `try_join_all` known limitations of the unbounded fan-out carry over **per-wave** (narrowed, not widened). Trade-off: chunked waves, not a true sliding window — a wave does not refill until every activity in it completes (convoy effect on heterogeneous latencies), documented in CLAUDE.md. Docs: CLAUDE.md "Fan-out / Parallel Activities" method table + a "Bounded / windowed fan-out" subsection. Example: `examples/fanout_batch.rs` gains a `windowed_batch` workflow (single-call fan-out over a collection larger than the window) with an embedded `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "testing"))]` `WorkflowTestEnv` test; a `cargo test --features testing --example fanout_batch` CI step is added. Tests, TDD red→green→refactor: pure unit tests in `tests/integration/fanout_tests.rs` (first-wave ≤ W, ≤ W-in-flight-every-wave via a hand-rolled multi-cycle drive over 10 inputs, input-order results, W>=N identical-history-to-unbounded, W=0-clamps-to-1, collect-all-processes-every-input-despite-failure, fail-fast-stops-later-waves, shared-seq-counter, empty-records-marker, count-mismatch → non-deterministic, cancellation → Cancelled) plus the two-phase resume regression + coverage set (`windowed_fan_out_resumes_under_increased_window`: a partial `W1=1` history re-driven under `W2=3` re-parks on the in-flight slot ONLY — 0 `ScheduleActivity` in the resume batch — then dispatches the fresh remainder after it completes, driven to completion byte-identical to unbounded; `windowed_fan_out_resumes_under_decreased_window`: a `W1=4` all-in-flight history re-driven under `W2=2` resumes all 4; `windowed_fan_out_mid_wave_cancellation_does_not_dispatch_next_wave`; `windowed_collect_all_whole_wave_failure_still_dispatches_next_wave`; the previously-uncovered typed collect windowed `windowed_typed_collect_returns_typed_ok_and_err_slots_in_order` + `windowed_typed_collect_surfaces_deserialization_error`; and the `is_local`-guard `windowed_typed_methods_reject_local_activities`); `WorkflowReplayer` fixtures in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` (ReplaySucceeded, window-independence across W=1/2/100/unbounded with byte-identical results, ≥25 randomized-completion-order histories — now asserting ≥2 distinct non-identity permutations so it can't pass vacuously — plus `replayer_windowed_shaped_history_replays_under_any_window` over a genuinely windowed-SHAPED wave-by-wave history under W=1/W=4/unbounded, and `replayer_windowed_fail_fast_history_reproduces_failure_deterministically` proving a fail-fast bounded history replays cleanly as `WorkflowFailed`, never false non-determinism); a `WorkflowTestEnv` drive-to-completion test in `tests/integration/workflow_test_env_tests.rs`; and the DB e2e success-metric test `windowed_fan_out_peak_task_rows_bounded_by_window` in `tests/integration/integration_e2e.rs` (N=20, W=5: a concurrent DB poller — reusing one connection across the poll loop — confirms peak `RUNNING`/`PENDING` activity rows for the execution stays ≤ 5, results are byte-identical to an unbounded fan-out over the same inputs, and exactly 20 `ActivityScheduled` + one `fan_out` marker are recorded). All pure/testing tests and — via a local Postgres 16 (`HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) — the DB e2e test were executed green. **Post-review hardening (determinism-critical fix).** The original single-loop windowed impl regrouped an in-flight slot with never-scheduled fresh slots on a mid-flight window CHANGE, emitting a mixed `[WaitForActivity + ScheduleActivity]` suspension batch the worker cannot persist — terminally FAILING the run (falsifying the window-independence AC). Fixed by the two-phase resume-then-dispatch restructure above, backed by the new read-only `HistoryMatcher::count_pending_scheduled_activities(cap)` (cursor-non-mutating; changes no matching semantics or event contract). Every fixed-window case stays byte-identical, so all pre-existing windowed tests pass unchanged; the only new behavior is the now-correct window-change case in both directions.
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Single-execution replay diagnosis endpoint — see issue #614. New read-only, admin-gated management route `POST /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/replay-diagnosis` that loads ONE execution's recorded history from its owning shard and replays it against the **currently-registered** `#[workflow]` handler via the already-reachable `WorkflowReplayer` (`autumn_harvest::testing`, already enabled since the plugin builds core with `features = ["db","testing"]`), returning a structured determinism verdict. It answers, on demand for one specific run, the same question the fleet-wide #480/#603 non-determinism-block incident signal raises: "will — or did — this run diverge under the code I have deployed right now?" — the headline use case being a PAUSED or non-determinism-blocked RUNNING run, or a terminal FAILED run for retroactive forensics (AC4). **Verdict shape.** `200` for every reachable diagnosis (the diagnosis, not the HTTP status, carries the answer): `clean` (message `"no divergence under current code"`, AC6), `diverged` (with a `divergence { kind, event_index, expected, actual }` object mirroring the #603 block diagnostic vocabulary so an operator can cross-check it against a blocked run's `search_attrs`, AC2), `workflow_failed` (with `failure { error, event_index }`), `not_registered` (the workflow type is not registered on this node), or `not_replayable_dag` (a classic non-unified DAG is not on the replay path). The AC5 `not_registered`/`not_replayable_dag` verdicts are resolved by a pre-check (`runtime.registry.workflows.contains_key` then `runtime.is_registered_dag`) BEFORE any history is loaded. Non-`200` statuses are reserved for the resource itself: `400` (malformed id), `404` (unknown execution), `408` (replay exceeded the `WorkerConfig::query_timeout` budget), `410` (history unavailable, on either of two terminal-only gates mirroring the #612 terminal-query path: a terminal execution whose recorded history is truncated BEFORE its terminal seal — pruned by retention or released on reset — gated by `executor::history_reached_terminal_seal` since such a prefix-only history replays to a frontier suspension that canary would falsely report as `clean` (Codex review); or a terminal execution whose payloads were PII-erased per issue #495, gated by the terminal-only O(1) `erase::execution_input_is_erased` row check). Both gate ONLY terminal executions — a seal-less prefix is the NORMAL shape of a healthy in-flight RUNNING/PAUSED/SUSPENDED run, which still replays to a real `clean`/`diverged` verdict. **Read-only / zero-writes (AC3).** New pure plugin module `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/replay_diagnosis.rs` owns the serializable DTOs (`ReplayDiagnosisResponse`, `DiagnosisVerdict`, `DivergenceDetail`, `FailureDetail`) and the total `report_to_response` / `not_registered_response` / `not_replayable_dag_response` mapping (every `ReplayStatus` variant → a distinct verdict), unit-tested with no DB or async. The `api.rs` handler mirrors `hydrate_ctx_for_query`'s (#612) discipline: load the execution (shard-routed via `db_conn_for_execution`), run the erased/410 and AC5 pre-checks, load the history (via `store::load_history_inflated` with the runtime's own `PayloadCodecs` + registry offloader, so an encrypted (#608) or offloaded (#524) history replays as the live worker sees it — the default no-codec/no-offloader path is byte-identical to `load_history`), **drop the DB connection**, apply the terminal-only truncated-history seal-gate/410 (Codex review; `executor::history_reached_terminal_seal` — a terminal execution with no seal is refused before replay, mirroring #612), then build a `HistorySnapshot` from the execution row + history (threading its own `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at`/`parent_id`/`workflow_id`/`context_headers` per #772/#698/#481 so a deadline-/parent-/header-aware run replays cleanly instead of false-reporting non-determinism) and replay via `WorkflowReplayer::replay_canary_snapshot` (drop-first, so no pool slot is held during the replay — chosen over `replay_from_db`, which holds its connection across the whole replay). The replay is bounded by `query_timeout` via `tokio::time::timeout`; on the timer winning, `408` — the `query_timeout` bound applies to async-yielding replays, and a workflow that busy-loops synchronously without ever `.await`-ing is out of scope, exactly as for the live executor. A large but healthy history is not at risk from the executor's 100 ms `SUSPENSION_TIMEOUT`: that per-cycle heuristic fires only when the handler future is genuinely *pending* on an unresolved oneshot at the replay frontier — it never cuts off a CPU-bound replay consuming recorded events, so a completed history replays to its verdict regardless of wall-clock duration (bounded only by the outer `query_timeout`, ample headroom for the ~<200 ms/10k-event replay budget, issue #135). The DTO layer is pure in-memory replay: no events appended, no state recomputed, no audit row written. **No feature-gate change, no core-signature change, no migration, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant.** Route registered admin-gated (`.route_layer(require_admin)`) in the axum router, in all four parallel plugin registries (`management_api_routes()`, `management_api_request_fields()` = `Some(&[])`, `management_api_response_fields()`), `docs/api-contract.json` (`read_only: true` + `post_for_body_only: true`, the same POST-but-read-only precedent as the query route), and the three `autumn_harvest::audit` route lists (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` `ReadOnly` / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` `None` / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`) with dedicated pinned classification tests in both `audit.rs` (`replay_diagnosis_route_is_classified_read_only`) and `contract_regression.rs` (`replay_diagnosis_route_is_classified`) — the pins catch the route being dropped from BOTH lists at once, which the mutual cross-check guards miss. CLI: `harvest workflow replay-diagnosis <id>` (bodyless POST, mirroring `resume`/`retry-now`), with mapping + coverage tests. **AC9 runbook / alert wiring.** `docs/runbooks/nondeterminism-block.md` gains a "Diagnose the divergence" triage section (the curl, the `diverged { kind, event_index, expected, actual }` body, the confirm-a-fix-is-clean and pinpoint-the-reset-`event_index` workflows), and the #480/#603 `harvest_workflow_non_determinism` starter-pack alert (`docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`) lists the endpoint as a recommended `management_checks` next step (plus a `#614` dependency entry). Tests, TDD red→green: 11 pure unit tests in `replay_diagnosis.rs` (every `ReplayStatus` → verdict mapping, the two not-replayable builders, snake_case serialization, and the five `reclassify_sealed_mid_await` cases below) — RED was captured on the `audit.rs` pin (route absent from the class lists → `test result: FAILED`) and confirmed GREEN after wiring; DB/HTTP integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/replay_diagnosis_integration.rs` (clean, diverged, FAILED-retroactive, 404, 400, not_registered, not_replayable_dag, erased→410, zero-writes incl. no task-queue enqueue, the headline nd-blocked-RUNNING → diverged, and the three post-review scenarios below). Registered as one sorted manifest line in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`; run Docker-backed on Linux in CI (and, unlike prior slices, executed against a real local Postgres 16 in the authoring sandbox via `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`), per the #543/#544/#601 precedent. **Post-review hardening.** **Canary, not strict, replay mode (P1 correctness).** The endpoint replays via `replay_canary_snapshot`, not `replay_from_snapshot`. Strict replay classifies a *frontier suspension* — every healthy in-flight `RUNNING`/`SUSPENDED`/`PAUSED` run parked mid-flight, the endpoint's HEADLINE use case — as `NonDeterminismDetected`, a FALSE `diverged`. Canary excepts exactly that frontier suspension → `clean`, while a genuine mid-history divergence still surfaces (it resolves synchronously during the drive, never as a frontier suspension). So a healthy PAUSED / in-flight run now correctly returns `clean`. Proven by `running_healthy_run_parked_mid_activity_is_clean` (fails under strict, passes under canary). **Sealed-mid-await terminal reclassification (P2 correctness).** A terminal run externally sealed *mid-await* (`TIMED_OUT`, or operator cancel/terminate) records its terminal-lifecycle seal where the next command would go. In the single-activity shape (`WorkflowStarted + ActivityScheduled(a) + WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`, the activity never completed) the workflow *suspends* awaiting the in-progress result → canary reports `clean` directly. In the multi-activity shape (item 1 completed, sealed awaiting item 2), the workflow consumes item 1 and issues the NEXT command, which lands on the seal → a raw `diverged{actual: "WorkflowExecutionTimedOut"}`. The pure `reclassify_sealed_mid_await` (unit-tested) rewrites *that* false positive to `clean` — but ONLY when the divergence's `actual` names an EXTERNAL-seal event (`WorkflowExecutionTimedOut` / `WorkflowCancelled` / `WorkflowResetTerminated`) AND the run's DB state is terminal AND the history reached a terminal seal. The load-bearing condition is the external-seal `actual`: a genuine mid-history divergence (an activity rename) names a real command event, and new code that does MORE work than a `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` run names the workflow's OWN outcome seal (`WorkflowCompleted`/ `WorkflowFailed`) — neither is an external seal, so both correctly stay `diverged` (retroactive forensics, AC4, is never masked). Proven by `timed_out_run_sealed_mid_activity` (clean via suspension) and `timed_out_run_sealed_awaiting_second_activity_is_clean` (clean via reclassification). **Codec/offload read fidelity (P2).** History is loaded with the runtime's `PayloadCodecs` + registry offloader (`load_history_inflated`) rather than the identity `load_history`, so an encrypted deployment (#608) no longer hard-500s on ciphertext and an offload deployment (#524) no longer false-diverges on a reference envelope. Identity deployments (the default) are byte-identical. **Tighter assertions + task-queue zero-write.** The diverged tests now assert the exact `event_index`/`expected`/`actual` (AC2), the nd-blocked test uses a clean-prefix history so the divergence lands at a real mid-history position (event index 3), and the zero-writes test also asserts `harvest_task_queue` is unchanged (no spurious enqueue, AC3). Negative admin-gate coverage in `security.rs` (`eris_unauthenticated_replay_diagnosis_is_blocked` → 401).
- **Phase 3.53** (implemented): Signal & update lifecycle metrics — see issue #684. **Observability** (implemented): Six new `MetricsRecorder` counters give operators first-class, alertable visibility into the signal- and update-handler lifecycle, closing the gap where signal delivery/consumption and the update admit→complete/fail path had no metric surface. Modelled exactly on the issue #519 `record_workflow_terminal` recipe: additive no-op-default trait methods + a `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge + coverage tests. **AC7 invariant: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no macro-path change** — this is a pure additive-metrics slice. The six counters (all bounded labels; `execution.id` is never a label, per ADR-0001 §7): `harvest.signal.received` (`workflow`, `queue` — see the Codex P2 cardinality note below; the signal `name` is NOT a label) — a `SignalReceived` event was durably delivered into a workflow's history. Emitted once per delivered signal at the single **live-only** delivery choke point (`ingest_due_timers_and_signals`, beside the existing `harvest.signal.deliver` span in `worker::process_workflow_task`), iterating `prepared.signals_delivered`. Each signal is marked consumed in `harvest_signals` so it appears in the delivered list exactly once; never emitted on replay. `harvest.signal.unhandled` (`workflow`, `queue` — see the Codex P2 cardinality note below; the signal `name` is NOT a label) — a delivered signal was never consumed (no `wait_for_signal`/`receive_signal`, no #546 push handler claimed it) by the time the run reached a **Completed or Failed** terminal outcome. Backed by new `HistoryMatcher::unconsumed_signals_by_name`, which mirrors `has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed`'s two sources (cursor scan + `pending_signals` buffer) restricted to `SignalReceived` and grouped by name, honoring the issue #476 lost-signal-or-deadline-race carve-out (`late_race_signal_events`) and #546 push-handler consumption (`claim_pending_signal` marks consumed). **Emission is post-commit, in the worker's `Persisted` arm — the same discipline as `harvest.update.completed/failed` — so it counts DURABLE terminal outcomes only, not the executor:** the executor's `drive_workflow` terminal arms compute the map (after `flush_pending_signal_handlers`, so #546 push handlers claim first — the only place the driven matcher's authoritative consumed-set exists) via `WorkflowContext::unhandled_signals` and **carry it out on `WorkflowOutcome::Completed`/`Failed` (a new `unhandled_signals: BTreeMap<String,u64>` field)**; the **worker** collects the map before the persist transaction (`outcome_unhandled_signals`) and emits it via `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics` **only in the post-commit `Persisted` arm**, alongside the update-result emission. Because that arm is reached only after a successful commit, the emit is downstream of **both** the #603 ND-block gate (an ND-carrying `Failed` early-returns via `block_workflow_for_non_determinism` before persist, so an ND-blocked/re-driven cycle never counts) **and** `check_paused_and_park` (a claimed-then-paused race returns via the `ParkedPaused` transaction result, and a persist failure via the `Err` arm — neither reaches the emit). A retry/resume of such a discarded cycle therefore **cannot double-count** — closing the Codex P2 edge where the earlier pre-persist placement (co-located with `record_workflow_terminal`) incremented the counter without a durable terminal event/state. Emitting in the executor (as an even earlier cut did, via `report_unhandled_signals`) was **upstream** of the ND gate entirely and would re-fire unboundedly during a persistent ND-block. **Known limitation (deliberate, documented):** covers only **Completed and Failed** (a run that reaches a *graceful* terminal via its own logic) — the paths with a driven matcher. **`TIMED_OUT` / `CANCELLED` / `TERMINATED` / parent-close-cascade / history-cap-failure runs with an undrained signal are NOT counted** (a scanner/operator force-kill has no driven matcher to reconstruct the consumed-set, and reconstructing it would need a re-drive; a partial/inaccurate count on a watched SLO metric is worse than none). For the stuck-timed-out case, use the workflow-timeout counter (`harvest.workflow.timeout`) + the stack API instead. `harvest.update.admitted` (`workflow`, `queue` — see the Codex P2 cardinality note below; the update `name` is NOT a label) — a workflow update was durably admitted (`UpdateAdmitted` appended). Emitted **post-commit** at the single admission choke point `store::admit_update_event`, which gained an `Option<&dyn MetricsRecorder>` param and now returns the resolved `(workflow_name, queue_name)`. Threaded through its callers: the HTTP `admit_update` handler and Vantage-UI submit pass the runtime recorder; **the in-process typed client (`handle::execute_update_in_process`) now passes the recorder too** — the client gained a `metrics: Arc<dyn MetricsRecorder>` field wired from the runtime at both `WorkflowHandleClient` construction sites (default no-op), because an in-process admit's *completion* runs through the worker (which emits update.completed/failed), so admitting without recording admitted would leave that path asymmetric; `update_with_start` passes `None` and emits at its own **outer-commit** boundary (gated on `outcome.update_admitted`, labeled by the pre-move `queue_for_metric`) so a rollback never over-counts. `harvest.update.rejected` (`workflow`, `name`) — a workflow update was rejected by its registered validator before admission (a durable pre-admission `422`). Emitted at the two — and, by an independent audit of every `HarvestError::UpdateRejected` construction and every registered-validator invocation, the **only** — durable validator-rejection sites: the `admit_update` and `update_with_start` HTTP handlers. Scope is deliberately limited to **validator** rejections; non-`RUNNING`/paused admission-state conflicts are surfaced as caller errors, not counted here. Not emitted in `WorkflowContext::validate_update` (replay-driven) or `execute_update_in_process` (runs no validator). The scheduler's reuse of the `UpdateRejected` variant for DAG manual-trigger deferral is unrelated and untouched. `harvest.update.completed` (`workflow`, `name`, `queue`) / `harvest.update.failed` (`workflow`, `name`, `queue`) — an admitted update's handler returned success/error (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed`). Emitted **post-commit** via the pure, unit-tested `collect_update_result_metrics` helper, which resolves each `RecordUpdateResult` command's `update_id` → update name from the `UpdateAdmitted` events in the loaded history (the command carries only the id). **Fires on every persist path (terminal, suspend, continue-as-new, and the two inline external-signal suspension branches), not just the terminal one.** The primary main-transaction emission (worker `Persisted` arm, post-commit) reads its `RecordUpdateResult`s via the new pure `update_result_command_source(&outcome, &pending_cmds)`: on a **Suspended** outcome the results live in `outcome.commands` (the executor returns `(Suspended{commands}, vec![])`, so `pending_cmds` is empty), on terminal/CAN they ride in `pending_cmds`. An earlier cut collected from `pending_cmds` only and therefore **undercounted the common case** — an update completes and the long-running workflow loops back to a `wait_for_signal`/activity and suspends. The two inline external-signal branches persist their update results outside the main transaction and strip them from the reconstructed suspension, so they emit inline (post-autocommit) via the shared `emit_update_result_metrics` helper. **No emit on the paused-park discard path** (the `ParkedPaused` transaction result returns before the `Persisted`-arm emission). Exactly-once: `RecordUpdateResult` is produced once on live execution (replay short-circuits in `execute_admitted_update`). **Emission discipline:** `record_signal_received` is live-frontier-only by construction (delivery choke point). `record_signal_unhandled` is emitted by the worker **post-commit, only in the `Persisted` arm** when a terminal outcome carries the map — the same durable-commit gating as `harvest.update.completed/failed`, so a `ParkedPaused` discard or a persist failure never over-counts; `WorkflowReplayer` drives the strict/canary executor path (a different function that never populates the map / never reaches the worker), so a replay of an already-terminal history emits zero unhandled samples — AC2, pinned by `replay_of_terminal_history_never_emits_signal_unhandled`. The update counters emit at the same post-commit `Persisted` boundary. Bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` (`MetricsRsRecorder`) using the existing `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_NAME`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE` constants (the two signal counters **and `update.admitted`** use `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE` only — no `name`, per the Codex P2 cardinality note below). Two new starter-pack alert rules (`harvest_update_rejected_rate`, `harvest_signal_unhandled_rate` — thresholds documented as starter defaults, not universal SLOs) with full runbook sections; six new dashboard panels (a "Signal & update lifecycle" row) in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`; ADR-0001 §7 catalogue and `docs/telemetry.md` updated. Tests, TDD red→green (verified RED→GREEN by reverting each fix): `metrics_coverage.rs` (RecordingMetrics impls + reachability + cardinality + exact-bounded-label test); `replay.rs` unit tests for `unconsumed_signals_by_name` (undrained/consumed-by-wait/consumed-by-push-handler/lost-race/multiple-same-name/stashed-but-unconsumed); `executor.rs` tests via `run_workflow_with_state_advancing_clock` proving the terminal outcomes **carry** the map and the executor **emits nothing** (Completed/Failed carry, Suspended does not, recorder sees zero samples); `context.rs` unit tests for the `unhandled_signals` reader; `worker.rs` unit tests for `collect_update_result_metrics` and `update_result_command_source` (the pure test that would have caught the suspend-path undercount), plus `outcome_unhandled_signals_reads_terminal_maps_and_is_empty_otherwise` / `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics_fires_once_per_occurrence` / `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics_is_a_noop_for_the_empty_collected_map` (the pure companions to the Codex-P2 post-commit move: the terminal map is captured before persist, and the `Persisted`-arm emit is a no-op for the empty map a non-terminal / discarded cycle carries); `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` label-content bridge test for all six; `replayer_tests.rs` AC2 test (replay path never emits `signal.unhandled` across ≥5 cycles); doc-enforcement registries in `dashboard_pack_docs.rs`/`alert_pack_docs.rs` extended. DB/worker integration tests: `metrics_integration.rs::update_completed_metric_fires_on_the_suspend_path` (an admitted update that completes while the workflow SUSPENDS emits exactly one `update.completed`) and `nd_block_tests.rs::{genuine_terminal_with_undrained_signal_emits_signal_unhandled, nd_blocked_cycle_does_not_emit_signal_unhandled}` — env-redirectable (`HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) so they run against a migrated Postgres without Docker; the suspend-path and genuine-terminal-emits tests were executed green against a real local Postgres 16 (and confirmed RED against a reverted fix), while the ND-block-suppression test (which needs the testcontainer nd-block harness) is compile-checked, its suppression additionally guaranteed by the post-commit `Persisted`-arm placement being strictly downstream of the #603 ND-block gate (the base `divergent_replay_blocks_instead_of_failing` test already asserts `terminal_failed_count == 0` on an ND-block, so the still-later `Persisted` arm is never reached either). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** `harvest.signal.unhandled` was initially emitted pre-persistence, co-located with `record_workflow_terminal` (#519), *before* the persist transaction and *before* `check_paused_and_park` could return `ParkedPaused`. On a claimed-then-paused race or a persist failure the counter incremented without a durable terminal event/state, and a retry/resume of that discarded cycle counted the same unhandled signal again. Fixed by mirroring the `harvest.update.completed/failed` discipline exactly: the `unhandled_signals` map is collected into a local (`outcome_unhandled_signals`) *before* the persist transaction moves `outcome`, and `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics` is called *only* in the post-commit `Persisted` arm — reached only after a successful commit, downstream of both the #603 ND-block gate and `check_paused_and_park`. `record_workflow_terminal` (#519) is untouched and keeps its own pre-persist placement. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2 — cardinality):** the initial cut labeled `harvest.signal.received` / `harvest.signal.unhandled` with a `name` (signal name) label. Signals are delivered via the **free-form** route `POST /workflows/{id}/signal/{signal_name}` — the `signal_name` path segment is caller-controlled and, unlike activity names or `#[update]` handler names, has **no declared registry** to bound it, so a caller using per-entity / dynamic signal names would create unbounded metric series (worst for `signal.unhandled`, whose names are by definition the mismatched / unlistened-for ones), violating the ADR-0001 §7 cardinality contract. **Fixed by dropping the `name` label from both signal counters** — they are now labeled `workflow` + `queue` only (both bounded). The signal name remains a span-only attribute on `harvest.signal.deliver`. For `signal.unhandled`, the worker now **sums** the terminal outcome's per-name unconsumed map (`emit_unhandled_signal_metrics`) into one increment per unconsumed occurrence against the single `(workflow, queue)` series, preserving the total unconsumed volume without the unbounded dimension. Per-signal-name diagnostics are explicitly out of scope for this slice (use the per-workflow stack / open-awaitables API). The `MetricsRecorder::record_signal_received`/`record_signal_unhandled` trait signatures dropped the `signal_name` parameter, so a caller-free-form name cannot reach these counters by construction. **AC3 reconciliation (per-name update visibility kept on the resolved counters; every counter bounded by construction).** After the fixes below, **no** `harvest.update.*` counter carries a name that is free-form at emission — so no counter can be driven to unbounded cardinality by a hostile/buggy caller. A boundedness audit found a genuine unbounded risk: the raw route `POST /workflows/{id}/update/{name}` admits **any** name (the validator lookup is best-effort, so an *unregistered* free-form name falls through and is durably admitted), reaching `harvest.update.admitted` with the raw name; the same admitted name then fails the worker's handler lookup (`"update handler '<name>' not found"`), reaching `harvest.update.failed` with the raw name. **Crucial constraint found while fixing it:** update handlers register via *two* paths — declarative `#[update]` (→ `registry.update_handlers`) **and** imperative `ctx.register_update_handler` (→ the per-execution `WorkflowContext`, the common pattern, e.g. `metrics_integration::update_then_suspend_workflow`) — and only the declarative set is visible outside execution. **Bucketing against `registry.update_handlers` would therefore mislabel every legitimately imperatively-registered update as `__unregistered__`** (a worse regression than the theoretical risk; it also fails the existing `update_completed_metric_fires_on_the_suspend_path` label assertion). So each counter is bounded where it can be done *correctly*, and per-name visibility lives on the three post-resolution counters (`completed`/`failed`/`rejected`): **`update.failed`** (the concrete unbounded vector): bounded via the **result**, not the registry. A genuinely-unregistered name is exactly the one whose result is the pure, exact `"update handler '<name>' not found"` error minted by `execute_admitted_update`; the worker's `collect_update_result_metrics` (new pure `is_unregistered_update_failure(name, result)` helper) buckets **only** that case to the new `UNREGISTERED_UPDATE_NAME = "__unregistered__"` sentinel. Every real handler — declarative **or** imperative — keeps its name, because the discriminator is the not-found result, not the declarative registry. This collapses a hostile `POST /update/{RANDOM}` storm's failed samples to one series. **`update.completed`**: inherently bounded — a completed update always ran a real handler, so its name is the app's real handler set. **`update.rejected`**: already bounded — validator rejection fires only for a *registered* handler. **`update.admitted`**: **name dropped — bounded by construction (issue #684, follow-up).** The admission site has no result to key on and cannot see imperative handlers, so it *cannot* bound the name without mislabeling legitimate imperative updates. Rather than carry a raw, caller-controlled name (the earlier "documented residual"), the label is **dropped entirely** — `update.admitted` is now labeled `workflow` + `queue` only (queue is available at both admission sites: `execution.queue_name` in `store::admit_update_event`, `request.queue_name` in `update_with_start`). This is the only way to bound the counter's cardinality by construction. Per-name admission volume is recoverable in practice by correlating with the resolved counters — every real admit resolves to a `completed`/`failed` sample carrying the name, and a hostile-admit storm collapses to `update.failed{name="__unregistered__"}`. The durable `UpdateAdmitted` event always carries the **raw** name (the workflow needs it to resolve its handler); only the metric labels are bounded. **Net cardinality contract:** after this follow-up, **no** signal or update counter carries a name that is free-form at emission — signals are labeled `workflow`+`queue` only, `update.admitted` is `workflow`+`queue`, and `update.completed`/`failed`/`rejected` carry the `name` only after it has been resolved against a real handler (declarative or imperative; `failed` buckets a genuinely-unregistered name to `__unregistered__`). Per-name **signal** observability remains explicitly out of scope (no declared registry exists to bound it).
- **Phase 3.53** (implemented): Auto-heartbeat guard for long-running activities — see issue #682. **Before:** an activity that runs longer than its `heartbeat_timeout` but makes steady progress (a long transcode, a big batch job) had to either sprinkle `ctx.heartbeat(..)` calls through its body or hand-roll a `tokio::select!` + ticker in every such activity, or risk being spuriously reclaimed by the heartbeat-timeout scanner and dead-lettered. **After:** one line — `let _guard = ctx.start_auto_heartbeat_default()?;` — installs a background ticker that keeps the activity's `last_heartbeat_at` fresh for as long as the guard lives. New `ActivityContext` surface: `start_auto_heartbeat(interval)` and `start_auto_heartbeat_default()` (derives `interval = heartbeat_timeout / 3`), both returning a `#[must_use]` RAII `AutoHeartbeatGuard` (re-exported from `lib.rs` and the prelude alongside the sibling RAII handles `TimerHandle` / `Session` / `RaceWinner`); plus a `with_heartbeat_timeout(Duration)` builder and a `heartbeat_timeout` field the worker populates from the task row via the internal `with_heartbeat_timeout_opt` (the single worker.rs edit, on the `new_with_cancellation_check(..)` dispatch builder chain). **#151 read-path preservation.** A liveness-only auto-heartbeat that pings before any manual `ctx.heartbeat(..)` persists a JSON `null` into `harvest_task_queue.heartbeat_details`; a `start_to_close`/crash reclaim that preserves that column (the #151 contract) would then feed `null` back to the retry. `heartbeat_details::<T>()` now treats a stored JSON `null` as *no checkpoint* (`Ok(None)`) rather than a hard `Serialization` error — so a liveness ping never flips the documented `Ok(None)` resume API into a failure (and potential DLQ) or masks a real checkpoint. **Design.** The guard spawns a ticker on `self.cancel.child_token()`, so cancelling the activity's own token auto-stops the ticker while the handler still observes cancellation through `is_cancelled()` / `check_cancellation()` (the guard never swallows it). Dropping the guard — typically when the handler returns — cancels the child token and aborts the ticker. Each tick re-sends the activity's most recent heartbeat payload from a shared last-payload cell that `heartbeat()` now writes on every call (last-write-wins); the cell is seeded from the previous attempt's resume snapshot (`heartbeat_details`) so the first liveness ping preserves — rather than clobbers — the durable checkpoint used by `heartbeat_details()` on a later retry (issue #151 contract). With no manual heartbeat and no resume snapshot the liveness ping is a JSON `null`. A closed heartbeat channel makes the ticker `break` (never `.unwrap()`/panic); a zero-period interval is clamped to 1ms (a zero `tokio::time::interval` panics). **Guardrails.** Both methods reject with `HarvestError::Config` on a local activity or a no-flusher context (heartbeats are unsupported there), and reject when no `heartbeat_timeout` is configured — an auto-heartbeat whose liveness pings are never checked by the scanner would be a silent no-op, so the caller is told to configure `#[activity(heartbeat_timeout = "..")]`. **Liveness tradeoff (documented on both methods):** auto-heartbeat keeps a *progressing-but-not-manually-pinging* activity alive, but necessarily weakens heartbeat-based wedge detection for a live-but-deadlocked future. The independent `start_to_close` / `schedule_to_close` timeouts remain the hard wedge ceiling and are unaffected by heartbeats — pair auto-heartbeat with a `start_to_close` for a guaranteed runtime upper bound. **Invariants:** no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no management-API surface, no scanner/flusher/schema change. The timeout scanner (`timeout.rs`) and the batched heartbeat flusher (`heartbeat.rs`) are untouched — the guard simply feeds the existing flusher channel. **Tests.** Pure unit tests in `context.rs` under paused-clock time (`start_paused = true`): ticking sends payloads, guard-drop stops the ticker, cancellation stops it while `is_cancelled()` stays true, closed-channel exits cleanly (`AutoHeartbeatGuard::into_join_handle().await` returns `Ok(())` — a stronger no-panic proof than `is_finished()`, which is also true for a panicked task), last-write-wins re-send, liveness-only `null` ping, the require-`heartbeat_timeout` rejection (message-pinned) and the local/no-flusher rejection, the AC#2 `heartbeat_timeout / 3` interval derivation (a 9s timeout pings at exactly 3s — distinguishing `/3` from `/2`, `/1`, `*3`), the AC#4 #151 seed-from-resume-snapshot (the first liveness ping re-sends the resumed checkpoint, not `null`), and the stored-`null`→`Ok(None)` read-path. DB integration tests in `tests/integration/auto_heartbeat_tests.rs`: `auto_heartbeat_prevents_spurious_heartbeat_reclaim` drives a real worker + background timeout scanner and proves a long-running activity that only auto-heartbeats is never reclaimed via `TimeoutReason::Heartbeat` and completes (AC#8, success metric; widened freshness margin — 6s window, 2s interval — for CI headroom); `fresh_heartbeat_does_not_defeat_start_to_close` is a pure, deterministic scanner proof that a fresh `last_heartbeat_at` (what auto-heartbeat produces) shields the heartbeat timeout but NOT the independent `start_to_close` ceiling — and that a stale heartbeat IS reclaimed as `Heartbeat`, so the protection is real; `auto_heartbeat_activity_still_reclaimed_by_start_to_close` is the end-to-end complement — a real auto-heartbeating activity that wedges past a tight `start_to_close` is still reclaimed as `StartToClose` (never `Heartbeat`) and the workflow fails, the airtight full-composition proof. Example: `autumn-harvest/examples/auto_heartbeat.rs`.
- **Phase 3.54** (implemented): Update admit→terminal latency histogram — see issue #781. **Observability** (implemented): Closes the residual of issue #781 (PR #1032 shipped the six `harvest.*` signal/update lifecycle **counters**; this adds the remaining success metric — a p99 admit→complete latency panel). New histogram `harvest.update.duration` (`METRIC_UPDATE_DURATION`) records the wall-clock seconds from an update's durable admission (`UpdateAdmitted`) to its terminal result recording (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed`). **AC: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no macro-path change** — a pure additive-metrics slice modelled on the #519/#487 recipe (additive no-op-default trait method + `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge + coverage tests). **Naming / family:** shipped as `harvest.update.duration` (family-consistent with #1032's `harvest.update.*` counters, NOT the issue's literal `harvest.workflow.update.duration`). Prometheus series `harvest_update_duration_{bucket,count,sum}`. **Labels — `workflow`, `name`, `queue`, `outcome`** (all bounded; `execution.id`/`update_id` never a label, ADR-0001 §7). Mirrors the exact label vocabulary of the `harvest.update.completed`/`failed` counters (`workflow`, `name`, `queue` — the update name resolved to the registered/imperative handler set, an unregistered raw-route name bucketed to the `__unregistered__` sentinel by the shared `collect_update_result_metrics`), plus an `outcome` label (`completed`/`failed`) so one histogram covers both terminal kinds. **Rejected updates are excluded** — no handler runs, so they never enter the histogram. **Duration source:** the admit timestamp comes directly from the `UpdateAdmitted.timestamp` field already present in the loaded `history_events` slice (no new event variant, no timestamped-history load). The terminal time is `Utc::now()` at the post-commit emit (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed` carry no timestamp). New pure, unit-tested helper `worker::update_admit_duration_secs(admit_ts: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, now) -> Option<f64>` computes `(now - admit).max(ZERO)` in seconds — a clock-skew negative delta **clamps to `0`** (never a garbage/negative sample), and a `None` admit (the admit could not be resolved from history) **skips the histogram sample entirely** (the counter still fires with name `"unknown"`). **Emission point (piggybacks on #1032's exact path — inherits its delivery semantics):** `collect_update_result_metrics` was extended to carry the admit `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` alongside each `(name, completed)` pair, and `emit_update_result_metrics` now captures one `now` per cycle and calls `record_update_duration(workflow, name, queue, outcome, secs)` alongside the existing completed/failed counter emit — at all three call sites (the terminal/suspend `Persisted` arm and the two inline external-signal branches). No separate `is_replaying` gate: `RecordUpdateResult` is produced only on live execution and the emit is only post-commit, so exactly-once is inherited by construction. **Delivery semantics (documented by reference to the #684 counters, not over-claimed):** exactly-once on the happy path; a crash after the persist commit but before the post-commit emit drops the sample (at-most-once for that window, never a double-count). **`metrics_scrape.rs` — deliberately OMITTED (with justification):** the plugin's built-in Prometheus scrape recorder is per-metric hand-maintained (only `workflow_duration`/`activity_duration` histograms have a field + `record_*` override + `push_histogram` call; there is no generic histogram render path). The #1032 update lifecycle **counters are entirely absent** from it — the `HarvestMetricsRecorder` impl implements no `record_update_*`, so all update metrics fall through to the trait no-op and are exposed only via the `metrics-rs` adapter path. Adding `harvest.update.duration` there would be the lone update-family metric in the scrape recorder, inconsistent with its five sibling counters; omission is the consistent choice (the `_bucket` p99 series comes from the metrics-rs Prometheus exporter regardless). Bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` (`MetricsRsRecorder::record_update_duration` → `histogram!` with the `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_NAME`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE`/`METRIC_LABEL_OUTCOME` constants). One new dashboard panel (id 908, "Update latency (admit → terminal)") in the "Signal & update lifecycle" row of `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` — p99 `histogram_quantile` over `_bucket` plus a bucket-less `_sum`/`_count` avg fallback, mirroring the `harvest_workflow_pause_duration` panel. **No alert rule added** — panel only (an arbitrary latency threshold is a review-time decision). ADR-0001 §7 catalogue, `docs/telemetry.md` (emission-points + labels tables), and the CLAUDE.md telemetry module row updated; anti-drift coverage extended (`DASHBOARD_PROMETHEUS_SERIES` + `SERIES_LABELS` in `dashboard_pack_docs.rs`). Tests, TDD red→green (verified RED via compile errors + a live anti-drift failure): telemetry constant-name + no-op-default unit tests; `metrics_rs_adapter` label-content bridge test (`bridges_update_duration_histogram_with_bounded_labels`, via `metrics::with_local_recorder`); `worker.rs` pure unit tests (`update_admit_duration_secs` none/positive-delta/negative-clamp, and `collect_update_result_metrics_carries_admit_timestamp` — plus the four existing collect tests updated to the 3-tuple); `metrics_coverage.rs` reachability + bounded-label test (`update_duration_histogram_reachable_with_bounded_labels`); `dashboard_pack_docs.rs` anti-drift gate (panel + series + labels). All executed green in the sandbox (no-DB surfaces); the worker pure helpers run under `--features db --lib` without a live database.
- **Phase 3.55** (implemented): Run WASM-sandboxed polyglot activities inside the Rust worker — see issue #965. **R&D spike (not a committed GA feature)** proving polyglot activities: an activity implemented as a WebAssembly module — compiled from any guest language — runs sandboxed, metered, and hot-swappable inside the existing Rust worker, dispatched through the **standard task-queue path** (JSON in, JSON out, honouring the activity's queue/retry/start-to-close exactly like a native activity). One fleet, any guest language, capability-based sandboxing, per-invocation resource metering, and content-hash hot swap — capabilities no per-language-SDK durable-execution engine offers. Everything is behind the `wasm-activities` Cargo feature; the **default build carries zero new dependencies and is byte-for-byte unchanged** (the feature adds `wasmtime 46` + `wat`, and implies `db`). **Runtime (`src/wasm_activities.rs`).** A wasmtime 46 `Engine` configured once for deterministic resource bounding — `consume_fuel` (per-instruction CPU) + a single global epoch ticker (`harvest-wasm-epoch`, `increment_epoch()` every 1 ms) for wall-clock interruption + `StoreLimits` for a linear-memory ceiling. Each invocation gets a fresh `Store` with its own fuel budget and an **independent** wall-clock deadline: the store arms `set_epoch_deadline(1)` and installs an `epoch_deadline_callback` that, on every tick, compares `Instant::now()` against a per-invocation `hard_deadline` (`Instant` captured at dispatch, `checked_add`ed with the effective ceiling) and either interrupts or extends by one more tick. Bounding by **elapsed time**, not by a countdown of tick callbacks, is load-bearing: the epoch ticker fires every 1 ms but a guest only *observes* it at wasmtime's instrumented check points, so a single long bulk-memory instruction (a 16 MiB `memory.fill`) runs to completion between two checks and a tick-countdown deadline overshoots by that instruction's cost. Measured overrun of the old tick-countdown form was bounded at **1.2–2.3x** (each `memory.fill` is its own check point, so it does not compound) — not unbounded, but the documented ceiling is now exact rather than approximate (`wall_clock_ceiling_bounds_elapsed_time_not_callback_count`). N concurrent guests each get their own deadline off the same monotonic clock — one guest's expiry never trips another's (`concurrent_deadlines_are_independent`). The wall-clock ceiling (`max_wall_clock`, default **300 s**) is **mandatory**: a guest can spin without consuming fuel, and it runs on `spawn_blocking` and cannot be torn down before the ceiling — so fuel alone can never guarantee termination. **Guest ABI is core-WASM + JSON over linear memory:** the guest exports `memory`, `alloc(len)->ptr`, and `run(in_ptr,in_len)->i64` (packed `(ptr<<32)|len`); the host reinterprets the return as `u64` before shifting and bounds-checks every read/write against live guest memory (an OOB `(ptr,len)` is a typed `WasmTrap`, never a host OOB read). **Sandbox is deny-all by default:** a fresh empty `Linker` links a host function only for a capability explicitly granted via `WasmCapabilities` (`allow_clock`/`allow_random`/`allow_env` allowlist); filesystem and network are **not grantable** (no host function backs them), so any guest importing them is denied at instantiation. The granted `env::random_u64` host fn seeds each store's PRNG from a process-global `AtomicU64` counter itself seeded once from `rand::random::<u64>()`, so two processes (and two invocations) never replay the same draw sequence — an ungated fixed constant would make a guest's "randomness" predictable across the fleet (`rng_seed_stream_is_not_a_fixed_process_constant`). Classification is **precedence-ordered**: a `SandboxDenied` instantiation failure is returned *before* the cancellation/deadline reclassification, so a guest that imports a denied capability while its workflow is concurrently cancelled still surfaces the non-retryable denial rather than a retryable cancellation (`sandbox_denial_outranks_a_concurrent_cancellation`). **Storage + dispatch seam (`src/wasm_store.rs`).** Modules are content-hash (SHA-256) versioned and distributed via Postgres — no CDN/S3/broker in core. Table `harvest_wasm_modules` (the single additive migration `20260711000000_harvest_wasm_modules`) has a **composite PK `(hash, activity_name)`** so identical bytes bind to two names independently, plus a **partial unique index `WHERE active`** guaranteeing at most one active version per name. `publish_wasm_module` serialises concurrent publishes for the same name with a per-name transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, so two workers converge on exactly one active row. `resolve_wasm_dispatch` is **resolve-hash-first**: it resolves the active hash cheaply and serves a compiled module from the in-process content-addressed cache, fetching bytes **only** on a cache miss. Hot swap is atomic and restart-free — a new publish flips the active row; the next attempt sees it while an already-resolved in-flight attempt keeps running its pinned compiled module (`in_flight_dispatch_is_pinned_across_a_mid_flight_republish`). **Startup-seed is wired into `Worker::run`** (`seed_registered_wasm_modules`, the single startup batch helper — SEED not-clobber semantics: activate-only-if-no-active-version, so a restarted older worker cannot flip a hot-swapped shard back to its embedded version), so an embedder gets a working WASM activity by calling `HarvestBuilder::wasm_activity(WasmActivityRegistration::new(...))` alone. The always-activate `publish_wasm_module` remains the operator hot-swap primitive. `MAX_WASM_MODULE_BYTES` (32 MiB) is enforced before any hashing or DB work. `WasmActivityRegistration` carries the per-activity dispatch knobs a WASM activity can honour — `queue`, `max_attempts`/`retry`, `start_to_close`, and (added in review) `schedule_to_close` (`with_schedule_to_close`, `None` by default) — threaded into the generated `ActivityInfo` so a WASM activity gets the same cross-retry wall-clock deadline (#378) a native `#[activity]` does. The knobs deliberately **omitted** (heartbeat timeout, circuit breaker, rate limits, per-activity payload caps, `schedule_to_start`) are enumerated with rationale on the struct's docs — a WASM guest cannot heartbeat, so silently accepting a heartbeat timeout would be worse than not offering one. **Typed failures, no new event surface (AC6).** Every guest-controlled failure maps to a typed `ActivityFailure` recorded as an **ordinary `ActivityFailed`**: sandbox denial → non-retryable `SandboxDenied`; fuel/wall-clock/memory-growth → retryable `ResourceExhausted`; trap/ABI-violation/non-JSON-output/contained host-glue panic → retryable `WasmTrap`; plus `WasmModuleUnavailable` / `WasmModuleInvalid` (non-retryable) / `WasmModuleLookupFailed` (retryable) for the storage layer. A host-glue panic is caught (`catch_unwind`), so a guest can never crash the worker and a runaway module never trips the poison-pill quarantine (#367). A WASM activity is **indistinguishable from a native one in history**: it records the same `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted`/`ActivityFailed` events. **Zero new `WorkflowEvent` variants, zero replay impact, exactly one additive migration.** (The memory-growth classification is a string match on the wasmtime error Debug form, guarded by a test — revisit on a wasmtime bump.) **R&D exit criteria (AC8).** Written recommendation in `docs/rnd/wasm-activities-spike.md` covering runtime choice (wasmtime vs wasmer), core-WASM vs component-model ABI, guest interface shape (JSON-over-buffer vs WIT-typed), the **partial** heartbeat/cancellation story (timeouts delivered via epoch/fuel; cooperative heartbeat/cancel host imports are the biggest GA gap — a "cancelled" guest holds a blocking thread until its ceiling), the measured cold-start/instantiation cost, the security posture, and the storage/distribution model — all backed by the working spike. **Success metric — met.** `runs_one_native_and_one_wasm_activity_to_completion` drives a single workflow running **1 native + 1 WASM** activity to COMPLETED through the real worker loop, asserting both outputs are correct **and** that history carries only ordinary `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted` (no wasm-specific type). The `#[ignore]`d `dispatch_overhead_wasm_echo_vs_native` microbenchmark measures per-invocation overhead of a **cached** echo (compilation excluded) vs a native closure and now **asserts** the issue's `< 10 ms` p99 budget rather than only printing it: measured WASM p99 ≈ 474 µs, native p99 ≈ 5 µs, **overhead p99 ≈ 469 µs — ~21× under the < 10 ms target** (debug build, so a release worker is faster). The sandbox suite denies 100 % of ungranted FS/network/env attempts. **Example.** `autumn-harvest/examples/wasm_activity.rs` (`required-features = ["wasm-activities"]`) assembles a WAT guest inline via `wat::parse_str`, registers it via `HarvestBuilder::wasm_activity(...)`, and demonstrates a capability grant and a sandbox denial. `autumn-harvest/examples/wasm-guests/` holds the WAT guest source (`echo.wat`, now the single source of truth `include_str!`d by both the example and the integration suite — no more drifting inline copies), an AssemblyScript guest (`echo.ts`) implementing the same `alloc`/`run` ABI **plus its committed `asc`-compiled `echo.wasm` artifact**, and a `README.md` documenting the ABI, the `asc` build command, and why a real-toolchain guest is worth testing alongside hand-written WAT. That AssemblyScript guest is **executed end-to-end in CI** (`worker_runs_an_assemblyscript_compiled_guest_to_completion`), which is what actually substantiates the polyglot claim — and it immediately earned its keep: `asc --runtime stub` emits a module with **zero initial memory pages**, so a naive bump-pointer `alloc` handed back an out-of-bounds address and the first run failed with a `WasmTrap`. A hand-written `.wat` guest declaring `(memory 1)` can never surface that class of bug. The guest's `alloc` now grows linear memory before returning. **Test evidence (recounted precisely — verified by `cargo test` name enumeration, not estimated).** **70 unit tests** across the `wasm` filter: **45** in `src/wasm_activities.rs` (runtime: deadline math, hash/cache, echo round-trip, the three sandbox-deny categories, the three capability grants + in-band env denial, fuel/memory/wall-clock/mandatory-ceiling exhaustion, concurrent-deadline isolation, the elapsed-time wall-clock bound, RNG seed-stream variation, sandbox-denial precedence, and the containment suite), **15** in `src/wasm_store.rs` (registration defaults/setters incl. `schedule_to_close`, binding projection, size cap), plus 2 in `worker.rs`, 2 in `builder.rs`, and 6 in `failure.rs`. **26** tests in `tests/integration/wasm_activities_tests.rs` — **25 run in CI** via the `linux autumn-harvest integration wasm-activities wasm_activities_tests` manifest row (storage round-trips, hot-swap + single-active + composite-PK independence, the concurrent-publish race, oversized-module reject, startup-publish, `resolve_wasm_dispatch` unavailable/invalid/invoke, the worker-e2e echo, the **AssemblyScript-compiled guest e2e**, the sandbox-denial terminal, the in-flight pin, the **live-worker hot swap reaching the next attempt without a restart** (asserted within `< 5 s`), the fuel-retry — which also asserts `crash_strikes == 0` and zero DLQ rows, proving a runaway guest never trips the poison-pill quarantine (#367) — and the 1-native + 1-WASM success-metric e2e) plus 1 `#[ignore]`d overhead microbenchmark. All integration tests **ran green against a local Postgres 16** during development (via `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`); CI executes them Docker-backed via the manifest row. CI additionally runs the `wasm_activity` example under the feature on Linux, so the documented embedder entry point is compile- and run-checked rather than prose-only. The `wasm-activities` feature is out of the default build, so the default build and `cargo tree -i wasmtime` (default features) are unchanged / empty. **MSRV note:** the feature has an effective MSRV of **1.94** (wasmtime 46.0.1's own minimum), distinct from the crate's core MSRV of **1.88** — the default build and the CI MSRV job (`cargo check --workspace`, default features) never compile wasmtime and are unaffected, so the crate continues to advertise `rust-version = 1.88.0` for every non-`wasm` consumer.
- **Phase 3.56** (implemented): DAG node input binding: pass data between graph nodes — see issue #702. A `#[dag]` node's activity is fed the DAG's *trigger input* (wrapped in a `{ "conf": …, "dag_task": "<name>" }` envelope), **not** the output of the upstream node it depends on — so a classic `extract → transform → load` pipeline, where each stage consumes the prior stage's output, forced authors to flatten the pipeline into one mega-activity or hand-thread outputs through shared state. **Node input binding** closes that gap: bind a node's activity input directly to one or more upstream node outputs, one builder call per data edge, zero hand-written output-threading. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, core-only** — node inputs are computed deterministically in the workflow body from already-recorded `ActivityCompleted` outputs (frozen in `harvest_events` before the bound node is dispatched), so replay reconstructs byte-identical inputs on every worker and every pass. Bindings take effect on the unified workflow-execution path (`unified-dag-execution`). **API — three fluent `DagTaskRef` methods** (all by-value `self -> Self`): `.input_from(&upstream)` — the bound activity receives that upstream's recorded output **verbatim** (`DagInputBinding::Single`). No `conf`/`dag_task` envelope (AC2). `.input_from_all(&[&a, &b])` — a JSON object merging every upstream's output, keyed by each upstream's **activity name** (`DagInputBinding::Merged`). `.input_from_aliased(&[("k", &up), …])` — the same merge, keyed by the **given alias**. New public types re-exported from `autumn_harvest`: `DagInputBinding { Single(usize), Merged(Vec<DagMergeSource>) }` and `DagMergeSource { key: String, upstream_index: usize }`. **Binding implies the dependency edge (AC4).** Each method auto-adds the upstream to `task.upstreams` (deduped), so no separate `.upstream(&up)` is required — a binding *is* a data edge, and the bound node runs only after its bound upstream(s) have recorded their outputs. An extra explicit `.upstream(&up)` is harmless. This is the faithful reconciliation of AC4's "binding implies a dependency edge": the edge is auto-added at bind time rather than requiring a literal `.upstream(…)` (or a macro-level error for its absence). Binding edges accumulate across calls while the binding itself is last-wins, so a bound upstream also appears in the node's `.condition(|ups| …)` slice in builder call order. **Semver.** Adding a `pub input_from` field to `DagTask` and new variants to the (non-`#[non_exhaustive]`) `DagBuildError` is a minor addition that is breaking only for a downstream exhaustive `match` on those types — consistent with the repo's existing `WorkflowInfo`/`ActivityInfo` public-field-addition norm. **Raw output vs. the trigger-input `dag_task` wrapper (AC2/AC3).** At runtime the unified level walker (`run_unified_dag`) resolves a bound node's activity input via the pure `bind_activity_input(binding, &outputs)`: the raw upstream output for `Single`, or a keyed `serde_json::Map` for `Merged` — with **no** `dag_task` injection and **no** `conf` wrapping. The unbound branch (trigger-input + `dag_task` envelope) is left byte-identical, so an unbound DAG is unchanged (AC3, regression-guarded). **Skipped/failed upstream → deterministic `Value::Null` (AC6).** The `outputs` vector is initialized to `Value::Null` per node, and a skipped-or-failed node never overwrites its slot, so a binding to such an upstream contributes `Value::Null` — never a missing key. A bound node whose upstream was skipped is itself skipped by default; give it `TriggerRule::AllDone` to run anyway and branch on null-vs-payload. **Five build-time error guards** (all in `DagBuilder::build`, caught at compile-of-the-DAG time, never at run time): `DagBuildError::ConflictingInputBinding { task }` — a node declares both an `input_from` binding and a mapped upstream (`.map_activity(…).over(…)`); the two are contradictory input sources. `DagBuildError::DuplicateInputBindingKey { task, key }` — a `Merged` binding has a repeated key: two upstreams sharing an activity name via `input_from_all`, or a repeated alias via `input_from_aliased`. `DagBuildError::EmptyInputBinding { task }` — a `Merged` binding has no upstream sources (an empty `input_from_all(&[])` / `input_from_aliased(&[])` would deliver an empty JSON object). `DagBuildError::InputBindingOnGate { task }` — a signal-gate node declares an `input_from*` binding; a gate dispatches no activity, so the binding is the same category as a binding on a `map_activity` node (`ConflictingInputBinding`) and is rejected. `DagBuildError::InputBindingNotAnUpstream { task }` — a bound source is not a declared upstream; unreachable via the public API (bindings auto-add the edge), validated defensively. An `input_from*` on a signal-gate node is a build error (`InputBindingOnGate`). This closes a review finding: a gate dispatches no activity, so the binding *value* is ignored — but unlike the inert activity-only setters (`.queue()`, `.retry()`, `.start_to_close()`), a binding also auto-adds a dependency edge, which would silently make the gate wait for that upstream before its signal wait.
