Production intentionally **concatenates** per admission (issue #921) and dedups only at delivery, so the stored value is `[hook, hook, hook]` (len 3), not `[hook]` — the concatenate-and-merge contract proven by the passing sibling `a_later_admissions_completion_callbacks_are_merged_not_dropped` (two distinct targets → len 2). Fixed the assertion to expect the concatenated union. **CI wiring + allowlist:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s Docker-backed step for `workflow_retry_tests::workflow_typed` (a `::` sub-filter that masked the other tests) was expanded to run the full `workflow_retry_tests` module, and new Docker-backed run steps were added for `completion_callback_tests` and `event_batch_tests` (matching the file's `-p autumn-harvest --test integration -- <module> --test-threads=1`, `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` convention). The three entries were removed from `ci_run_coverage.rs`'s `ALLOWLIST`, `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` dropped 77 → 74, and the two now-unused reason constants (`ALLOWLIST_WORKFLOW_RETRY_REASON`, `ALLOWLIST_COMPLETION_CALLBACK_REASON`) removed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact, no production-logic change** — test-harness fixes + CI wiring only. - **CI** — manifest-driven integration-suite runner (test-infra). Replaced the ~35 copy-pasted per-suite `cargo test` steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test` job — 29 Docker-backed run steps, the shared 17-token plugin `--no-run` compile line, the `mcp_tools_integration` compile step, and 5 all-OS target-run steps — with **one parameterized runner** (`.github/ci/run-suites.sh`) reading a **line-oriented, `merge=union`-safe manifest** (`.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`). Adding an integration suite is now **one sorted manifest line** — no `ci.yml` edit, no shared-tail conflict. **Root cause fixed.** Three shared append-tail regions made any two concurrent suite-adding PRs collide: the per-suite Docker run steps, the one physical plugin `--no-run` line (every new plugin suite appended a `--test` token to it), and the Rust `ALLOWLIST` array. The manifest is `merge=union` (see `.gitattributes`), so two PRs each appending a line both land with **no textual conflict**; a union-merge duplicate/reorder residue is caught deterministically (never a conflict) by `ci_run_coverage.rs::manifest_is_sorted_and_unique`, which prints a one-command `sort -u` fix. **Manifest schema** (`osclass crate target features filter`, whitespace-columnar, `#`-comment tolerant, `-` = none): `osclass` ∈ `linux` (run serial on Linux against Docker Postgres + compile-checked on every OS) | `allos` (run on all 3 OSes, parallel, no live DB) | `compileonly` (`--no-run` on every OS, never executed). `--test-threads=1` and `--no-run` are **derived from `osclass`** by the runner and never written in the manifest — so the `--test-threads=1`-after-`--`-after-filter ordering is correct by construction (kills the mis-emit class). For `autumn-harvest` `integration` `allos` rows the runner adds `--no-default-features` (strips the crate's `default = ["db", "unified-dag-execution"]`, since `allos` has no Postgres); this reproduces the old `:142`/`:145` commands byte-for-byte while leaving the `property` `allos` row (which keeps `db`+`unified-dag-execution`) unchanged. **Every generated command is byte-faithful to the pre-refactor `ci.yml`.** **Runner** (`.github/ci/run-suites.sh`, `run <linux|allos>` and `compile` modes) is bash-3.2 / Git-Bash portable (no associative arrays, no `mapfile`; compile-mode batching groups by `(crate, features)` via `sort` + adjacent-run walk). It wraps each suite in `::group::`/`::endgroup::`, **collects failures instead of aborting on the first** (a strict improvement over the old fail-fast leg, which hid every suite after the first failure), and exits non-zero at the end printing every failed suite. `compile` mode regenerates both the shared plugin `--no-run` batch and the `mcp,unified-dag-execution` batch from the manifest, so every `linux`/`compileonly` plugin target is still compile-checked on macOS/Windows. **Gating preserved exactly.** The 3 replacing steps keep **per-step** `if:` (`allos`/`compile` → `needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`; `linux` → `runner.os == 'Linux' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`) and `shell: bash` — never hoisted to a job-level `if:` on the matrix job (which would strip the leg contexts and hang branch protection). The heterogeneous steps (fmt/clippy, `--lib`, the core blanket `--all-features --tests --no-run` compile, `cargo build --example`, whole-crate and example runs, `cargo clean`) stay hand-written. **Coverage guard rewrite** (`autumn-harvest/tests/integration/ci_run_coverage.rs`) now derives "which suites have a real CI run" from the **manifest** (structured columns) instead of scraping `ci.yml` `run:` lines: the `--test-threads=1` special-casing, `--no-run` string-grepping, and `module::filter` re-tokenization are deleted. Preserved: the ratcheted `ALLOWLIST` + `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` cap (73 entries / cap 77, unchanged — the covered set is identical), feature-awareness (a `testing`+`db` suite's manifest row must carry `testing`), the plugin dir-scan, the all-`#[ignore]`d handling, and the stale-allowlist check. Added: (i) `ci_yaml_invokes_the_runner_against_the_manifest` (a manifest can't be silently ignored — `ci.yml` must invoke `run-suites.sh {compile, run allos, run linux}` and the script must reference the manifest path), and (ii) `manifest_is_sorted_and_unique` (union-artifact self-heal with a `sort -u` fix message). The guard was proven fail-closed: deleting one `linux` line makes it fail naming that suite and printing the exact manifest line to re-add. **Adding a suite going forward:** append one sorted line to `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` (keep the header comment on top; `sort -u` the data lines). No `ci.yml` edit; no `ALLOWLIST` edit for a wired suite. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no runtime-code change — CI infrastructure only.

- **#476-parity — signal-or-deadline race follow-ups (from PR #1029 review).** Two fixes to the issue #476 `receive_signal_timeout` / `wait_for_signal_timeout` machinery, porting fixes already made to the issue #779 child-timeout twin (PR #1029). `context.rs`-only plus one pure read-only `replay.rs` helper; **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** (1) **Timer-retention leak on signal-win:** the still-armed `__signal_timeout:{seq}:{name}` durable timer was left `fired=false` in `harvest_timers` forever (a completed workflow's task is never re-claimed to ingest `TimerFired`, and `retention::should_skip_candidate` treats any pending timer as an inflight dependency), permanently pinning the run against retention. The `SignalOrTimerMatch::SignalWon` arm now pushes `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { timers: [timer_id] }` (applied by `worker::apply_race_loser_cancellations` → `queue::delete_pending_timer`), **gated on the new pure `HistoryMatcher::history_contains_timer_started(&timer_id)`** so the stashed-signal-before-race short-circuit (which records no `TimerStarted`) emits no spurious teardown — a discriminator the child twin doesn't need (a winning child always records `ChildWorkflowStarted`+`TimerStarted`). The redundant `CancelRaceLosers` push in `race_timer_signal_impl` was removed (exactly one teardown per race-win). Re-pushing on every strict-replay cycle is divergence-free (`CancelRaceLosers` appends no event; `delete_pending_timer` is idempotent). Inherited residuals — a workflow-handler panic before persist (#782) or a history-hard-cap seal on the same cycle drops the pending teardown — documented not fixed, identical to the twin. (2) **Canary-frontier false non-determinism:** `match_signal_or_timer`'s `InProgress` arm errored unconditionally under `strict_replay`, so a deploy replay canary (`run_workflow_canary`) over a parked signal-timeout race false-reported non-determinism. Now suppressed under `self.canary_mode && at_frontier` (`at_frontier = !m.has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed()`), byte-identical to the child twin's `InProgress` guard; non-canary strict `WorkflowReplayer` runs still error (fixture-problem detection intact) and a genuine `Diverged` result always errors. (3) **Over-deadline reorder — deliberate refute:** unlike child terminals (appended out-of-band by worker child-wake / operator cancel-terminate / child execution-timeout), signals have no out-of-band `SignalReceived` append — `send_signal` only queues a `harvest_signals` row and wakes; `SignalReceived` is materialized solely by `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`, which atomically interleaves signal-vs-deadline by DB clock via `merge_wake_events` (`received_at < fires_at` ⇒ signal-first) — so the twin's `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` hazard is structurally unreachable. Documented as a rustdoc asymmetry note on `wait_for_signal_timeout`; the existing `signal_timeout_timeout_branch_with_ignored_late_signal_replays_succeeded` replayer test already pins the "late signal after `TimerFired` loses" contract. **This supersedes the stale Phase 3.24 note** that "`wait_for_signal_timeout` itself still leaves its timer armed on signal-win — the same latent retention leak, tracked as a separate follow-up." Tests (red→green, no-DB): two `context.rs` unit tests (exactly-one / zero teardown), a `history_contains_timer_started` matcher test, four `replayer_tests.rs` canary-parity tests.

Neither the existing `migration_hygiene` completeness guard nor the `ci_run_coverage` run-coverage guard catches a reintroduced hand-rolled bundle. **After:** a no-DB guard in `tests/integration/migration_hygiene.rs` fails if any file under `autumn-harvest/tests/**` or `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/**` contains a hand-rolled migration `include_str!` outside a small, commented allowlist — making the paved path self-enforcing. **No product-code behavior change.** **Allowlist** (deliberately-partial fixtures, each entry commented with why): `integration_e2e.rs` (legacy upgrade-path / workflow-start-uniqueness excluded); `schedule_update_integration.rs` (omits `harvest_start_throttle` for the `to_regclass` graceful-degradation path); `timeline_integration.rs` (inserts into `harvest_dag_runs`, which the full bundle drops — `20260514000000_drop_harvest_dag_runs`); and `outbox_integration.rs` (a separate plugin app-DB `harvest_workflow_outbox` migration, not part of the core `migrations/` bundle). Adding a new partial fixture requires a conscious allowlist edit + documented reason. **Design:** the guard is *bidirectional* — it fails both on a new offender outside the allowlist **and** on a stale allowlist entry (a fixture later converted to `full_migrations_sql()` that no longer contains a hand-rolled include), so the allowlist can't rot. Detection is text-based (per-line: `include_str!` + `migrations` + `up.sql`), so it catches a reintroduction regardless of `#[cfg]` gating; the guard file itself is excluded (it carries those tokens as literals), and `ci_run_coverage.rs`'s own non-migration `include_str!(".github/...")` lines are correctly not flagged. A pure unit test (`line_detector_flags_a_handrolled_include_and_ignores_others`) locks the detector semantics. **No new suite** — a test fn added to the already-run no-DB `migration_hygiene` target, so no `integration-suites.txt` change; `ci_run_coverage` is unchanged (stays 13/13). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact, no production-logic change** — test infra only. Verification: red→green demonstrated (a stray hand-rolled `include_str!` appended to the non-allowlisted `audit_tests.rs` fails the guard naming that file; reverted → green); `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings` clean; `migration_hygiene` 6/6 (was 4) and `ci_run_coverage` 13/13 green in the no-DB leg. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** the offender scan now uses a whole-file structural detector (`detects_handrolled_migration_include`) that collapses whitespace before checking each `include_str!` argument, so it catches the **rustfmt-wrapped** multi-line form (`include_str!(` and its `"…/migrations/…/up.sql"` path string on separate lines) that the previous per-line scan missed. The structural check is also strictly more precise — the tokens must belong to a real `include_str!` argument — so prose/doc comments merely mentioning `migrations/…/up.sql` are no longer flagged. The 4-entry allowlist and the single-line `line_is_handrolled_migration_include` unit predicate are unchanged.

Because the full `metrics_integration` module is now green on PG16 (17/17), it moves off the `ci_run_coverage` allowlist onto a real CI run row in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` so the fix stays guarded. No production code changed. The two remaining #1045 failures — the start-throttle admission-gate and `query_integration::ac6` (`drive_query_replay` misclassifying a `yield_now` spin as `410` instead of `408`) — turned out to be real production bugs and are tracked in separate PRs.
- **Fix** — query-replay suspension classification: spinning terminal query is 408, cold-park query serves fast (issue #612). `executor::drive_query_replay` (the read-only replay driver behind post-mortem queries on terminal workflows, issue #612) misclassified `Poll::Pending` cycles because it inferred workflow suspension from a custom `QueryReplayWaker` flag — assuming `tokio::task::yield_now()` calls the waker synchronously — but inside a tokio runtime (the real HTTP query path) `yield_now` **defers** its wake to the scheduler queue rather than invoking the custom waker synchronously. The sync driver's tight manual poll loop never yields back to the scheduler, so the deferred wake was never delivered and a genuinely-spinning terminal query was misread as a command-suspension → `classify_terminal_query(Suspended, sealed=false)` → **410** instead of the #612-documented **408**. **Fix (executor-scoped redesign):** discriminate a `Poll::Pending` by a **per-poll delta** on the emitted replay-significant command count, then a **three-way** suspension discriminator: **Case 1 — command this poll** (positive delta): a genuine workflow suspension on a durable command (`WaitForActivity`/`StartTimer`/`WaitForSignal`/`StartChildWorkflow`/`ContinueAsNew`/…) → `Suspended`. **Case 2 — self-wake spin** (zero delta, `QueryReplayWaker` flag set): a `tokio::task::yield_now()` spin → keep driving to the deadline → `TimedOut` → 408. **Case 3 — command-less cold park** (zero delta, flag cold): the workflow parked waiting on an external re-poll that never comes during a query drive (the sole engine primitive that does this is non-timeout `ctx.await_condition`, which pushes no command and leaves its waker cold) → `Suspended` **immediately**, so a RUNNING query over such a park serves its partial state fast rather than burning the whole `query_timeout` budget, and a terminal run sealed while parked on it serves 200 (not 408/410). The command signal is now a **delta** (`WorkflowContext::count_commands`), not a bare "any pending" peek: the command buffer is never drained during a query drive, so an "any pending" check stays true forever after the first command and would misclassify a *later* cold `await_condition` park as still making progress and busy-drive it to 408 — the delta reflects only what THIS poll emitted. Command classification reuses the executor's shared `is_replay_significant_command` deny-list (`UpsertSearchAttributes`/`SetCurrentDetails`/`CancelRaceLosers`), also used by the `run_strict_with_ctx`/`run_workflow_canary` non-determinism checks, so command kinds are never re-enumerated by hand. **Sync + async twin driver.** The 16 pure `#[test]` callers run out of a tokio runtime (where `yield_now` fires synchronously) and keep the synchronous `drive_query_replay`; the single production caller (`hydrate_ctx_for_query`, already async) now uses `drive_query_replay_async`, which opens a **single `tokio::task::yield_now().await` quiet window** on a zero-delta poll to observe tokio's *deferred* `yield_now` wake before deciding case 2 vs case 3 — replacing the old busy-wait `std::thread::yield_now()`, so a spinning query cooperatively yields the runtime each cycle instead of hard-pinning a core. Both loop over one shared, `!Send`-safe `poll_query_step` helper that **builds and drops the `waker_ref`/`std::task::Context` internally**, so nothing `!Send` crosses the async driver's `.await` (the returned future stays `Send`, as the axum handler requires). **Behavior change:** a spinning query on a terminal workflow returns **408** (retryable request timeout) instead of a misleading **410**; a RUNNING or sealed-while-parked query over `await_condition` now serves fast/200 instead of burning the full budget. The #612 contracts are preserved: sealed-while-parked runs still `Suspended` → **200**, truncated history (no terminal seal) still → **410**, code-drift still → **410**, unregistered name still → **404**. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change** — production files only (`executor.rs`, `context.rs`, plugin `api.rs` call site). Pure `query_terminal` suite green (19/19, incl. the new RED→GREEN `await_condition` fast-suspend and sealed-while-parked tests, both proven to busy-drive to timeout under the old `any_pending_command` guard); `query_integration::ac6_spinning_replay_returns_408` still 408. Both suites run in CI.
- **`harvest det-check` CLI — the runnable front door for `det_check`, plus one first-party hop of transitive reachability (issue #778).** Turns the already-shipped `det_check` engine (DET001–DET011, `harvest-suppress`, `DetCheckReport`, `has_hard_blockers`) — which had **no runnable front door** — into a governance gate authors actually invoke, and closes the exact coverage gap #386 punted: a non-deterministic call (`chrono::Utc::now()`, `rand::random()`, …) factored out of a `#[workflow]` body into a **first-party helper function the body calls directly** used to sail past `cargo build`, the macro lint, and the body scanner, only to DLQ post-deploy. **Read-only source analysis: no `WorkflowEvent` variant, no event-schema change, no migration, no change to the `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path contract, no runtime code touched.** *(PR #1055.)* **Engine (`autumn-harvest/src/det_check.rs`):** (a) **serde (AC2)** — `DetSeverity` (with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` → `"error"`/`"warning"`), `DetLocation`, `DetFinding`, `DetSuppression`, and `DetCheckReport` now derive `serde::Serialize` for `--format json`. (b) **`DetLocation.col` (AC1)** — a new `pub col: u32` (always `> 0`), computed as the 1-based character column of the matched substring in the raw source line for the substring-table rules (DET001–DET009, DET011); the bespoke DET010 pass and any offset-less site report `1`. (c) **`DetFinding.via_helper: Option<String>` (AC4)** — `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`; `None` for a direct-in-body finding (`workflow_name = Some(wf)`, unchanged), `Some(helper)` for a transitive finding (`workflow_name = Some(entry_point)`, `location` = the offending line inside the helper). (d) **Transitive reachability** — the old `#[workflow]`-only `extract_workflow_bodies` is generalized to `extract_all_functions`, which walks each file tracking brace depth and captures every **top-level** (file-depth-0) `fn` definition with `is_workflow`/`is_activity` flags and an owned body (so a cross-file index can outlive per-file line buffers); methods inside `impl`/`trait` blocks (depth > 0) are never captured. `check_source` resolves one-hop calls within one file; `check_dir` first builds a first-party function index across every `*.rs` in the tree, then follows one hop of **direct free-function calls** (`helper(` — never `x.helper(` method calls, never `m::helper(` path-qualified calls, never identifier-continuation) from each `#[workflow]` body into plain (non-workflow, non-activity) helpers, scans those helper bodies with the *same* per-body analysis (all rules, suppressions included), and attributes findings to the entry point via `via_helper`. **One hop only** (workflow → A → B is not followed into B); **`#[activity]` callees are skipped** (an activity legitimately reading the clock reached from a workflow is not flagged); a helper **name defined by more than one plain helper is ambiguous and never resolved**, so an ambiguous resolution can never introduce a false positive. Findings are deduped by `(rule_id, entry-workflow, file, line)`. `check_dir` now also **skips `target` and hidden directories** so a scan of a repo root stays fast and never lints generated code. **CLI (`autumn-harvest-cli`):** new `harvest det-check [PATHS...]` subcommand (default `.`). Local `--format text|json` flag (distinct from the global `--output`), `--deny-warnings`, and `--list-suppressions`. Handled entirely in-process before the HTTP execute path (mirrors the Tui early-return; `api_request()` for it is `unreachable!`). Text mode prints `file:line:col DETxxx (safe alternative: …)` per finding — with `[in helper `H` reached from workflow `W`]` for a transitive finding — plus an always-echoed `suppressed:` audit footer (AC5). `--list-suppressions` prints `file:line RULEID "reason"` per active suppression and exits `0` (AC6). Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` on any hard-blocker (or, with `--deny-warnings`, any warning); findings/JSON are always on stdout before the non-zero exit. New `CliError::DetCheckFindings { errors, warnings }` (exit code `1`, the default arm). Formatting/gating live in pure, unit-testable helpers (`det_check_report_for_paths`, `format_det_findings_text`, `format_det_suppressions`, `format_det_suppressions_list`, `det_check_json`, `det_check_gate`, `run_det_check`). **AC4 boundary (mirrors #386):** `#[activity]` bodies, method/path-qualified calls, two-plus hops, third-party crates, trait-object dispatch, function pointers, and closures-captured-by-reference are all out of scope. **AC8 (tree is clean):** `harvest det-check autumn-harvest/src autumn-harvest/examples autumn-harvest-plugin/src autumn-harvest-cli/src` reports **zero** hard-blocker findings in ~0.9 s. One pre-existing offender surfaced and was resolved with the sanctioned escape hatch: `autumn-harvest/examples/deterministic_primitives.rs` reads `std::env::var("DEPLOY_REGION")` **inside a `ctx.side_effect(...)` closure** (a deterministic, recorded-once read the text scanner can't see through) — suppressed with `// harvest-suppress: DET004 "env read is wrapped in ctx.side_effect(); recorded once and replayed deterministically"`. A whole-workspace `harvest det-check .` scan (~1.4 s) surfaces only the deliberately-non-deterministic trybuild fixtures under `autumn-harvest/tests/compile_fail/` — **true positives** that exist precisely to be rejected by the compile-time guardrail, left unmodified (a comment line would shift their committed `.stderr` snapshots and break the macro tests). **Docs (AC7):** new "Running the check in CI" section in `docs/workflow-determinism-guide.md` — flags, exit-code contract, the AC4 boundary, a GitHub Actions job snippet, and a git pre-commit hook, plus the note that the shipped examples/fixtures pass. **Success metric (proven by test):** a 14-workflow fixture (7 hard-blocker classes × {direct-in-body, one-hop-in-helper}) flags **100% of the 7 helper-reachable (transitive) violations** — the class today's macro lint + scanner catch 0% of — and produces exactly 14 findings (zero false positives on the fixture), with the self-scan of `autumn-harvest/src` staying clean (well under the < 5 s / no-DB / no-dependent-build budget; ~0.9 s measured). **Tests:** engine — transitive same-file / cross-file (`check_dir` over a tempdir) / two-hop-not-flagged / activity-callee-not-flagged / method-call-not-resolved / clean-helper boundary tests, the 14-fixture success-metric test, and `via_helper`/`col`/serde-round-trip metadata tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/det_check_tests.rs`, plus `fn_decl_name`/`is_activity_attr` module unit tests. CLI — inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests in `src/lib.rs` (parse → `Commands::DetCheck { format: Json, .. }`, defaults, `DetCheckFormat::default() == Text`, the text-line/suppression formatters, `det_check_gate`, exit-code, JSON serialization) and black-box integration tests in `tests/integration/det_check_cli.rs` (text + JSON attribution over a tempdir, clean tree → Ok, `--deny-warnings` gating, `--list-suppressions` listing, hard-blocker → exit 1, missing-path read error). Deliberately **not** added to `request_mapping.rs`/`contract_coverage.rs` (no HTTP route — mirrors Tui/Events). **Post-review hardening (four-agent review):** (1) **AC8 — bare `harvest det-check` at the repo root now exits `0`.** `collect_rs_sources` / `check_paths` skip any directory named `compile_fail` (alongside `target` and hidden dirs), so the deliberately-broken trybuild fixtures under `autumn-harvest/tests/compile_fail/` — true positives that exist to be rejected by the compile-time guardrail and carry committed `.stderr` snapshots — are no longer lint-flagged by the text pre-check; a bare `det-check` (default `.`) reports zero findings. (2) **Zero-FP — closures and fn-pointer params never resolve to a same-named free helper** (#386 explicitly excludes function pointers and closures). `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` now shadow-suppresses any call whose name is bound by the caller: parameter names (`FnDef.params`, over-collected from the param list via `extract_fn_params`) plus body `let`/closure bindings (`collect_body_let_idents`, reusing `det010_parse_let`). Safe-direction: a name that is both shadowed and legitimately a free-fn call is conservatively skipped (an accepted false-negative, never a false-positive). (3) **Multi-file / symlink / non-UTF-8 — one shared cross-path index.** New engine entry point `check_paths(&[&Path])` collects the full `.rs` source set across **all** path arguments into a **single** first-party index and scans once, so a cross-file transitive violation is caught even when the two files are passed as **separate** arguments (the `det-check $(git diff --name-only '*.rs')` changed-files CI pattern that per-file scanning silently missed — a false-negative on a determinism gate). It de-duplicates overlapping arguments (a dir plus a file inside it, or a repeated path) by canonicalized path so nothing double-counts; skips symlinked files and directories via `entry.file_type()?.is_symlink()` (a self-referential dir symlink can no longer explode the scan, and a `../..` symlink can no longer pull out-of-tree files in); and skips a single unreadable / non-UTF-8 `.rs` file mid-walk with a warning naming the file rather than `?`-aborting the whole scan. A missing top-level path argument still surfaces as an error. `check_dir`/`check_file` are unchanged. The CLI's `det_check_report_for_paths` now calls `check_paths` once instead of merging per-path `check_file`/`check_dir` reports. (4) **`--list-suppressions --format json` now emits JSON** (via the new `det_suppressions_json` helper) instead of silently falling back to the text listing; default stays text. (5) **Docs:** the AC7 GitHub Actions job and pre-commit hook use the now-clean argless `harvest det-check` (the old `det-check src examples` recipe failed on this repo, which has no root `src/`), with a note that a larger downstream workspace can enumerate specific crate `src` directories; a new "Known limitations (conservative, safe-direction)" note documents the ambiguity guard, local shadowing, path-qualified/associated-call non-resolution, and turbofish/space-before-paren call-form gaps as deliberate false-negatives (never false-positives) that the body-only compile-time #386 guardrail **also** misses (it does not hard-block a violation inside a skipped helper), backstopped by runtime replay (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) plus manual review rather than #386; a "Flag scope" note records that `det-check` has its own local `--format` and ignores the global network/`--output` flags; and a DET010/DET011 reconciliation sentence clarifies that `det-check` surfaces the entire shared engine (including the pre-existing DET010 HashMap-iteration and DET011 select rules) — #778 adds no new HashMap/data-structure linting, but does not hide the engine's existing DET010 output. **Post-review tests:** engine — `check_dir_excludes_compile_fail_fixtures`, `check_dir_skips_target_and_hidden_dirs`, `fn_pointer_param_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `local_closure_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `shadowing_does_not_suppress_a_genuinely_reached_helper`, `check_paths_resolves_cross_file_between_two_file_args`, `check_paths_dedups_overlapping_args`, `check_paths_does_not_follow_directory_symlinks` (`#[cfg(unix)]`), `check_paths_skips_non_utf8_file_and_continues`, `check_paths_errors_on_a_missing_top_level_path`, `transitive_helper_det010_is_flagged_via_helper`, `finding_column_is_exact`, `one_bad_helper_reached_by_two_workflows_yields_two_findings`, `suppression_inside_transitive_helper_is_honored` (all in `det_check_tests.rs`). CLI — `det_suppressions_json_is_valid_json_containing_the_suppression`, `run_det_check_list_suppressions_json_exits_ok` (inline), and `two_separate_file_args_resolve_cross_file_transitive`, `overlapping_dir_and_file_args_do_not_double_count` (`det_check_cli.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P1 — module-scoped workflows).** The initial `extract_all_functions` rewrite tracked a **flat** brace-depth counter and skipped every line at depth `> 0`, which conflated a `mod NAME { … }` opener with an `impl`/`fn`/`struct` block — so a `#[workflow]` (or its first-party helper) declared inside a Rust module was **never scanned**, a broad false-negative: `harvest det-check .` could pass despite hard-blocker code in module-scoped workflows. **This was a regression introduced by #778's rewrite** — the superseded `extract_workflow_bodies` on trunk scanned for `#[workflow]` at any brace depth and therefore did scan module-nested workflow bodies (it simply lacked transitive helper resolution). The fix makes extraction **module-aware**: a `Vec<ScopeKind>` scope stack classifies each opening brace as transparent `Module` (`mod NAME { … }`, keep item-scanning inside, at any nesting depth) or `Opaque` (`impl`/`trait`/`struct`/bare block, skip contents), so module-scoped `#[workflow]` entry points and their module-scope helpers are scanned for direct and one-hop transitive violations while **methods inside `impl`/`trait` blocks remain excluded** (the #386 boundary — never indexed as free helpers, a `self.method()`/`Type::method()` callee is never resolved). `#[activity]` bodies remain unscanned at any nesting; a `fn` body's internals are still consumed wholesale by `extract_fn_body` (local fns inside a body are not indexed as top-level helpers). New pure helpers `is_mod_block_decl` (inline `mod NAME { … }` vs. external `mod NAME;`), `strip_leading_visibility`, and `apply_line_braces`/`apply_line_braces_stripped` (the scope-stack walker); the now-unused `code_brace_delta` was removed. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `module_scoped_workflow_direct_violation_is_flagged`, `module_scoped_workflow_transitive_helper_violation_is_flagged` (asserts `via_helper`), `nested_module_workflow_direct_violation_is_flagged`, `module_scoped_det010_hashmap_iteration_is_flagged`, and the two negative guards `module_scoped_activity_violation_is_not_flagged` / `impl_method_callee_is_not_resolved_as_helper` (in `det_check_tests.rs`); `is_mod_block_decl_matches_inline_modules_only`, `strip_leading_visibility_handles_pub_forms`, `apply_line_braces_classifies_module_vs_opaque` (unit tests in `det_check.rs`); and `module_scoped_workflow_direct_violation_trips_the_gate` (CLI behavioral test in `det_check_cli.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P1/P2 — scope-aware same-name resolution + turbofish calls).** Two false-negatives the module-aware rewrite left, both fixed TDD red→green. **(P1) Scope-aware same-name helper resolution.** The prior code marked any identifier defined by more than one plain free helper as globally ambiguous (`None`) and never resolved *any* workflow call to it — even when the calling workflow's own in-scope sibling was the obvious, Rust-correct target (e.g. `mod a { #[workflow] async fn wf() { stamp(); } fn stamp() { chrono::Utc::now() } }` alongside an unrelated `mod b { fn stamp() -> String }` reported no findings, skipping the reachable hard-blocker in `a::stamp`). Resolution is now Rust-accurate nearest-scope: a candidate in the caller's **own module** (same file + `module_path`) wins, else the sole candidate in the caller's **file**, else a **globally unique** candidate, else (multiple candidates, none in the caller's module/file scope) the call is conservatively skipped — the only remaining safe false-negative. This is a strict accuracy improvement with no added false-positive risk (preferring the same-module/same-file definition is exactly what the compiler resolves a bare call to). Shadow-suppression still runs first, so a locally-bound name is never resolved. Implementation: `FnDef` gains a `module_path` (the `mod`-nesting path, tracked in `extract_all_functions` via a `mod_stack` maintained in lockstep with the `Module` scope entries — new `extract_mod_name` + `apply_line_braces_scoped`); the helper index changed from `HashMap<&str, Option<usize>>` to `HashMap<&str, Vec<usize>>`; new pure `resolve_helper(candidates, fns, caller)`. **(P2) Turbofish call form.** A generic first-party helper called with a turbofish (`bad::<u64>()`, `bad::<Vec<u8>>()`) had the byte `:` (not `(`) after the ident, so the call-paren matcher never scanned the helper body and a reachable violation was missed. `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` now skips an optional balanced `::<…>` segment (new `skip_balanced_angles`) before requiring `(`. The `.`/`:` before-guard is unchanged, so method (`x.method::<T>()`) and associated (`Type::assoc::<T>()`) turbofish calls are still never resolved. **Both fixes preserve every existing guarantee** — `#[activity]` bodies unscanned, impl/trait methods never indexed or resolved (#386), closure/fn-pointer shadow-suppression, and zero false positives on the real tree. Tests: `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name`, `same_file_different_module_helper_disambiguates`, `genuinely_ambiguous_same_name_helper_is_skipped`, `same_name_impl_method_is_not_resolved_via_method_call`, `turbofish_helper_call_is_resolved`, `nested_generic_turbofish_helper_call_is_resolved`, `method_and_assoc_turbofish_are_not_resolved` (in `det_check_tests.rs`); `extract_mod_name_reads_the_module_identifier`, `skip_balanced_angles_matches_nested_generics` (unit tests in `det_check.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2 — source-order shadow tracking).** The zero-FP shadow-suppression above used a **whole-body** shadow set: any locally-bound name (params + every `let` binding anywhere in the body) suppressed a call to that name, regardless of where the binding sat relative to the call. That over-suppressed a genuinely in-scope call: a free helper called **before** a later same-name `let` binding is resolved by Rust to the free helper (the binding is not yet in scope), but the whole-body set wrongly skipped it — a false-negative in AC4 transitive coverage (e.g. a free `fn bad()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, reached by a `bad()` call preceding a later `let bad = |x| …`, went unreported). Suppression is now **source-order aware** (`collect_body_let_idents` → `collect_body_let_binding_lines`, name → earliest binding line; `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` takes `params` + `let_binding_lines` and compares each call's source line): a `let` shadow suppresses a call only on a strictly-later source line (so a pre-shadow call — and a call on the binding's own line, `let bad = bad();` — resolves to the free helper, matching Rust); params still bind for the whole body. **No new false positive** — this only ever suppresses *less* than the whole-body set, so every previously-suppressed post-shadow call stays suppressed and the original closure / fn-pointer-param FP-avoidance (`local_closure_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `fn_pointer_param_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`) is preserved. A `let` shadow bound in an inner block already closed before an outer call still suppresses it (source-order, not full brace-scope tracking) — a documented safe-direction residual false-negative, never a false-positive. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix whole-body set): `pre_shadow_call_resolves_to_free_helper_not_the_later_binding` and the residual pin `block_confined_shadow_before_call_is_a_documented_false_negative` (in `det_check_tests.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex r4 — false-positive fix + raw identifiers).** Two more findings, both fixed TDD red→green. **(C) Removed the Rust-inaccurate same-file-different-module resolution (false positive).** `resolve_helper`'s prior order preferred the sole same-**file** helper (any module) before falling back to global uniqueness, but a bare call in a child module does **not** resolve to a same-file helper in a *different* module (a parent/sibling module of the file) unless brought in by a `use` — which this text-level analysis cannot see. So a module-scoped workflow doing `use crate::pure::helper; helper();` (real target: a clean `helper` imported from another file) had its call wrongly resolved to an unrelated file-root `fn helper()` and got that helper's `chrono::Utc::now()` reported as a hard blocker — a false positive that could **fail CI on innocent code**. Resolution is now: a **globally unique** helper resolves directly, else a helper in the caller's **own module** (same file + `module_path`), else — multiple candidates, none in the caller's own module — conservatively skipped (ambiguous). Removing the same-file preference is strictly *more* Rust-accurate and only ever resolves **fewer** calls (removes an FP; cannot add one); shadow-suppression and source-order tracking still run first, and the same-module nearest-scope resolution (the #386 module-nested P1 fix) is untouched. **(D) Raw-identifier function names are now parsed.** `fn_decl_name` accepts an optional `r#` prefix (`async fn r#gen(…)` — `gen` is a reserved keyword in edition 2024, so `r#gen` is a valid, increasingly-real workflow name), retaining the `r#` on the extracted name; previously the parser stopped at `r`, failed the tail sanity check, and the `r#`-named workflow's body was **never scanned** (a direct `chrono::Utc::now()` in it passed with zero findings — a false negative). Transitive `r#name()` *call* resolution is not added (a safe false-negative — the required coverage is that an `r#`-named workflow's own body is scanned). Tests, TDD red→green: `same_file_different_module_helper_is_not_resolved` (converts the now-incorrect `same_file_different_module_helper_disambiguates`, which asserted the buggy FP behavior — the real target is a `use`-imported helper, so the file-root helper's violation is not reachable and must not be flagged), `raw_ident_workflow_body_is_scanned` (in `det_check_tests.rs`), and raw-ident assertions added to the `fn_decl_name_handles_visibility_and_async` unit test (in `det_check.rs`). The FP fix improves accuracy and adds no new false positive; `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name` (the #386 module-nested resolution) and the source-order shadow tests are unchanged and still pass. **Post-review hardening (Codex r5 — restrict one-hop resolution to same-module, ending the cross-module false-positive family structurally).** Codex found a second aliased-import false positive after r4: a `mod inner` workflow doing `use crate::pure_helper as helper; helper();` (real target: a clean, aliased-in helper from another file) still had its bare `helper()` call resolved cross-module — via the surviving **globally-unique (`[only]`) branch** — to an unrelated file-root `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, reported as a hard blocker that would **fail CI on innocent code**. Root cause is fundamental: the line-based front-door **cannot see `use` imports/aliases**, so *any* cross-module resolution keeps producing this false-positive class (r4 was the same-file-different-module case with two candidates; r5 is the single globally-unique candidate; both are the same bug). Rather than chase each variant, resolution is now restricted **structurally to same-module candidates only**: `resolve_helper` resolves a bare call **only** to a helper declared in the caller's own module (same file + `module_path`), and treats **everything else** — cross-module, cross-file, `use`-imported, aliased, and even a *globally-unique* helper that is not same-module — as ambiguous and skips it (a safe false-negative, never a false-positive). The earlier globally-unique (`[only]`) and same-file-different-module fallbacks are **deleted**; this makes an import/alias false positive impossible by construction. For a CI gate a false positive (failing CI on innocent code) is the worst outcome and outranks marginal recall; because #386 is likewise body-only, it does not hard-block a violation inside a skipped cross-module helper either, so the backstop for these transitive false-negatives is runtime replay (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) plus manual review, not #386. Shadow-suppression + source-order tracking (r3) still run before resolution; turbofish call matching (r2), raw-identifier parsing (r4), module-nested `#[workflow]` scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]` / impl-method exclusions (#386) are all orthogonal and unchanged. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix `[only]` branch): `aliased_import_bare_call_is_not_resolved_to_root_helper_same_module_only` (the r5 aliased-import FP — a globally-unique cross-module root helper is no longer resolved); the two prior cross-file resolution tests are **converted to boundary tests** pinning the same-module-only limit rather than deleted — `transitive_cross_file_via_check_dir_is_flagged` → `transitive_cross_file_via_check_dir_is_not_resolved_same_module_only` (asserts a cross-file `check_dir` helper is NOT resolved) and `check_paths_resolves_cross_file_between_two_file_args` → `check_paths_cross_file_helper_is_not_resolved_same_module_only` (asserts a cross-file helper across two separate file args is NOT resolved; the `check_paths` shared-index dedup / symlink-skip / non-UTF-8 robustness tests are untouched — only the resolution they enabled changed). `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name` (the core same-module resolution) still flags `a::stamp`; `same_file_different_module_helper_is_not_resolved` (r4) still yields no finding, now via same-module-only; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 7 direct + 7 transitive (each transitive helper is same-module as its workflow — no fixture move needed) for exactly 14 findings, zero fixture FP; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. Same-module-only resolves strictly *fewer* calls than before, so it can only remove false positives — it cannot add a finding. **Post-review hardening (Codex r6 — block-local `use` imports shadow same-module helpers + raw-identifier calls).** Two more Codex P2 findings, both fixed TDD red→green. **(E) Block-local `use` imports now shadow same-module helpers (false-positive fix).** Even under r5's same-module-only resolution, a `use` **inside a workflow body** rebinds a name to an import, so Rust resolves a bare call to that import — not a same-module sibling `fn` of the same name. A module-scoped workflow doing `use crate::pure::helper; helper();` in its body (real target: a clean imported `helper`) still had `helper()` resolved to a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()` and reported as a hard blocker — a false positive that would **fail CI on innocent code**. The workflow-body shadow set (the r3 source-order set of params + `let`/closure bindings) is now extended to also include names bound by a **block-local `use`** in the body: `use path::name;` binds `name`, `use path::orig as alias;` binds `alias`, grouped `use path::{a, b as c};` binds `a` and `c`, and an unnameable glob `use path::*;`. New pure helpers `collect_body_use_bindings`, `parse_use_bindings`, `parse_use_single`, and `extract_use_ident` (all retain an `r#` raw-identifier prefix; `use<'a>` RPIT precise-capture clauses are ignored via a whitespace-after-`use` guard); `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` gains the `use` shadow params. **Only body-local `use` statements are in the shadow set** — a module/file-level `use` is not a body line (`extract_fn_body` captures body lines only), so the common top-of-file prelude-glob case is unaffected by construction, and a module-level `use` + a same-name `fn` is itself a compile error, making a block-local `use` the last same-module rebind vector. Adding `use` imports to the shadow set only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces **no new false positive**. **(F) Raw-identifier calls (`r#gen()`) are now tokenized correctly (false-negative fix).** r4 indexed a `fn r#gen` def under the key `r#gen`, but the call tokenizer in `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` split `#`, tokenizing `r#gen()` as `r`/`gen`, so the call never matched the def and a reachable hard blocker in a raw-identifier same-module helper was silently missed. The call tokenizer now consumes an optional leading `r#` as part of the call identifier (so `r#gen(` yields the token `r#gen`), completing raw-identifier support on **both** the def and call sides; the `.`/`:` before-guard (still excluding `x.r#method()` / `Type::r#assoc()`) and the turbofish skip (`r#gen::<T>()`) both compose with it unchanged. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `block_local_use_import_shadows_same_module_helper` (Codex's exact repro), `block_local_use_alias_shadows_same_module_helper`, `block_local_use_group_shadows_same_module_helper`, `block_local_glob_use_conservatively_suppresses_later_same_module_calls`, `same_module_call_without_block_local_use_is_still_resolved` (regression guard: a genuine same-module call with no shadow is still flagged — r5 preserved), `module_level_use_is_not_treated_as_a_body_shadow` (a file-level `use ...::*;`/`use path;` does not suppress a same-module call), `raw_ident_helper_call_is_resolved_and_flagged` (a `r#gen()` helper call is resolved and flagged transitively), and `raw_ident_method_call_is_not_resolved` (a `x.r#gen()` method call is still not resolved) — in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved: same-module-only resolution (r5), source-order shadow tracking (r3), turbofish calls (r2), raw-ident def parsing (r4), module-nested scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]`/impl-method exclusions (#386); the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations, and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. **Post-review hardening (Codex r7 — block `use` imports shadow the whole body, not source-order).** r6 added body-local `use` bindings to the shadow set but applied them **source-order** (a `use` only shadowed calls on strictly-later lines, like a `let`). That is wrong for `use`: unlike a sequential `let`, a Rust block `use` item is in scope for the **entire enclosing block** regardless of textual position, so a bare call may **precede** the `use` and still resolve to the import. A body doing `helper(); use crate::pure::helper;` therefore still false-positived — the call preceded the `use`, so r6's source-order check did not suppress it, and same-module resolution scanned the sibling `fn helper`'s `chrono::Utc::now()` and reported a hard blocker on code that never reaches that helper. Fix: body-local `use` bindings (and a body-local glob) now shadow the called name across the **whole body**, matching Rust's block-wide `use`-item scope — `collect_body_use_bindings` returns `(HashSet<String>, bool)` (a presence set + "any glob in the body") instead of source-line maps, and `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` suppresses a call whenever its name is in that set or any glob is present, on every line. **`let`/closure/param shadows stay source-order (r3) — only the `use`/glob half becomes whole-body.** This only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces **no new false positive** (a genuine same-module call with no body `use` for that name — and no glob — is still resolved and flagged; a module/file-level `use` is still never a body shadow). Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the r6 source-order check): `block_use_shadows_a_call_before_the_use_statement` (Codex's exact call-before-`use` repro → no DET001) and `block_glob_use_shadows_a_call_before_the_glob` (a glob preceding-call variant) in `det_check_tests.rs`; the r6 use/alias/grouped tests, the `same_module_call_without_block_local_use_is_still_resolved` regression guard, and `module_level_use_is_not_treated_as_a_body_shadow` all stay green, and the 14-workflow success-metric fixture and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan are unchanged. **Post-review hardening (Codex r9 — two false-positive fixes: top-level symlink PATH args + column-aware same-line `let` shadow).** Two more Codex P2 findings, both false positives that could fail CI on innocent code (the worst outcome for a gate), fixed TDD red→green. **(G) Top-level symlink PATH arguments are no longer followed.** The nested directory walker already skips symlinks, but a symlink passed **directly** as a top-level `det-check` PATH argument was classified with `std::fs::metadata` (which **follows**) before the walker ran, so `det-check link.rs` (a symlink to a file) linted the target and `det-check link-to-dir` walked the target — pulling **out-of-tree contents** into the report, contradicting the documented no-follow contract. `check_paths` now classifies each top-level argument with `std::fs::symlink_metadata` (which does **not** follow) first: a symlinked argument is **skipped with a warning** (`det-check: skipping symlink <path>`), mirroring the nested walker's no-follow and the existing non-UTF-8 skip-with-warning; only after confirming the argument is not a symlink is it classified as a file (scan) or directory (walk) as before. A missing top-level path still surfaces as an error (`symlink_metadata` errors on a nonexistent path). **(H) `let`/closure shadow suppression is now column-aware within a line.** The r3 source-order shadow suppression was **line-granular** — a `let` binding only suppressed a shadowed call on a strictly-later **line** — so a same-line `let helper = || 0; helper();` was **not** suppressed, and a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()` had the same-line `helper()` call wrongly resolved to that unreachable helper (a hard-blocker false positive). Rust resolves the second call to the local `let`. The suppression is now **column-aware for the same-line case**: `collect_body_let_binding_lines` records each binding's scope-entry point as a `LetBinding { line, in_scope_col }`, where `in_scope_col` is the byte column of the statement-terminating `;` (via the new depth-tracking `let_stmt_terminator_col`, so a `;` inside a closure block or nested expression is skipped; `usize::MAX` for a multi-line `let`); `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` suppresses a same-line call only when its column is **past** that `;`. This is deliberately **not** a conservative "suppress all same-line calls" approach — that would wrongly suppress a genuine pre-shadow `bad(); let bad = ...;` call — nor a "suppress when past the bound ident" approach, which would wrongly suppress the RHS of a self-referencing `let bad = bad();`. Column-awareness against the statement-terminating `;` keeps `let helper = ...; helper();` suppressed while the RHS of `let bad = bad();` (before the `;`) and a pre-shadow `bad(); let bad = ...;` call (before the binding) both **stay flagged** — avoiding a new false negative. Cross-line behavior (strictly-later line suppressed, earlier line flagged) is unchanged. Both fixes only ever **skip more** (a narrower followed set / more shadow suppression), so neither introduces a new false positive. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `check_paths_does_not_follow_a_top_level_symlink_file` and `check_paths_does_not_follow_a_top_level_symlink_dir` (`#[cfg(unix)]`, both RED before the fix), `check_paths_still_scans_real_file_and_dir_args` (regression: real file/dir args still scan), `same_line_let_binding_before_call_is_suppressed` (the FP, RED before), `same_line_call_before_let_binding_is_still_flagged` and `same_line_self_referencing_let_rhs_call_is_still_flagged` (regressions: pre-shadow / self-ref RHS calls stay flagged) in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved: same-module-only resolution (r5), whole-body `use` shadow (r6/r7), source-order `let`/closure shadow (r3), turbofish (r2), raw-ident def+call parsing (r4/r6), module-nested scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]`/impl-method exclusions (#386); the `check_paths` dedup / non-UTF-8 / nested-symlink-skip robustness is untouched; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. **Post-review hardening (Codex r10 — nested `fn` declaration false positive + documented block-scoping boundary).** Closes the Codex review loop with one false-positive fix and one documented safe-direction false-negative. **Fixed the nested-`fn`-declaration false positive.** A workflow body containing a nested item `fn helper() {}` had its **declaration** token `helper(` treated as a **call** by `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` (which only checked for a following `(`), resolved to a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, and reported as a hard blocker on an *uncalled* helper — an FP that could fail innocent CI. Two FP-preventing parts, both TDD red→green: (a) the call collector now **skips a `NAME(` token that is a declaration** — the ident is preceded (ignoring whitespace) by the `fn` keyword (new word-bounded `is_ident_preceded_by_fn` helper); the existing `.`/`:` before-guard is retained; and (b) block-local `fn NAME(...)` item names declared in the workflow body are collected into the **whole-body shadow set** (new `collect_body_fn_bindings`, reusing the raw-`r#`-aware `extract_use_ident`), exactly like block-local `use` items (r7), so a *genuine* call to a body-local nested `fn NAME` resolves to that nested fn (which shadows the module item) instead of the same-module `fn NAME`. Adding `fn` names to the shadow set only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces no new false positive; a `fn(..)` pointer TYPE has no following ident and binds nothing. **Documented the nested-block `use`/`fn` whole-body over-suppression as a safe-direction false-negative (a line-based-granularity boundary), declined in favor of the zero-FP whole-body treatment.** A block-local `use`/`fn` inside a **nested block** is scoped by Rust only to that inner block, but the whole-body shadow (r7/r10) suppresses a same-named call in a sibling or outer block *after* it too — a false **negative** (under-reports, never over-reports). Precise block-scoping would add brace-range-per-item machinery and risk reopening the ordering false-*positive* the whole-body treatment was chosen to eliminate, for a contrived shape; the code fix is **declined** and the boundary is instead documented in `docs/workflow-determinism-guide.md` "Known limitations" as an explicit line-based-granularity boundary, with the runtime replay net (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) + manual review as the backstop. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-r10 collector): `fn_declaration_in_body_is_not_collected_as_a_call` (a nested `fn helper() {}` decl + a same-module violating `fn helper` → no finding), `body_local_fn_shadows_the_module_helper_on_a_real_call` (a body-local `fn helper() {}` + a genuine `helper()` call → resolves to the nested fn, not the module helper → no finding), and `same_module_call_without_body_local_fn_is_still_flagged` (regression: a genuine same-module `helper()` call with no body-local `fn`/`use` is still flagged) in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean.
- Published interaction schema + `/interface` discovery + boundary validation (issue #610). Extend the #373 workflow input/output schema story to a workflow's **interaction surface** — its signals, queries, and updates. Each handler can publish an argument/response JSON Schema and a description: `QueryHandlerInfo`/`UpdateHandlerInfo` gain `description`/`arg_schema`/`response_schema` fields; a new `SignalHandlerInfo` type (arg-only, no response). Fluent builders `with_description`/`with_arg_schema_fn`/`with_response_schema_fn` and, under the `schema` feature, `with_schemas::<Arg, Resp>()` (`<Arg>` for signals). The `#[query]`/`#[update]`/`#[signal]` macros parse `description = "…"` and emit a public `{fn}_info()` alias; `signals![…]` collector added. New read-only management route **`GET /workflows/registered/{name}/interface`** returns a `WorkflowInterfaceRecord { signals, queries, updates }`, each entry `{ name, description?, arg_schema?, response_schema? }`, sorted by name and deterministic across calls. `404` for an unregistered workflow name. Signals never carry a `response_schema`. **Boundary validation:** when a signal or update handler has a published `arg_schema`, the payload is validated *before* durable enqueue at the three HTTP entry points — the signal-send route, `POST /workflows/{name}/signal-with-start`, and the update route. On failure returns `400` `{ "error": "…validation failed", "violations": [{ "message", "field_path" }] }` (RFC 6901 pointer), reusing #373's `validate_against_schema`. A handler with no published schema is not validated (unchanged behavior). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no adjacently-tagged JSON change, no replay impact** — validation runs at the HTTP boundary before enqueue, and discovery is a read-only projection of the registry. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/interface_schema_workflow.rs` (`--features schema`). **Source-visible change:** each `#[query]`/`#[update]`/`#[signal]`-annotated function now also emits a public `{fn}_info()` symbol (consistent with the existing `#[workflow]`/`#[activity]` convention). A downstream crate that already defines a hand-written `foo_info()` beside `#[query] fn foo` would need to rename one of them.
- **Trunk hardening** — heal the batch-route gate-bypass test (Refs #1085, #1053, #1073). **Test-code-only. No production change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** The Docker-only plugin test in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/start_throttle_integration.rs` that #1073 added for issue #1053 had a wrong runtime expectation. The plugin suite spins a testcontainers Postgres, so CI runs it Docker-backed but #1073 could only compile-check it — the assertion never actually executed. It is the deterministic ubuntu **Test**-leg red blocking every open PR (surfaced in #1085). Same class as the recent trunk heals #1076/#1077/#1078. **Root cause — a wrong test EXPECTATION, not a code bug.** The test seeded a `COMPLETED` prior for an explicit `workflow_id`, armed a fleet admission gate, submitted a non-atomic batch item under the batch route's hardcoded `AllowDuplicate` policy, and asserted `status != "rejected"`. But the batch route reports an *attach-to-existing* (`start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect` returning `created == false`) with `status: "rejected"` + the duplicate message `"workflow_id '…' already has an existing execution"` + the prior's `execution_id`. That mapping is a long-standing convention meaning "no NEW row was inserted" — authored 2026-07-09 (PR #991), six days *before* #1073 (2026-07-15); #1073's only `api.rs` change is the single Phase-1 gate-bypass hunk `@@ -12677,25 +12677,45 @@`. It is **not** an admission-gate block: a gate rejection produces `error = "admission blocked by gate …"` with `execution_id: null` in Phase 1 and never reaches the attach path. The active uniqueness partial index `(workflow_name, workflow_id) WHERE state NOT IN ('CONTINUED_AS_NEW','TERMINATED')` does not release `COMPLETED`, so `_collect`'s `on_conflict_do_nothing` insert is a no-op and it returns the existing run (matrix-consistent — no rejection thrown by `_collect`), and `start_will_create_new_execution(Some("COMPLETED"), AllowDuplicate) == false`, so the item correctly **bypasses** the gate and attaches. The old assertion conflated the benign duplicate-attach `"rejected"` with a gate block, and the `#1073` code is correct. (This refutes an early hypothesis of a code bug in the batch existence check.) **The test's name over-promised.** It was named `..._uses_start_will_create_predicate_not_bare_existence`, but verified against the #1073 diff, the OLD `has_execution` boolean it replaced used the *same* non-sealed-prior filter (`state NOT IN ('CONTINUED_AS_NEW','TERMINATED')`) the new predicate query uses, and the batch route hardcodes `AllowDuplicate` (`BatchStartItem` has no reuse-policy field). So the predicate and the old bare-existence heuristic are **behaviorally identical for every prior state** through this route (both attach for any present non-sealed prior, both create for `None`/sealed, including `TERMINATED`). The predicate-vs-bare-existence *implementation* distinction is therefore **not black-box observable** through the batch route today — #1073 calls it exactly this: a structural/defensive change that becomes observable only if a per-item reuse policy is ever added. The genuine predicate distinction is unit-tested directly in `autumn_harvest::execution::start_will_create_tests`. **Fix — heal the red AND make the test genuinely meaningful.** Renamed to `batch_gate_bypasses_an_attaching_item_but_blocks_a_would_be_fresh_create` and rewritten to guard the property it actually *can* prove: the end-to-end bypass DECISION OUTCOME, via a case that splits by will-create. Under one armed fleet gate, in one non-atomic batch: a `COMPLETED` prior → the item **bypasses** the gate and **attaches** (error is the duplicate message, not a gate block; an `execution_id` is present); a `TERMINATED` prior (sealed → excluded from the uniqueness index → `_collect` would CREATE fresh) → the item does **not** bypass; it **faces the gate and is blocked** (`error = "admission blocked by gate …"`, `execution_id: null`). The `TERMINATED`-prior gate block is the load-bearing assertion: it proves the gate is enforced exactly for an item that would create a NEW admission — the substance of #1053/#1073. (It does not, and cannot, distinguish the predicate from bare-existence; both block a sealed prior. The doc comment states this precisely.) The rewritten test (and the full `start_throttle_integration` suite) was **run green** against a local Postgres 16 via a temporary, uncommitted `setup_database` adaptation (Docker is unavailable in this sandbox), which was then reverted so only the test rewrite + this fragment remain.
- **Tooling** — Heal two RED `trunk-dev` failures after a merge burst (PR #1094). A merge burst left `trunk-dev` red on two independent gates; this PR heals both (precedent: PR #1078 folded two lint heals into one PR). **1. Missing route classification (`contract_regression`).** PR #1092 added the read-only route `GET /workflows/registered/{name}/interface` to the plugin's `management_api_routes()` but never classified it in `autumn_harvest::audit`, so the plugin's `contract_regression::every_management_route_is_classified` test — which enforces that every `management_api_routes()` entry has a `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` entry (issue #776 AC4 read-only enforcement source of truth) — failed on every trunk-based branch. Classified the route `ReadOnly`, exactly mirroring its existing sibling `GET /workflows/registered/{name}/schema`, across all four audit lists in `autumn-harvest/src/audit.rs`: `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (`RouteClass::ReadOnly`), `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` (read, no audit trail), `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` (op `None`), and the `newly_classified_reads_are_read_only` pin test. `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES.len()` and `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES.len()` stay balanced (one entry added to each), so `classified_routes_count_matches_route_manifest` still holds. **2. `clippy::redundant_closure_for_method_calls` (`-D warnings`).** PR #1093 merged while draft (CI skipped), introducing a redundant-closure lint failure in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/start_throttle_integration.rs` — `body["results"].as_array().map_or(0, |a| a.len())`. Replaced the closure with the method itself (`Vec::len`), which is behavior-identical and accepted by both clippy 1.94.1 (stable) and 1.97.0. The sibling `.map_or(0, |e| e[...].as_i64().unwrap_or(0))` on line 1896 is a non-trivial closure and is correctly not flagged. No production code or runtime behavior change beyond making the already-shipped `/interface` route reachable by a read-only principal and excluded from audit (consistent with the `/schema` sibling). No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.
- **Trunk heal** — add `StartSource` fields to `ui_integration` test literals (semantic merge conflict #1095 × #1085). **Test-code-only — no production code changed.** Trunk-dev went RED on the Lint leg (`cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets -- -D warnings`), which blocks every branch off trunk repo-wide, with a hard compile error: ``` error[E0063]: missing fields `start_source`, `start_source_ref` and `started_by` in initializer of `StartWorkflowParams<'_>` --> autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/ui_integration.rs:3670:9 ``` Root cause: a **semantic merge conflict** between two independently-green PRs. PR #1095 (issue #740, StartSource provenance, merged as `3fa812d2`) added three **required** fields to `StartWorkflowParams` in `autumn-harvest/src/execution.rs` — `start_source: StartSource`, `start_source_ref: Option<&'a str>`, `started_by: Option<&'a str>` — and updated every construction site that existed at the time (its CI was green). PR #1085 (Vantage DAG run-graph + timeline pages, merged *after* #1095 became ready) added a **new** `StartWorkflowParams { .. }` literal in the `dag957_seed_run` helper of `ui_integration.rs` that predates the field additions. Git merged the two cleanly (no textual conflict), but the combination does not compile: the new literal is missing the three now-required fields. Fix: add the three fields to the one un-updated literal, mirroring #1095's own neutral test convention verbatim (`StartSource::Api` / `None` / `None`, inserted right after `completion_callbacks: None,` — identical to the four sibling literals #1095 updated in this same file at the `insert_workflow_on_url` / `insert_child_workflow_on_url` / `workflow_detail_ui_*` helpers). A brace-tracking scan of every `StartWorkflowParams { .. }` literal across the whole workspace confirmed this was the **only** straggler — all core-crate and other plugin literals were already updated by #1095. Because `start_source` is metadata only (never read during replay), this is not a behavioral change: **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact.** Validation (Docker-backed Postgres 16): the 8 DAG run-graph/retry `ui_integration` tests that seed via the fixed `dag957_seed_run` helper (`ui_dag_run_graph_*`, `ui_dag_retry_*`) all pass end-to-end — exercised, not merely compile-checked (10/10 in the `ui_dag_` filter). Gates green: `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets -- -D warnings` at both stable and 1.97.0 (plus the `mcp,unified-dag-execution` / `webhooks` / `metrics` feature combos), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and MSRV `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace`.
- **CI** — gate `webhook_receiver_integration` and fix its `TestApp::plugin` deadlock (test-infra). **Tooling/testing** (implemented): the Docker-gated plugin suite `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/webhook_receiver_integration.rs` (issue #344) was absent from `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`, so CI only *compile-checked* it — it had **zero runtime regression coverage** and was listed in the `ci_run_coverage.rs` `ALLOWLIST` as a `webhooks`-feature-gated, all-`#[ignore]`d suite that "no CI run can execute". This slice reproduces and fixes a genuine test-harness **deadlock** in 5 of its 6 tests, un-`#[ignore]`s the suite, and wires it into the manifest so it runs for real against Docker Postgres. **Test-harness change only — no production webhook code touched, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change.** **Root cause — current-thread runtime + `TestApp::plugin`.** `TestApp::plugin(HarvestPlugin)` runs the plugin startup hook on a spawned thread via `Handle::block_on` while the test thread blocks on its join; under a plain `#[tokio::test]` (single current-thread runtime) that mutual block **deadlocks**. PR #1095 (issue #740) discovered this when it added `webhook_start_records_webhook_source` and fixed *that one* test with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]` — but the 5 pre-existing tests, never actually run in CI (`#[ignore]` + no manifest row), kept the plain-`#[tokio::test]` shape and the latent deadlock. **Red→green.** Reproduced against a live Postgres 16 (testcontainers, `--include-ignored`, 90 s per-test timeout): the 5 pre-existing tests (`duplicate_webhook_delivery_creates_exactly_one_execution_with_same_exec_id`, `duplicate_webhook_delivery_to_signals_target_delivers_signal_exactly_once`, `blank_delivery_id_is_rejected_as_missing_for_signals_target`, `upstream_idempotency_key_header_does_not_trip_throttle_mutual_exclusion_on_starts`, `distinct_deliveries_sharing_an_upstream_idempotency_key_are_not_collapsed`) all **hung/deadlocked** (killed at the timeout); `webhook_start_records_webhook_source` (already multi-thread) passed in 1.88 s. After applying the same multi-thread flavor to the 5, two consecutive serial full-suite runs were fully green: `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored` (4.55 s, then 2.56 s). **Fix pattern (mirrors #1095 exactly).** Each of the 5 pre-existing tests changed from `#[tokio::test]` to `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]`, with a one-line rationale comment pointing at the fuller note on `webhook_start_records_webhook_source`. **Gating (the actual runtime-coverage enabler).** The manifest `linux` runner never passes `--include-ignored`, and `ci_run_coverage.rs::all_tests_ignored` disqualifies an all-`#[ignore]`d suite from being credited — so the `#[ignore = "requires Docker (testcontainers)"]` attribute was removed from **all 6** tests (matching every other `linux` plugin suite, e.g. `fail_now`/`timeline`, which are un-ignored and run against Docker Postgres). The file's `#![cfg(feature = "webhooks")]` gate means a plain `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-plugin` (no `webhooks` feature) still compiles it away entirely, so no default-feature developer flow is affected. Added one sorted manifest line — `linux autumn-harvest-plugin webhook_receiver_integration webhooks -` — and updated the coverage guard: dropped `webhook_receiver_integration` from the `paved_path_db_tests_are_classified_and_flagged_all_ignored` all-ignored self-test, and removed its `ALLOWLIST` entry (it is now covered by a real `linux` run). `webhook_durable_integration` and `mcp_tools_integration` stay all-ignored/allowlisted (out of scope). **Verification.** Full local CI mirror green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (1.97.0), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings` (covers `ci_run_coverage.rs`), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets --features webhooks -- -D warnings` (covers the webhook suite), MSRV `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace`, and the 13-test `ci_run_coverage` guard (all green, including `manifest_is_sorted_and_unique` and `every_db_gated_test_has_a_ci_run_step_or_is_allowlisted`).
- **Explicit shard pinning for data-residency workflow placement** (implemented) — see issue #697. Before, the only way a new workflow landed on a shard was rendezvous hashing over `(workflow_name, workflow_id)`; `docs/sharding.md` documented an ID-prefix workaround and admitted it was unreliable, so an embedder with a data-residency obligation had no supported mechanism. Now the start path accepts an **optional explicit placement**, and residency is transitive across the whole workflow tree. **Core (`shard.rs`)**: new `ShardPlacement` enum (`Auto` (default) / `Shard(ShardId)` / `ResidencyKey(String)`), typed `ShardPlacementError` (`UnknownShard` / `ShardNotWritable` / `UnknownResidencyKey` / `EmptyResidencyKey`, each naming the valid set), a `residency_map: BTreeMap<String, ShardId>` field on `ShardRouter` with the fluent `ShardRouter::with_residency_map(...)`, and `ShardRouter::resolve_placement(&placement, workflow_name, workflow_id) -> Result<ShardId, ShardPlacementError>`. `ShardPlacement`/`ShardPlacementError` are re-exported from `lib.rs`; `ShardPlacementError` converts into `HarvestError::Config` (→ HTTP 400). `WorkflowHandleClient::resolve_shard_placement` is the client-side sibling of `pick_shard_for_new_workflow`. **AC1 — `Auto` is byte-for-byte today's routing**: `resolve_placement(Auto, ..)` delegates verbatim to `pick_for_new_workflow`, pinned by a unit test that compares both across 200 ids. **AC3 — residency keys resolve through an operator-DECLARED map, never a hash** (the load-bearing design decision): rendezvous hashing deliberately re-balances (~1/N keys move when a shard is added) and cannot know which physical database is in which jurisdiction, so a hash can satisfy neither half of AC3. The declared map gives the guarantee residency needs — *the same key resolves to the same shard across process restarts AND across a widening of `writable_shards`*, changing only when an operator edits the map. Pinned by `residency_key_resolution_is_stable_across_a_widening_of_the_shard_set`, which also asserts the *hash* DOES move those keys, so the test proves the map buys something. An **unmapped** key is a typed error, never a silent hash fallback (a silent hash is exactly the failure mode that produces a compliance breach). Map misconfiguration (blank key, or a target outside `readable_shards`) **panics at `ShardRouter` construction**, consistent with `ShardRouter::new`'s documented panic contract, so it fails at boot rather than at the first request. **AC2 — a pin outside `readable_shards` is rejected**, never defaulted; the `UNENCODED` (`0xFFFF`) sentinel and a negative `shard_id` are likewise rejected. **Deliberately stricter than AC2's literal wording**: a pin to a shard that is readable but NOT in `writable_shards` (a draining shard) is also rejected (`ShardNotWritable`), because (i) placing new work on a shard the operator is draining contradicts the drain, and (ii) the #808 mint loop can never converge to a non-writable shard and would spin to `MINT_CAP` and warn. **AC6 — HTTP surface**: `POST /workflows/{name}/start` gains two optional, mutually-exclusive `#[serde(default)]` body fields, `shard_id: Option<i32>` and `residency_key: Option<String>`, parsed by the pure `parse_shard_placement` (both-supplied / negative / sentinel / blank-key all rejected). Every rejection is a `400` JSON error with a **failed audit row** (new `audit_start_failure` helper) — never a `500`, never a silent re-hash, never a quiet fall back to the default shard. An explicit placement **overrides** both hash routes (the plain rendezvous pick and the #808 idempotency-key pick). **AC5 — observability with no new column**: `StartWorkflowResponse` gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] shard_id: Option<i32>`, populated **only when a placement was requested**, so an unpinned start's response stays byte-for-byte the pre-#697 shape; the chosen shard is also readable from the encoded `ExecutionId` (`exec_id.shard()`) and the execution row's existing `shard_id` column. **AC4 — residency is transitive** across the workflow tree. Two genuine bugs were found and fixed here (RED→GREEN): the **awaited** child path (`context.rs`) and the **`ctx.race()` child branch** both minted `ExecutionId::new()` — the `UNENCODED` sentinel — so a child's row landed on the parent's shard (the worker sets the row's `shard_id` from the parent) while its **encoded id** routed every later id-based lookup to the deployment's *default* shard. Both now mint `ExecutionId::new_for_shard(self.exec_id.shard())`, matching the detached path and the child-timeout race, which were already correct. `continue_as_new` (`worker.rs`), workflow-level retry (#523), and reset forks (#148) were audited and already inherit. **#808 interaction**: the bounded rejection-sampling mint loop that re-mints an auto-generated `workflow_id` so it hashes to the target shard now also runs for a **pinned** start, closing the `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` per-shard uniqueness hole for auto-generated ids (a pin moves a run off its hash-derived shard, so a later *unpinned* start of the same id would route elsewhere and could duplicate). For a caller-supplied **explicit** `workflow_id` this cannot be closed mechanically — be consistent (always pin it or never pin it), the same documented consistency requirement idempotency-key routing already carries. Placement is resolved **before** the #808 committed-replay probe (the probe needs the shard), so a retry of a keyed start must carry the same placement as the original delivery. **Registries + CLI**: `shard_id`/`residency_key` added to `management_api_request_fields()`, `shard_id` to `management_api_response_fields()`, and both plus the extended 400/success notes to `docs/api-contract.json` (the `contract_regression` cross-check stays green). CLI: `harvest workflow start --shard-id <N>` / `--residency-key <KEY>` (clap `conflicts_with`, so the mutual exclusion is caught at parse time), emitting the fields only when supplied. **AC7 — `docs/sharding.md`** replaces the unreliable ID-prefix workaround with a full "Explicit shard placement and data residency" section (the two placement forms, the resolution rule + stability guarantee and *why* it is a declared map, the rejection table, the three observation surfaces, the transitivity table, a worked two-region EU/US example, and the uniqueness / retry-consistency caveats); the three "see the concurrency routing guidance above" back-references now point at it. **AC8 — no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to the adjacently-tagged JSON contract, no replay-determinism impact**: placement is a pre-start routing decision, and the shard was already encoded in the `ExecutionId`. **Two unanswered design questions were resolved by documented assumption** (the user was asked and did not answer): (a) residency-key resolution is a declared map rather than a hash, for the AC3 reasons above; (b) a pin to a drained (readable-but-not-writable) shard is rejected rather than accepted. **Success metric**: `residency_conformance_n_workflows_across_k_keys` exists at both levels — a pure router test (2 keys × 100 runs) and a DB/HTTP test (2 keys × 12 runs against two genuinely separate shard databases) — each asserting **100%** of starts land on the intended shard, with no sampling and no tolerance. **Tests**: 15 pure unit tests in `shard.rs` (Auto-equals-rendezvous, unknown/drained/sentinel rejection, unmapped-key rejection, the AC3 stability money test, conformance, two `#[should_panic]` construction tests);
